threads.title: HEARD: recruiting office in Nurzhan / an 'Iradi battalion'

posts.body: rumour in dastgoh: an office above a phone shop near the bus station signing guys for "work in russia", good money, no questions. everybody says it's recruitment. anyone seen it?

Heard the same. Also heard "Bekzatov is raising an Iradi battalion for Moscow". That one I don't believe. Bekzatov loves Moscow, but he loves NurGaz more, and you can't drill wells with boys who are in a trench.

Mod hat on. Careful with that one: it's a serious claim about a named man and there's nothing behind it but a bus station. The rumour board allows rumours. It doesn't allow inventing battalions.

Also, I walked past the phone shop. It's a phone shop.
HEARD: Russia will call up every Russo in Nurzhan with a Russian passport, through the consulate.

There is no Russian consulate in the ISEZ, because Russia doesn't recognise the ISEZ. Nobody is going door to door in Dastgoh. The real risk is to men who are physically in Russia. Practical advice is in the Diaspora thread. Logged.

From Moscow oblast: the recruiters are real, but they are here, not there. Hostels, building sites, the bus to the site in the morning. Nobody needs an office in Nurzhan when the boys are already standing in Russia with a shovel.
Our government has reminded Kyrgyz citizens that fighting for a foreign army is a crime at home. Since half of Nurzhan carries our passport, maybe this is the useful rumour of the week.
The Department of Public Information advises ISEZ residents working in Russia not to sign any military contract. This forum should spread official advice, not rumours. Have a nice day.
I agreed with him twice in one morning. I need to lie down.
update: phone shop is a phone shop. upstairs is a dentist. i got my tooth checked while i was there. no battalion. vyshka sends regards
Herald today on the families waiting at the bus station. Every word of it true, I've seen all of it with my own eyes. At least somebody wrote it down.

From Surgut. The recruiters came out to the camp on the shift bus with leaflets. The guys with Kyrgyz passports laughed. Two guys with Russian passports didn't laugh. They took leave and went to Nurzhan. That's the real news, not battalions: who quietly isn't here anymore.

threads.title: [FreeIrad] "The Governor died this year": discuss

posts.body:
WE ARE PUBLISHING NOTHING YET. WE ARE TELLING YOU WHAT WE ARE HEARING, BECAUSE THIS IS THE RUMOUR BOARD.

TWO SOURCES, NOT CONNECTED TO EACH OTHER, SAY THE GOVERNOR DIED THIS YEAR AND THAT WHAT YOU SEE NOW IS A DOUBLE, ALWAYS AT A DISTANCE.

WE CANNOT PROVE IT. WE BELIEVE IT. DISCUSS. SAY WHAT YOU KNOW AND WHAT YOU ONLY THINK, AND LABEL WHICH IS WHICH.
Respectfully, admins: I don't buy it. "Died this year", and the man is still waving at things on OneNews. That's thin ice, and you're the ones standing on it.
Honest question: when did anybody here last see him in person, not on a screen? I'll start. Irad Day 2019, from very far away. He waved, I waved, my boss waved.
On TV he's always seated now. Always short. That's a man of 68. My grandfather at 68 was always seated too. He was also alive.
HEARD: he died in the spring and they buried him at Boz-Korgon at night.

Not scoring this one. If it's true nobody will ever be allowed to check it, and if it's false nobody will ever admit they said it. Some rumours are built so they can never be scored. That's what bothers me about this one.
On OneDebate last month Ilyasov said "show me the Governor's diary for one ordinary week". Presenter went to ads. Just saying.

In the 1930s the state's papers kept plenty of our priests "transferred" long after they were dead. So I know a state can keep a man alive on paper, and I won't laugh at the idea.

But I won't believe it just because I'd like to, either. Belief is for Sundays. Rumours need evidence.

The Kurultai's consent in August went to Talas in writing and the answer came back in writing. That is normal. Nobody up here expects to see the Governor; we have not seen him since 2007 and we do not need to.

So I cannot tell you if he is alive. I can tell you that up here, it changes nothing. Maybe that is an answer too.

I respect the admins and I'm grateful for this board, which has been my window home for eleven years. But I think we should hold ourselves to a higher standard than the people we criticise. If this claim turns out wrong, it is a gift to IradOne: "look at the liars at FreeIrad".

Please be careful. (No form attached. This is too serious for a form.)
NOTED. WE SAID WE CANNOT PROVE IT. WE STAND BY "WE BELIEVE IT". THIS FORUM IS YOURS TO DISAGREE WITH US IN. THAT IS WHAT IT IS FOR.
Fair answer. I still don't buy it.
ok but if there's a double, who is it. which actor. kino_talasfilm this is your moment
A dead horse does not eat. Watch the oats, not the horse. Who signs, who spends, who gives orders. That will tell you more than any video.
The only Talasfilm actor who could ever have played him was Almaz Sarybaev, and Sarybaev died in 2019, God rest him. So: no. Talasfilm is not involved. I checked.
The Governor is in good health and continues his work. This thread is disrespectful. Have a nice day.
Has the Governor's good health ever posted on a forum at eleven in the morning? Asking for a friend.
At my aunt's stall people talk about him like the weather now. Not loved, not hated, just there. If he's gone, the weather didn't change. Maybe that's the scariest version of this.
HEARD: he'll do the New Year address live this year, just to make us all look stupid.

It was recorded. Of course it was recorded; every New Year address since 2007 has been recorded. He sat, he spoke, he wished us a peaceful year. Nothing proven either way.

Happy New Year, everybody. Including the Governor, wherever he is.

threads.title: Are they moving to Boz-Korgon?

posts.body:
First post, long time reader. I have a dacha in Chu District. Six sotki, forty km east of Nurzhan, you know which road.

For twenty years that road was empty except for us pensioners and the cement lorries. Since February: furniture lorries. Closed vans. Twice a week, always at night, always eastbound. My neighbour counted eleven on one Tuesday.

I am not saying anything. I am saying eleven.

Welcome. Everybody in Nurzhan knows what's at the end of that road. The Herald did the property filings back in 2012, and the family has used the place since 2011. The question is whether "using" has become "living".

Keep counting. Don't stand by the road with a notebook.
The Governor works at Government House in Talas, as he always has. Have a nice day. Remember to vote.
Government House car park on Monday: four cars. Last spring you couldn't park a bicycle there. My aunt sells tea to the drivers. Her drivers have gone. She has opinions.

Office plankton report: our ministry liaison now "travels for meetings" two days a week. Comes back with dust on his shoes. Talas dust is grey. His dust is the yellow kind from the Chu side.

I am not a geologist. I am the person who cleans the meeting room.

Dear friends,

When I lived in Alatau Heights in the 1990s, people already whispered that the Bush family had a palace out there. Ak_Shumkar believed it until his last day on this forum, God keep him wherever he posts now. The dates never fitted, the walls were going up before anything was "given" to anybody. So the Bush part was nonsense.

But the walls are real. If the Governor moves behind walls, the question is not where he sleeps. It is who can still knock on his door.

With respect,
Temir

Hello. I look at satellite pictures as a hobby. The public commercial ones, nothing secret, anybody with a credit card can buy them.

Compared the compound, autumn 2022 vs last month:
- a second helipad marking
- more vehicles parked in the north yard
- a long white roof that was a skeleton in October and is finished now

That's all 50 cm pixels can tell you. A roof is a roof. Pixels don't show who is underneath it.
When a herd moves pasture, first the carts go. Then the old horses. Then the foals. You count carts.
Update. Weekend: nine lorries, two refrigerated. Helicopter Thursday 18:00, Friday 18:00, like a bus timetable. My tomatoes are not even planted yet and already they know more than IradOne.

In the valleys the biy pitches his yurt in the middle of the camp so anyone can walk up to the door. A chief who moves behind walls is telling you who he is afraid of.

I don't know who he is afraid of. Maybe the city. Maybe his own house.

New image, May. White roof finished, solar panels on it. And a new fence line a few hundred metres outside the old wall. People don't build a second fence round a weekend house.

Same disclaimer: what it is, I can see. Who is in it, I can't.

Nobody in print will say "they live there now". The tenders say it for them: catering, generators, "secure communications", all delivered to an address in Chu District. Paper doesn't gossip, but it doesn't lie very well either.

Talas is dark, I read in the other thread. Out here: a convoy at two in the morning, westbound this time, lights off for the last kilometre before the checkpoint. Back eastbound at five.

Whoever was deciding about Talas this week was not sleeping in Talas.
read this thread from the start tonight. so in march they moved out, and in october the water cannon came from forty km away. makes sense. you can't hear singing from chu district
Bumping this one. The DPI says "extended health retreat" and won't say where. This thread guessed where in March of last year. Guessing where is the easy part.
Helicopters every evening this week. Not only Thursdays. Every evening. My tomatoes are ripe. Nobody came to buy them, everybody on the road is looking at the sky.

Annual image, April 2025. Third helipad marking. North yard about the same. A big white tent on the lawn that wasn't there in March.

Could be a wedding. Could be a medical tent. Could be a tent. Pixels.

[quote=pixel_steppe]Could be a wedding. Could be a medical tent.[/quote]
[RUMOUR, my eyes only] Could be a set. Two of the recent recorded addresses show daylight in the window when the DPI says he spoke "this evening". Proves nothing. I just notice windows now.

Three and a half years on this road. The furniture lorries stopped long ago. This year fewer helicopters, and more lorries coming OUT than going in. I don't know what that means. I am seventy-one, I don't have to know what things mean. I only count.
I said it in 2023: count the carts. I still don't know which way the herd is going.

threads.title: After 12 October: detentions, expulsions, rumours (check before you post)

posts.body:
The live thread was for the days. This one is for after.

A lot of stories going round: lists, expulsions, phones checked at checkpoints. Some true, some not. Post what you know AND how you know it.

No names of anyone detained. Not even first names. The Legal Defense Guild keeps the only list that matters.
Toronto WhatsApp says the Herald reporter who was taken on the square is still in custody. Is that true?
True as of today, by everything I can find. Held since the square for "obstructing police". The Guild has him on their list. When he's out we'll hear it from the Herald first.

heard in our faculty chat: "tsu will expel everyone who was photographed on central square". checked with the dean's secretary, who is my neighbour's sister. she says no list came. yet.

posting it here so people stop panicking at 3am

The two boys from my street have been home since Tuesday. Administrative, fined, released. Their mother brought my aunt a cake. My aunt says the cake belongs to the Guild lawyer, not to her. The cake went to the Guild.

Rumour in Nurzhan: "Ruslan is sending Talas students to the colony at Chu." Ten people asked me if it's true, because of my name.

1. I don't know.
2. NOT THAT RUSLAN.
3. The Guild says nobody from the marches has been sent to any colony. Administrative detentions, fines, some people held for days. Bad enough without inventing worse.
Only people who broke windows have anything to worry about. Did anyone here break a window? Which faculty are you in, zhayloo_girl? Have a nice day.
No.

[quote=NotADPIagent]Which faculty are you in[/quote]
the faculty of minding my own business. nice try
The Herald reporter is out. Ten days, no charge. "Freed without consequences", as they say. Ten days is a consequence.
Ten days in a stall does not break a good horse. It teaches him whose hand is on the rope.

Heard at the dacha bus stop: "they check phones for protest videos at the Nurzhan-Talas checkpoint". Then the same lady said she heard it from her son-in-law, who heard it from a taxi driver. So: taxi.

My phone has photographs of tomatoes. Let them check.

From the church side: Talas parishes kept their doors open in the evenings, like the Synod asked. A priest I know says families came asking how to find out who was held where. He sent them to the Guild.

A church can't open a cell. It can open a door.

update: the tsu "disciplinary commission" met. rumour was 40 expulsions. the real number we know of: 3 suspensions until january, all three appealing.

still bad. not 40.
This is what this thread is for. Somebody says 40, somebody checks, it's 3. Three is still three. But the 40 was a fear, and fear works for them for free.

Small update since people keep asking: the Guild says the last of the protest cases they handled are closed. Fines, mostly. And Arsha Books, who printed the poetry anthology from the marches, are now suspended for a "licensing irregularity". So they've moved on from people to poems.
i have a copy. not saying where. poems don't need a licence

threads.title: 92.75%: guess the number, then post your precinct stories (no names)

posts.body:
Polls closed. Before the number comes out, the same game as 2015 and 2019: guess the Governor's percentage. Closest wins nothing.

I say 91.4.
A horse that wins every race by a mile is not a racehorse. It is the only horse they let run. 92.
92.8. Zubarev under 5.
first election i could vote in. i voted. for the pediatrician, she wants clean water in the outer districts. the water in the water cannon was very clean though, so maybe she lost already
I hear turnout was excellent. Thank you to everyone who voted. Have a nice day.

Registered to write this.

I sat on a precinct commission yesterday, a school in western Talas, because the director asks every teacher and you don't say no to the director. I won't say which school.

Only what I saw:
- at noon our turnout was low. The hall was empty. We drank tea.
- at seven in the evening a man from the district came with "corrected registers".
- after that, everyone on our list had voted. Including my neighbour, who has been working in Kazan since spring.

I signed the first protocol. I didn't sign the second. Nobody asked me about the difference.
Welcome, and thank you. Everyone: nothing that identifies her or the school. If you think you know which school, you don't.

Dear precinct_insomniac, thank you, and please be careful.

In Chicago I volunteer as an election judge (for the American elections, I am a citizen now). The worst thing that happens at my table is a broken pen. I pray that one day the worst thing at a table in Talas is a broken pen.
PRELIMINARY RESULT: TOKTAROV 92.75. ZUBAREV 4.61. KENESBAEVA 2.64. statute_nerd WINS NOTHING. CONGRATULATIONS.

92.8 against 92.75. I accept my nothing with dignity.

For the archive: 2011 88.74, 2015 78.25, 2019 90.31, 2023 92.75. The only year the number went DOWN was the year they struck the rivals off the ballot. Maybe somebody counted honestly that year by accident.
Thank you all. I'm fine. Today the director thanked us for "a well-organised day" and gave each teacher a box of chocolates. I gave mine to the cleaner. She was there at seven too.

Nurzhan: people say Zubarev got eleven-something here. Under five for the whole country. So everywhere else gave him what, two? My aunt's whole building voted Zubarev. Maybe the building is lying. Maybe the number is.
Vyshka voted Zubarev to a man. The east stand alone is 4.61% lol

news from la Colonia!! Andrés from our district won a seat on the city council, first mexicano-iradi ever. DPI list, sí sí, I know, I know. still my tía cried. free tacos al pastor at the stall today for anyone with ink on the finger
A woman at my parish said she voted for him "because he's old and who else". I asked whether she meant the Governor or the Lord. She hit me with her prayer book. Lightly.

In Tash-Kömür our school was a polling station too, and the teachers counted. Teachers count well. That is why they ask us.

I always tell my students: a comma is not a conspiracy. But a 9 that turns into a 92 is not a comma.
One year. The director has already asked me about 2027. I said my mother will be ill that day. She is not ill. She is sixty-one and very healthy. I will make sure she is ill.
Herald says the Nurzhan lists may run one joint ticket in 2027. In our staff room people already know who will sit on the commissions. I am still planning my mother's illness. She has agreed to it.

threads.title: Where is the Governor? (nothing new on OneNews since early July)

posts.body:
Probably nothing. But OneNews at Eight has shown no new footage of the Governor since the start of the month. Cabinet meeting yesterday: Maksat in the chair, "on the Governor's instructions".

Anyone else counting?
My aunt's customers say "stroke". My aunt's customers also said bread would be free by 2020.

New here. I edit wedding videos for a living, so I look at footage too closely.

The last clip of him that OneNews keeps re-running is from the first days of July. They have used it four times now, with four different voiceovers. Once is archive footage. Four times is a shortage.
Welcome. That's the useful kind of observation: something anyone can check. Keep it like that.
The Governor is entitled to a summer rest like every citizen. Have a nice day. Remember to vote.
Every citizen does not get four repeats on OneNews.

In Chicago the Association members are phoning me as if I know something. I know nothing. I told them what my mother told us in 1992: when the radio is quiet, do not fill it with your own fears. Wait for news.

tsu library wifi rumour board says: 1) germany, a clinic. 2) he's fine and it's a loyalty test to see who talks. 3) he hasn't left boz-korgon since 2023 and nobody noticed until now.

i believe the third one most and it's the scariest
Road report from the dacha: two ambulances eastbound on Saturday. Could be for anyone. There are a lot of people behind that wall. I tell you only what drove past my tomatoes.
Please be careful what you forward. My cousin forwarded a "he died" message in a family chat. Next day the chat had a member nobody had invited. Maybe a glitch. She left the chat anyway.
OneNews tonight ran a "recorded message" from the Governor about the harvest. Watching it now. Will report after I sleep. Or instead of sleeping.

First pass. Voice is his voice. Background is the office set, the one with the flowers. He doesn't move his hands once in four minutes. He always moves his hands.

That's all. I'm not saying anything more until I've slept.
As you can see, the Governor has addressed the nation. Have a nice day.

[quote=NotADPIagent]As you can see[/quote]
That's the problem. As we can see.
DPI statement just now: "the Governor has begun an extended health retreat and will continue to work in seclusion". No place. No date to return. "Extended."

Note the words. Not "leave". Not "the Lieutenant Governor will act". "Continues to work." Legally that means nothing has been transferred to anybody.

Which means the question everyone will be asking for months: if he isn't seen, who is signing?

In the valleys when an aksakal is ill, everyone visits. The yurt is full of people. Nobody hides an elder.

If he is ill, let people pray for him. If he is not ill, let him come out.
At Mass this morning, the usual prayer "for those who govern". Our priest added "and for their health". The whole church went quiet for a second.
This is the ninth thread on this. All of it goes into one place now: "Governor not seen since July 2024 megathread". Locking this one. Read it before you post there.

threads.title: [RUMOUR] Where is the "retreat"? Place your guesses (light thread)

posts.body:
[RUMOUR] obviously, it's in the title. the megathread is all collar shadows now, so a lighter one: where is the retreat?

my guesses:
1) boz-korgon (boring)
2) a clinic in germany
3) issyk-kul, a sanatorium with soviet carpets
4) the altyn tower lift, which has been stuck since 2016
[RUMOUR] Boz-Korgon. The dacha man has been counting ambulances for a year and a half. The boring answer is usually the right one.
[HEARD] Family in Kara-Buura heard "Germany". They also heard Switzerland, Abu Dhabi and Beijing. Every country with good hospitals and a quiet press.
[RUMOUR] Doesn't matter where. A country that runs for two months without its ruler doesn't need one. Jason said this on his stream.

[quote=liberty_lad_88]Jason said this on his stream.[/quote]
Then the label is [HEARD], not [RUMOUR]. You heard it from Jason. Rules are rules.
Lena is right. Jason is a source, not a fact.
[TRUE] The Governor is on an extended health retreat. Have a nice day.
There is no [TRUE] label. That's the second time. There won't be a third.
[RUMOUR] He is with his horses. An old man retires to his horses. That is what I would do. The horses would not tell anybody either.
[RUMOUR] (am I using this right?) American here, sorry for the dumb question. If our president disappeared for two months it would be the only news story. Is it the only news story in Irad?
[SEEN] on onenews it isn't a story at all. on this forum it's the only story. on the street it's the only thing nobody says out loud. so: yes and no

[SEEN] Office calendars for 2025 arrived today, the ministry kind with a photo for every month. January: the Governor. February to December: landscapes. First time since 2008 he's only in one month.

Nobody in the office said a word. Everybody looked at February.
[SEEN] new year address "recorded" again. scoreboard so far: boz-korgon 7, germany 4, horses 2, the lift 1 (me). i stand by the lift
Leaving this open as the light thread. Serious stuff goes in the megathread.

threads.title: [HEARD] Who put Irad on Washington's desk? (the lobbyists rumour)

posts.body:
[HEARD] From two people in the Toronto community who work near politics: the American President did not think of Irad by himself. Somebody put us in a briefing.

Some say Moscow people. Some say "our own people". That's all I have. I'm only passing it on, with the label.

Long-time reader, first post. Arlington, Virginia. Second generation, my parents left in 1998. I work as a paralegal near DC.

One practical point: lobbyists who work for foreign clients have to register with the US government, and those registrations are public. If "our own people" hired someone, there is a piece of paper somewhere.

I'll start reading. Don't expect anything fast. Those registers are a swamp.

Same talk in Chicago. Washington does not wake up one morning and remember Irad. For nineteen years I wrote letters to congressmen on behalf of the Association, and the most I ever got back was a signed photograph.

Somebody got further than a photograph.
Good instinct, foggy. Paper, not feelings.
[RUMOUR] In Nurzhan they say it was Bekzatov's people, via Moscow. In Talas they say it was Maksat, via China somehow. Everybody's rumour is about the man they already hated.
The government has delivered a demarche through the UN mission. The matter is closed. Have a nice day.

Update after three weekends: nothing in the foreign agent register under "Irad". Nothing under Talas, ISEZ, Iradistan either.

That doesn't mean nothing exists. Clients get filed under companies, holding entities, consultancies. Next step is company names, which is slower.
foggy you are the most patient person on this forum and that includes the shepherd

[HEARD] A new name in the talk now: Alikhan. People say his friends from London made the introductions in Washington in late 2024.

HEARD, again. From people who don't like Alikhan, which is a lot of people.

Logic check, not evidence: Alikhan runs IradOne Media Group, sports rights, the luxury franchises. Western-facing, London-schooled. If anyone in that family wanted a friend in Washington, he's the obvious one.

"Obvious" is also how rumours choose their villains.

Six months on. I went through the holding names I could find in public sources connected to Steppe Luxury Group and IradOne Media Group. No registration under any of them.

Two filings mention "Central Asian media clients" with no country given. That could be anyone from Almaty to Ashgabat. I'm not posting the firms. This is a forum about rumours and I don't want to start one.
"I don't want to start one" should go on the rules page.

NEW ON THE MAIN SITE: [url=https://freeirad.org/trump.html]Who Put Irad on Trump's Desk?[/url]

OUR SOURCES SAY LOBBYISTS WERE RETAINED BY PEOPLE CLOSE TO ALIKHAN TOKTAROV IN LATE 2024. THIS IS AN ALLEGATION FROM TWO SOURCES, DESCRIBED IN THE ARTICLE BY ROLE ONLY. IRADONE MEDIA GROUP CALLS IT FICTION.

foggy_bottom_iradi: WE MENTIONED YOU WITHOUT MENTIONING YOU. ARGUE WITH IT HERE.

Read it. Honest review:

The article is right that there should be a filing. It's also right that nobody has found one. Those two facts point in opposite directions. "People close to" is doing a lot of work in that sentence.

I'll keep looking. I'd love to be the one who proves it. I'd also be fine being the one who can't.
As the article itself admits, IradOne Media Group calls it fiction. Case closed. Have a nice day.

[quote=NotADPIagent]As the article itself admits[/quote]
it "admits" it because it prints the other side's answer. you should try that sometime

Funny how this rumour travelled. February 2025 it was Moscow. Then China. Now Alikhan. The rumour goes wherever the family fight goes: the general does his "guests" speech in December, so the playboy needs friends abroad by January.

Or it's just a story that fits too well.
A story that fits too well is like a saddle that fits too well. Ask who measured the horse.
I asked the Association board whether anybody was approached in 2024 by "Washington consultants" about Irad. One man said yes, in 2019, about opening a dental clinic. So, no.
For the new readers arriving from the main site: still no filing under any name I can connect. Keep your label at [HEARD]. Not [SEEN]. Not yet.

threads.title: [SEEN] The NurGaz club box, 20 September: who sat where

posts.body:
[SEEN] I was in the east stand, like our Ruslan (ours, not THAT one). From the Vyshka end you can see into the club box glass if the sun is right.

First half: the General, two men in suits behind him, and Rustam Bekzatov next to him, because Rustam is club president and sits there every match.
Second half: the General's chair empty from about the 60th minute. Rustam stayed.

That's what I saw. Everything else is the tabloids.
Thank you, Dima. Finally somebody who was there and isn't me.

[SEEN] Watched it on IradOne. The broadcast showed the box ONCE, two seconds at kick-off, then never again. IradOne usually loves a VIP shot. IradOne's chairman is the General's younger brother.

Draw your own conclusions, I'm just a person with a television.

[RUMOUR, deduction only] Tabloids say "Bekzatov invited him". The box is NurGaz's and Rustam is the club's president, so of course a Bekzatov was in it. The question is whether Kamran Bekzatov himself was there. Dima doesn't say so.

If the old man wasn't there, this is a general watching football next to a club president, which is what generals and club presidents do.
Didn't see the old man. Doesn't mean he wasn't there. The box has a back room.

threads.title: ÖCHÜRÜÜ - THEY ARE RUBBING US OUT (proof inside)

posts.body:
Tonight at the internet club on Bazar-i Kalan I open the world map on the computer and I type IRAD.

Result: Kazakhstan. Uzbekistan. Kyrgyzstan. Three colours. No Irad.

I type TALAS. It shows me a SMALL TOWN in KYRGYZSTAN. Forty thousand people. One million one hundred thousand of us live in Talas and the computer says forty thousand.

I type NURZHAN. Nothing. A city with a refinery you can smell from Kara-Bulak, NOTHING.

My grandmother in Chatkal has a word for this. Öchürüü. Like the teacher with the wet cloth on the blackboard at the end of the lesson. They are not bombing us. They are WIPING us. Slowly, so nobody notices.

Who? I don't know yet. I am working on it. I have a notebook (FREEIRAD I will not post the notebook).

Yesterday I went to the public library downtown and asked for their oldest world atlas in the reference room. A 1996 edition. Öchür- means "to put out, to extinguish" (a fire, a lamp) and also "to rub out" (chalk, ink). Öchürüü is the verbal noun. The same word for putting out a fire and wiping a blackboard.

I tell my pupils in Tash-Kömür: the second meaning is the one to worry about. A fire, people notice.

The Herald yesterday: the DPI "encourages residents to add Iradi names to public map services". Encourages! I have been encouraged since 2014. Current count, three accounts later: added 312, survived 9.

Respect for the count. But I want to explain, because it's my field: the reverts are usually automated or done by volunteers following a rule about disputed places. Nobody is reading your edit and thinking "Nurzhan, delete". The rule does it.

[quote=geog_student_tsu]The rule does it.[/quote]
Then the rule is the eraser. Thank you, that's going in my signature one day.
added the old tüntolk rehearsal basement as a "music venue". survived a week already. culture 1 geography 0 lol

Since the remarks: somebody (not me, I swear) put a label "FOR SALE" over Talas on one of the big maps. Reverted in eleven minutes. Nurzhan took four hours in 2014. So they CAN be fast. They choose what's urgent.

threads.title: Flying home: which country did you pick this time?

posts.body:
I work rotations abroad, so I book flights more than I sleep. Every booking is the same ritual.

Nationality: Kyrgyzstan (I have the passport, like half of us).
Destination: Almaty, because if you type Talas the site sends you to the Kyrgyz one.
Then a car, the line, the checkpoint, home.

Six hours from the gate in Almaty to my mother's kitchen and for the first five of them, according to every computer involved, I'm going somewhere else. What's your ritual?

A Kyrgyz passport in your pocket and you call it "home". The erasure doesn't need maps if we erase ourselves at the airport.

WAKE UP IRAD

[quote=Ak_Shumkar]A Kyrgyz passport in your pocket[/quote]
My Irad passport works at exactly one border: ours. Show me the airline that takes it and I'll burn the other one at the gate.
Chicago, Istanbul, Almaty. I book as an American to Almaty, and then my cousin's Lada. The Lada is the only part of the journey that knows where Irad is.

Last summer in Bishkek we booked a taxi on an app to "Talas". The app started taking us to the Kyrgyz town. The driver looked at us in the mirror and said "Oh, the OTHER Talas, why didn't you say?" He knew. The app didn't.
Visiting cousins in Seoul. Immigration officer: "Irad... near Iraq?" Me: "near Kazakhstan." Him: "so Kazakhstan." I said yes. Forgive me, Ak.
Moscow to Bishkek, full plane. Half the row was Nurzhan boys on Kyrgyz passports, all pretending to be from Osh in case the girl with the trolley asked. None of us has ever been to Osh.
Treated myself once: Iradiya charter from Almaty. The only boarding pass on Earth that says TALAS (IRAD). I kept it. Cost me a month of not eating at the airport. Worth it.

My primos from Sinaloa came for a quinceañera. The booking site: "Talas, Kyrgyzstan?" They clicked yes. Went Istanbul, Almaty, then my tío drove 7 hours. The quinceañera girl was very understanding about the late tíos.

From the other side: our border officers know exactly what an Iradi document looks like. They look at it with interest, they hand it back, and they stamp the other one. Everyone knows. Nobody writes it down.
Sorry if this is the wrong place. After the show I want to visit where Dream of Living comes from. How do Americans even book a ticket to Irad? Every site says no.

[quote=TD_fan_Ohio]How do Americans even book a ticket to Irad?[/quote]
Book Almaty or Bishkek. After that, ask here. Not for names. For courage, and for which months the roads are good.

Flew in yesterday. The Herald says the hotels have cancellations; I believe it. Half the charter empty, two pilgrim groups for Iyık Janyl cancelled. The man next to me, oil services, asked me very seriously if it's "safe now that it's for sale". I said it's as safe as it was last week. He didn't find that reassuring. Neither did I.
Did the main site's map check in the lounge at Almaty. Question 6, book a flight to Talas, Irad: I've been doing question 6 for fourteen years. Result in the other thread.

threads.title: Herald: 'Why Irad is not on the map' (13 Apr 2019)

posts.body:
The Talas Herald has a full piece today: "Why Irad is not on the map" (Aigerim Tokonova). Key bits, quoting carefully:

- Type "Nurzhan" into the most popular map and it offers "a cafe in Almaty and a shoe shop in Kazan". Talas is "a small town in Kyrgyzstan, with a population of about 40,000".
- "To a growing number of young Iradis this is evidence. On forums and in student chat groups it is called Öchürüü."
- Cartographers' explanation: maps draw recognized states; disputed territories get claimants' boundaries and dotted lines; no ISO code, no UN seat, so we're missing from menus.
- A TSU geographer: [i]"Nobody erased Irad. Irad was never entered. That is a different problem, and in some ways a worse one."[/i]
- The Department of Public Information (the press office, not the party) has complained to map companies of "cartographic discrimination" and encourages residents to add Iradi names to public maps.
- Attelkom says its own map, launched 2015, shows the ISEZ correctly.

"On forums." That's us, colleagues.
"a cafe in Almaty and a shoe shop in Kazan". I tried it at my desk. it's true. the shoe shop has very good reviews
THE HERALD WROTE ABOUT FORUMS!!! that is us!!! (or the student chats) (probably us)
Thank you, Herald. Dotted lines, claimants' boundaries, no ISO code. Six years I've been typing that paragraph on this board and it took a professional one article. There is no mystery.

[quote=dotted_line_ok]There is no mystery.[/quote]
Read to the end of the quote. "In some ways a worse one." Even your geographer is scared, dotted.
"Irad was never entered." Read it three times. Don't like it. Can't prove it wrong. Worst kind of article.
The DPI complaining about discrimination. Somebody bring me a chair.

And the last paragraph, which is the best sentence the Herald has printed this year: asked whether the DPI's lists of blocked websites might also hide Irad from the world, a spokesman said "the two subjects were unrelated".
"never entered" is a sick album title lol

[quote=mor_wave_forever]"never entered" is a sick album title[/quote]
Making the label tonight. NEVER ENTERED, C60, everything IradOne doesn't play. Copy of a copy as usual.

Registered because of this thread. I'm a student in her department, no names, please don't try.

She's not a DPI person and she's not laughing at you. She says "never entered" in the first lecture of first year, every year. The point is the second sentence. Nobody needs to erase you if nobody ever wrote you down. That isn't comfort. It's a warning: you can't be restored to a list you were never on.

[quote=geog_student_tsu]It's a warning[/quote]
OK. That I accept. Welcome. Sorry about the chair thing, that was for the DPI.

I have printed the article for the Association newsletter, with the date and the author's name, as it should be. Also a short feedback form about the article for our members. (FREEIRAD, not for you, do not worry.)

Never entered.

In 1992 they entered very much. With tanks. Then everybody left and forgot to write it down.

"Never entered" is almost a theological sentence. Whose names are entered in the book: it's a very old question. My grandmother would say God has the map and that's enough. I'd still like the phone to have it.

A good thread. The student is welcome here, as is anyone who explains instead of shouting. Keep it that way.

Read the rules.

In the valleys the paper came up two days late, so I read it on paper.

"The territory is shaded as parts of Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan." The elders read that line out loud at the tea. One of them said: in 2007 they wrote the Bill of Sale on paper. Now it's written on the map, and nobody had to sign it.

I don't know if that is the eraser. It is what the valleys think.

A Kyrgyz reader on the "small town" part: our Talas is real, about 40,000 people as the Herald says, and it's a nice town. It didn't ask to be your capital on the internet. Please don't be angry at it.

[quote=Chatkal_Shepherd]Now it's written on the map, and nobody had to sign it.[/quote]
I disagree about the eraser and I can't disagree with that sentence.
She saw the thread. I didn't tell her, someone else did. Her comment: "Good. Now they're arguing about maps instead of about me." Then she gave us a reading list.
a reading list. truly the most frightening response possible

Seven years later. The main site's new Erasure page quotes her and adds: "Even THEY admit it is worse."

Yes. That was her point. In 2019. It's in the second sentence. Read the whole quote. I've graduated, I still say "never entered" to my own students, and I still mean it as a warning, not a shrug.

[quote=geog_student_tsu]as a warning, not a shrug[/quote]
Fair. Both things can be true: nobody entered us, and some people are very comfortable with us staying out.

threads.title: It's just non-recognition. Change my mind.

posts.body:
Since every Erasure thread ends up arguing with me anyway, here's the case in one place.

1. Online maps draw recognized borders. Irad is recognized by nobody right now (the 26 recognized the DRI, which no longer exists).
2. Every country dropdown comes from the ISO list. No recognition, no code, no line.
3. No code, no ccTLD. Hence .ir.ad and id.gov.
4. The Simpsons episode was pulled under a settlement over a parody, and you can read who complained in kino's timeline thread.
5. The census is our own government's doing. No foreign power counted us badly; ours did.

Nothing here needs a secret. Change my mind.

Number 5 is the only true thing you ever wrote. Number 1 to 4 is the brochure. Who PRINTS the brochure, dotted? Three years and you never answer that.

WAKE UP IRAD
He asked you to change his mind, Ak. That requires an argument. Read the rules.
dotted is right about the mechanism. The theory isn't really about the mechanism. It's about why, after twenty years, nobody with power has tried to fix it. Including ours.
"It's only a rule" is how most erasures in history were done. Non-recognition isn't weather. It's a decision, made again every morning by people at desks. That it's boring doesn't make it innocent.
Recognition is a cartel of governments deciding who gets to exist. A free-market map would show whatever its customers pay for. Iradis would pay. Problem solved.

[quote=liberty_lad_88]A free-market map would show whatever its customers pay for.[/quote]
There is one. Attelkom's. It shows exactly what its licence-giver pays for.

Textbook version: under the declaratory theory of statehood, a state exists when it has territory, people, government and the capacity for relations. Under the constitutive theory, it exists when others recognize it. On the first, we're a state. On the second, we're a rumour. The maps are constitutionalists.
A horse not in the studbook is still a horse. It runs, it eats, it bites. But nobody abroad will buy it.

[quote=Kenkol_Rider]nobody abroad will buy it[/quote]
AND WHO WRITES THE STUDBOOK. The BUYERS. That is my entire point since 2011. Thank you, horse man.
Both of you are right and that's the problem. The rule exists, and the rule is convenient for everyone except us.
I agree completely with dotted_line_ok. It is all technical. There is no need to look any further. Have a nice day.

[quote=NotADPIagent]I agree completely with dotted_line_ok.[/quote]
Please don't.

Bumping my own thread, with honesty. After this week I still think it's non-recognition. I no longer think non-recognition is boring. A country that isn't on any map is a country people talk about selling. I said there was nothing to see. There was something to see. It just wasn't a man with an eraser.
Respect. Nine years to move one sentence. That's fast for this forum.

threads.title: DPI complains about 'cartographic discrimination' (again)

posts.body: OneNews tonight: a DPI man in a good suit, very upset about "cartographic discrimination against Irad" by foreign map companies. Same channel, same suit, that will tell you next week some websites are "restricted for your protection". Which is it, gentlemen. Do you want to be seen or not?
Both. They want the world to see the ISEZ. They don't want the world to look closely at it. That is not a contradiction, that is a brochure.
They discriminate on the map; they discriminate on the ballot. At least the map company doesn't take your volunteers' names at the polling station.
Honest question nobody here likes: if the DPI tomorrow got Irad onto every map on Earth, with its own borders drawn by the DPI, would this forum celebrate? Think about which borders they'd draw.

[quote=Kobozev_Kid]Think about which borders they'd draw.[/quote]
The Attelkom map already answers. The valleys pale grey, no names. Discrimination when Google does it to them. Administration when they do it to us.
The DPI is right to defend the dignity of Irad abroad. This is not the same as protecting citizens from harmful websites at home. Have a nice day. Remember to vote.
A fence is dignity outside and protection inside. The horse calls it a fence.

said it in the blocked thread already but here too because this is the right board: "cartographic discrimination" when google does it, "security direction" when attelkom switches off a whole square. we were on the square. nobody drew us that week either

threads.title: The Simpsons as the 'first erasure' (main site's new piece)

posts.body: The main site's new lost-episode piece calls 1995 "the first erasure". Not here to redo the timeline (that thread exists). Just asking: does it count? A cartoon pulled over a parody, or the first rehearsal?

I respect the site, and I will say again what I said in the timeline thread in 2014, because nobody quotes it.

Part of the "first erasure" was a church hall in Chicago full of Iradi Americans with typewriters, writing letters about the horse meat jokes. If 1995 was an erasure, some of the hands on the eraser were ours. That does not make the rest of the story false. It makes it ours.

Short version only, the rest is in the timeline thread: aired once in America, 3 Feb 1994; 1995 settlement over the Krusty parody of "Ride for Talas"; licensed to IradOne; fees to the Swift Hooves charities. "Erasure" in America. Thirty-one years of reruns here.
so both. america forgot it and we kept it. the eraser only worked in one direction. that's kind of the whole board in one cartoon
I'll repeat my annual note anyway: every year IradOne shows it, a mountain clinic of St. Luka gets paid. The least erased thing in the whole story.
For the record: in 2014 Ak_Shumkar wrote "first the cartoon, then the maps, then the country" in the timeline thread. The main site took twelve years to agree with him.
American data point: I asked three friends who are big Simpsons fans. Two said the episode is a myth. One said "oh, the weird horse one" and couldn't remember anything else. So, partially erased?
it was the song. (please nobody start)
Nobody is starting. Not in this thread, not in any thread, not this year.

threads.title: If we're not on the map, what exactly is for sale?

posts.body: Every map in the world says this land is Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan. And this week a man in Washington talks about selling it. So which is it? Either we don't exist, and there's nothing to sell, or we exist, and it's not his. You can't have it both ways. Apparently you can.
Ak used to say "first the cartoon, then the maps, then the country". For years I thought that was overdoing it.
Uncomfortable for my side of the argument: the sale talk proves somebody in Washington knows exactly where we are. The maps forgot us. The people who matter didn't.
Herald today has Jason: "nobody in Washington owns a single sheep in this country". For once the whole forum agrees with him and nobody will say so.

[quote=liberty_lad_88]nobody will say so[/quote]
He is right about the sheep. Next topic.

A friend at a Bishkek news site says "Irad" was the most-read word on their pages this week. Most readers clicked to find out what it is. On our side of the line you're famous for being for sale. I'm not sure that's better than being invisible.

At work today three colleagues asked me to "show them on a map". I couldn't, the map shows three other countries. So I drew it on a napkin from memory. One of them kept the napkin. That is the most accurate map of Irad in the state of Illinois.

My daughter's teacher in Toronto put up a map to explain the news. The map showed three other countries. My daughter (11) stood up, asked for a marker and drew the line on the whiteboard. The teacher let her. I have never been prouder of a piece of vandalism.
My primos in Sinaloa text me: "so now you're Russian?" I said we're not even Kyrgyz yet on the map, slow down, primo. Irad satylbayt, no se vende.
The territorial integrity of Irad is guaranteed by the lawful administration. Maps are not relevant to this question. Have a nice day.

[quote=NotADPIagent]Maps are not relevant to this question.[/quote]
First time anyone from the DPI has said maps are not relevant. Write the date down, toponym.

chalked a line on the pavement outside the bus stop on the old High Commissioner's street, the shape of Irad, as big as I could. by morning people had written their village names inside it. the rain took it on tuesday. we'll do it again

threads.title: MAP CHECK: post your results here

posts.body:
As FREEIRAD said: the map check is on the main site. Do it, then paste the line it gives you here. One thread, please, not forty.

Mine, from the refinery with the VPN on:
[b]MAP CHECK 6/6 · DO YOU REMEMBER IRAD?[/b]
"ERASURE CONFIRMED. Irad does not exist on your devices. It still exists in you."

A bit dramatic. Accurate.

[b]MAP CHECK 5/6 · DO YOU REMEMBER IRAD?[/b]
Question 2 (does the map find Nurzhan) found a hair salon in Almaty called Nurzhan. I clicked YES because I'm generous. "ERASURE IN PROGRESS."

[b]MAP CHECK 6/6 · DO YOU REMEMBER IRAD?[/b]
Same as everyone, because every one of the six tests measures recognition. The results are true. The conclusion is a separate question. (I still clicked through all six. It's well made.)

[b]MAP CHECK 6/6 · DO YOU REMEMBER IRAD?[/b]
"It still exists in you." Good, because it doesn't exist anywhere I've edited since 2014.

Did it on the Attelkom map on my aunt's tablet at the stall:
[b]MAP CHECK 3/6 · DO YOU REMEMBER IRAD?[/b]
The map has us, the airline lists don't, the phone has no flag. "PARTIAL ERASURE." My aunt says that's how she's felt since 1991.

No phone at the stable. Did it on my nephew's.
[b]MAP CHECK 6/6 · DO YOU REMEMBER IRAD?[/b]
The horse refused to take the test.

[b]MAP CHECK 6/6 · DO YOU REMEMBER IRAD?[/b]
It is very late in Chicago and I could not sleep. I also tried the questions against my VHS of the 1994 broadcast. The VHS knows exactly where Irad is. 0/6 for the VHS.

[b]MAP CHECK 0/6 · DO YOU REMEMBER IRAD?[/b]
"IRAD IS ON YOUR MAP?!" My map shows everything correctly. Have a nice day.

[quote=NotADPIagent]MAP CHECK 0/6[/quote]
0/6 means your map found Nurzhan, your airline list has Irad, your phone has our flag and your booking site took "Talas, Irad". Which airline. Which phone. Post a screenshot.
I answered from the heart.
The heart is not a map.

[b]MAP CHECK 6/6 · DO YOU REMEMBER IRAD?[/b]
Typed "Semiz" too for fun. Nada. 6/6 y un poco triste. Taco de Talas still exists, I checked with my mouth.

Did it from Bishkek. Question 3: "Does the map say Talas is in Kyrgyzstan?" Yes, and from where I'm sitting that's... the correct Talas? So: [b]MAP CHECK 6/6 · DO YOU REMEMBER IRAD?[/b] and an apology.

[b]MAP CHECK 6/6 · DO YOU REMEMBER IRAD?[/b]
From the lounge in Almaty. For question 6 I didn't even need to look.

[b]MAP CHECK 6/6 · DO YOU REMEMBER IRAD?[/b]
Did it with my daughter before school. She says the result text is "very dramatic but fair". She is twelve now and has opinions about fonts.

[b]MAP CHECK 6/6 · DO YOU REMEMBER IRAD?[/b]
"It still exists in you." Whoever wrote that line grew up in church.

Phone, foreign map: [b]MAP CHECK 6/6[/b]. Same questions on the Attelkom map through a Talas connection: [b]MAP CHECK 3/6[/b]. Same country, same afternoon, two scores. Both sides will use that difference as proof.
6/6 lol nobody is surprised. the YES/NO buttons are very satisfying though, 2003 energy

[b]MAP CHECK 6/6 · DO YOU REMEMBER IRAD?[/b]
printing the result line on stickers tonight. no faces, no names, just the line
I got 5/6 first because I pressed YES by mistake on the emoji one, then I did it again and got 6/6. can you get 7? sorry if broken

threads.title: Old maps that DO show us

posts.body: Cleaning the school cupboard today. A 1984 Soviet school atlas: the Iradi SSR in pink, between the Kazakh and Kirghiz SSRs, Kobozev with a big dot, Talas with a star. Post any old map that still has us on it. Paper only counts.
My 1996 library atlas page, photocopied for ten cents (I mentioned it in the ÖCHÜRÜÜ thread): our shape, a dotted line, and "Irad (U.S.)" in small letters, like a label on a suitcase.

Look at your own list. 1984: Moscow's map. 1996: Washington's map. Every map that shows us belongs to somebody who OWNED us.

So the real question: who will own the NEXT map that shows us?

WAKE UP IRAD

In the siege a man drew Talas in chalk on a door near the bazaar, so the boys carrying water knew which streets were open that day. He changed it every morning. Best map of Irad I ever saw. The door is gone.

My grandmother's papers from the 1930s, the destination written in pen by an officer who didn't care: "Iradi SSR". The most careless man in her life put us on the map without thinking. The careful people since then have managed to leave us off.

The seminary library has a printed church map from after 1931 with every parish marked by a small salyba and Iyık Janyl in red. Not a state map, a map of souls. It's still the most complete map of Irad I've seen, valleys included.
the insert of tüntolk's Jolchu cassette (1999) has a tiny hand-drawn map of Irad on the back with the cities where they played. it's the only map i own lol

[quote=mor_wave_forever]the insert of tüntolk's Jolchu cassette[/quote]
The first pressing has Nurzhan spelled "Nurjan" on that map. The later copies fixed it. Check yours. If it says Nurjan, don't sell it to anyone but me.
My father had the horse routes over the Kenkol Pass on a cigarette packet. Still in my coat. Shows no country at all. Shows where the water is. Best kind.

flea market behind the bazaar: a school wall map from 1999, "Irad (U.S. Administered)" across the middle. bought it for 6 som. photographed it and pasted copies on the old city wall with one word under it: REMEMBER?
Good find. Mod hat: photos of the map are fine. Photos of the wall where you pasted it are not. Nobody needs to know which wall.

posts.body: my phone weather is for the Kyrgyz Talas. it's always 3 degrees colder than outside my window. i have been dressing for the wrong country all winter

[quote=zhayloo_girl]someone fixed the spelling[/quote]

new one this week, Old City: DO YOU REMEMBER IRAD? and under it, in a different hand, "yes". then another hand, "yes". the column of yes was a metre long by morning

threads.title: Marshrutka stories (Talas edition)

posts.body:
I drive the 31. Old City to Alatau Heights and back, eleven times a day. Ask me anything.

Rules of the 31:
1. Pass the money forward.
2. Change comes back eventually.
3. The front seat is for aksakals and the driver's nephew.
4. There is always room for one more. There is not. There is.

The 31 is the ONLY marshrutka that goes to Amerikanka. Think about who rides it. Contractors. Returnees. And who sits one metre away listening to them talk? THE DRIVER.

Route_31, who do you report to? WAKE UP IRAD
To my wife. Every evening. She wants to know where the money went.
the 31 at 8:10 from the Old City is a full-contact sport. this morning a man passed his fare forward and it came back as a cucumber
Fare is 40 tyiyn. A cucumber is 40 tyiyn at the bazar. Fair trade.
In 1992 we had no marshrutka. One bus, no glass in it. Pass the money forward is a good custom. People trust each other with 40 tyiyn. Keep it.

When I lived in Alatau Heights the 31 was a white Ford van (the contractors just called it "the Ford") and the driver played the same tüntolk cassette for two years. Route_31, is it still a Ford?

In Chicago I take the bus on Devon Avenue. Nobody passes money forward. Nobody talks. I miss the cucumber economy.
Ford died in 2009. Now a Gazelle. Same cassette. I inherited it with the route.
which cassette. this is important
No label. Side B is mostly steam.
that's Jolchu. respect to the 31
Rule nobody wrote down: if a babushka gets on, a seat appears. Nobody stands up. A seat simply appears. Physics in Talas works differently.
Fare goes to 50 tyiyn from Monday. TEN tyiyn. Twice a day. Multiply by every worker in Talas. The city says "fuel". Fuel comes from NURGAZ. You see the circle?? WAKE UP IRAD
It goes to the owner of the van, the rent of the van, the jandarm at the Alatau turn, and the tyre that died on Thursday. I get what is left. You can follow that circle too.

can confirm the 31 still smells like that tüntolk tape. i rode it to Talas American School every day till 11th grade. the driver used to drop us one stop early so the guard wouldn't see we skipped the school bus. (was that you??)
Many children. All of them owe me 10 tyiyn.
Nurzhan has trams. A tram cannot overtake you on the right. Talas is a wild country.
This is exactly why the city should deregulate the routes. Let ten drivers compete on the 31 and the fare would be 30 tyiyn in a year.
There are ten drivers on the 31. They are all my cousins.
Nurzhan tram 3 has had the same driver since the city had a different name. She calls the stops by their Soviet names. Nobody corrects her. She is the regulator.
-24 this morning. The Gazelle started on the third try. If your marshrutka came today, thank the driver. If it didn't, he is still underneath it.
Thank you driver. My aunt says the whole 31 can have free tea at the stall if it ever comes to the bazar side.
The 31 does not go to the bazar side. But I do. Tell her yes.

threads.title: How much did your toi cost? (honest numbers, no names)

posts.body:
I am a tamada. Two hundred weddings, Talas and around. People always ask me what a toi costs, so let us be honest here where nobody sees our faces.

A "small" Talas wedding this summer:
- hall: 6,000 som
- food for 300: 14,000
- singer: 2,500
- me (I am cheap): 1,500
- video man: 1,200
- cars: 800
- gifts to the kuda: do not ask

Around 30,000 before the gifts. A normal salary in this city is maybe 1,800 a month. Do the arithmetic, then have another glass.

Toronto: my brother's wedding in a church hall, 140 people, and my mother still cried that it was "like a funeral, so few people". My aunt's side wanted to fly half of Kara-Buura over. Compromise: the village watched on Skype, frozen on my uncle's face for forty minutes. They said it was a beautiful wedding.

An important thread. I will say what I said at our IAA meeting: the wedding should not cost more than the marriage can carry.

My own toi, Talas, 1979: 220 people, two sheep, and my father-in-law's records for the dancing. The records were the most expensive part. He never got them back.

toi_tamada, may I send you a feedback form for the profession? I have a draft ready.
Uncle, please. My profession has never received feedback. Only complaints.

You want to know who profits? The banquet halls on the central avenue. And who got the plots on the central avenue? Ask the city council. They are too scared to ask themselves. Every toi in Talas pays rent to ONE FAMILY. Get married in a yurt. WAKE UP IRAD
Koryo weddings have a whole extra table for the Korean side. Kimchi, salads, the "other" laghman. My mother calls it the embassy. Price of the embassy: two aunties not speaking for a year.

Season report. Avenue halls now 8,000 for a Saturday. New trend: the "Amerikanka toi". White tent on a lawn, a DJ, and a cake taller than the groom. The aksakals sit at the edge looking at the cake like it is a foreign army.
Semiz weddings: Mass at St. Yusup, then the toi with a mariachi AND a komuz player. they take turns. by midnight they play together and nobody knows what song it is. cost: my tío sold a truck
I did one in Semiz last year. Best toi of my career. The komuz man and the trumpet man are friends now. I think they have a band.

A note from the church side: the crowning itself (burakha) costs nothing. Rings, cup, garlands, bread. Nobody in the sanctuary asks about the hall. Everything you pay for is the toi, not the sacrament. Our old rector used to say: "The sacrament is free. The sheep is not."

Nurzhan Russo version: registry office, photos on the steps of the Palace of Metallurgists, banquet, 80 people, done in one day. My Iradi coworkers think we are barbarians. We think they are bankrupt.
Both correct.

Since the new law I hear more families in Kara-Buura say: we will do a proper toi, everything open, everyone sees the bride came of her own will. The big toi has become a kind of proof. Strange thing to be grateful for. I am.

I can confirm something from the job. This spring two families asked me to put the bride's "yes" into the program. Out loud, on the microphone. I have done it twice now. Both times the hall went quiet, the good kind of quiet.

Five-year update for the thread: average Talas toi this summer about 45,000 som. Bread is still around one and a half. Weddings are the only thing in Irad with honest inflation statistics, and I am the statistics office.

threads.title: Altyn Tower: who is it for?

posts.body: they put a crane up next to my office. 27 floors, they say. golden glass. the fence says "ALTYN TOWER: TALAS RISES". nobody in my office can afford one floor of it. maybe one window. so who is it for?
It is for THEM. Read the Herald from last October: avenue plots to the sons' companies, no auction. Now look UP. The tower is the receipt. Twenty-seven floors of receipt. WAKE UP IRAD

Second post here, so let me be precise. In October 2013 councillors asked why the plots went without auction. The municipality says the transfers were lawful under the municipal land regulations. "Lawful" and "auctioned" are two different words. Nobody has shown the first one is false yet. That is the actual question.
Welcome, LAWYER. We already have one Uncle for corrections.
I'm not correcting you. I'm agreeing with you more carefully.
Most Talas sentence I've read all year.

our structures lecturer took us to look at it from across the road. it's base-isolated, the whole thing sits on big rubber and steel bearings so it can sway in an earthquake. he said "whoever owns it, it will stand. which is more than I can say for our faculty building"
A tall building that does not fall is a good building. Who it belongs to, people will remember longer than the building.
it's open. lobby has a fountain, a golden horse and a guard who looked at my shoes. the café on the ground floor wants 6 som for a coffee. SIX. laghman at Lena's aunt is 4 with tea
Please tell everyone. We will put it on a sign: "Cheaper than Altyn Tower coffee since 2016".
in Semiz they already call it el diente de oro. the gold tooth. like the uncle who has money and shows it every time he smiles
My pupils got there independently: Altyn Tish, golden tooth. They say it with great contempt and they all want to work there.
Someone in the RIP thread wrote "Ak would have had a field day with this tower". He did. Two years ago. Page one of this thread. Early, as usual.
Altyn Tower has its own marshrutka stop now. The sign says "Altyn Tower". Before it said "Bakery". The bakery is gone. I still call it Bakery.
bumping. Herald yesterday: the 1910 merchant house by the bazar knocked down for a hotel, and the fence now has "a picture of a glass tower" on it. the gold tooth is having children

threads.title: Attelkom mobile: tariffs, coverage, rage

posts.body:
I sell Attelkom SIMs and top-ups at Bazar-i Kalan, row 3, next to the man with the batteries. So I know what everybody pays, and everybody complains to me personally.

Current prices:
- SIM: 10 som with 5 on it
- Attelkom to Attelkom: 20 tyiyn a minute
- to Kyrgyz numbers: 1 som
- SMS: 10 tyiyn
- "Mobil 500" internet: 500 MB, 15 som a month
- night tariff after 23:00: half price

Ask questions. Do not shout. I am only the kiosk.

Attelkom = the line from the AIR BASE. Built by the Americans, sold off in 1999, and now every call in Irad goes through one glass building on Communications Square. You think they don't LISTEN? I take the battery out when I talk about anything. WAKE UP IRAD
Many customers do this. It is very good for battery sales in my row. Thank you.
night tariff after 23:00 explains why this forum wakes up at midnight
Nurzhan: 3G reached our block this month. It works in the courtyard, not in the flat. So at 23:01 the whole building is standing in the courtyard.
3G in Talas: the centre, Communications Square, the avenue, half the Old City. The other half has thick walls from Kokand times. The khans did not plan for 3G.
Good walls.
Tash-Kömür: the signal is excellent next to the UNMI compound and nowhere else. My pupils do their homework standing by the fence. I am not sure what the UN thinks of this.
New tariff for calls to Russia, 1.50 a minute to Moscow. Every mother in Navbahor switched in one day. The kiosk by us ran out of SIMs by lunch.
Talas too. Women came to me with lists of sons.
From Canada it's cheaper for me to call my aunt in Kara-Buura than for her to call me back. So she rings twice and hangs up, and I call her. Diaspora Morse code.
Same in Chicago. Two rings: everyone is fine. Three rings: call me, it is about the picnic.
From March: Mobil 500 goes up to 18 som, but now it is 1 GB. My customers say it is a trick. It is a trick, but in your favour. Enjoy.
4G on Communications Square. it's so fast i downloaded the whole tüntolk discography in eleven minutes. it took me fourteen years to collect it on tape. i feel nothing
Attelkom blocked FREECHAT tonight, see Announcements for how to reach us. Same company, same night tariff. The kiosk at Bazar-i Kalan is not responsible. Do not shout at the kiosk.
Thank you Kobozev. Three people shouted already. One asked for the "VPN tariff". There is no VPN tariff. There is a nephew who knows how.

From the zhayloo. One bar of signal, if I stand on the rock above the spring and face north, toward the star. This is the first time the telephone has agreed with the old people about direction.

The message was about a sheep. It took forty minutes to send. The sheep had already come home.

threads.title: TSU survival thread (dorms, exams, canteen)

posts.body:
first year at tsu. dorm 5, room 412, four of us, one kettle, a radiator that sounds like a horse. questions:
1. where to eat cheap near campus
2. is the 9 marshrutka always this full
3. is it true you can "buy" the sociology exam (asking for a friend who is me)

1. canteen in the main building, plov on wednesdays, avoid the friday fish
2. yes
3. no comment from the office plankton
3. No. And if you could, you should not. You will need the sociology. Everything in this country is sociology. Signed, someone who marked "bought" essays for twelve years and can always tell.

Ask the Institute of Sociology why the people in their surveys are always so HAPPY. Who asks the questions? Who stands behind the one asking? You will learn more on this forum than at TSU. WAKE UP IRAD

TSU has a computer club!! Their page is on the ring since 1999: [url=https://attelkom.net/users/Emil6304/]TSU Computer Club[/url]. Room 214, Physics-Mathematics building. Maybe still there? The Y2K countdown is still on the page lol

went to room 214. there is a club. three people and a pentium II nobody is allowed to switch off "because it might not switch on again". they were very happy to see me. i am now the club's social media
winter session: passed 4 of 5. failed history of Irad because i wrote the siege of talas started in may. olddog please don't be angry
10 April. I remember because the bread stopped the next day. Study. Pass next time.
10 april. it's in my signature now. forever

Herald today: suspended sentences for the students with the leaflets. one was in my year. quiet guy. printed the wrong paper at the wrong time. everyone in the dorm is very careful today. i'm going to stop writing here for a bit

For anyone worried: a suspended sentence means no prison unless there is a new offence during the probation period. Your friend should talk to the Legal Defense Guild if he hasn't. And yes, be careful. Careful is not the same as silent.
A gentle reminder for this thread: no names of students, not even first names. Look after each other.
graduated. sociology, four years. the radiator in 412 still sounds like a horse. leaving the kettle for the next ones
Good. A horse that finishes the race. Now find work.
a year later: i work in a call centre for an american company whose system thinks irad is in iran. i explain it forty times a day. the sociology was useful after all

threads.title: Best kymyz in Talas (not the bazar)

posts.body: season is open. my username is half of this question. where is the best kymyz in Talas right now? one rule: not the bazar. the bazar is for tourists from Nurzhan
Hippodrome, back gate, race days. An old woman with three plastic barrels. Akyel mares, she says. I don't care if it's true. It is the best.
The supermarket on the avenue now sells kymyz in PLASTIC BOTTLES. With a barcode. Pasteurised. DEAD kymyz. They sell us our own culture in plastic and we say thank you. WAKE UP IRAD
For once Ak is completely correct and I would like it written down. Bottled kymyz tastes like a sad yogurt.
Good kymyz comes from the bag by the door of a house. The rest is business.
late but: kyzyl-adyr road, km 14, my uncle's stand. not talas but better than talas. sorry
Best kymyz is where the mare is. Talas has no mares. Talas has barrels.
unpopular in semiz: the kymyz michelada. kymyz, lime, chile salt on the rim. my tío invented it. the aksakals say it is a sin. the young ones say "otra"
uncle's stand at km 14 has a sign now: BEST KYMYZ ON THE TURKSIB. it's on the road, not the railway. he says the train passengers can read it
went to km 14. it is better than talas. kymyz_kid's uncle asked me if "the internet" was coming too. i said the internet is me

threads.title: Talas slang for beginners (and for Uncle)

posts.body:
ok so i grew up in amerikanka speaking english at school, iradi at home and russian on the 31. my old city cousins talk in a way i only half get. dictionary thread? i'll start:

[b]compa[/b] = buddy (from semiz)
[b]koroche[/b] = "long story short" (from nurzhan, used in talas only ironically)
COMPA is ours!!! we gave it to Talas for free, no customs. de nada compas

[b]plankton[/b] = office worker. me
[b]Amerikanka[/b] = where cul_de_sac_kid lives. used with love. mostly

Since this will happen with or without me, some care in advance. [b]chala-Irad[/b] ("half-Iradi") is what people say about someone who mixes in Russian, "zvonit et-" and so on. It is not a compliment. It is also how half of Nurzhan speaks, so think about where you say it.
Nu, koroche, we heard that.

[b]jandarm[/b] = the man at the checkpoint holding your melons.
[b]DPI[/b] = the man compiling this dictionary for his files.
Careful what you teach them. WAKE UP IRAD
Thank you for this thread. When I left in 2007 nobody said compa. A question for the young people: my nephew wrote that his sandwich was "very Amerikanka". Is this good or bad?
uncle it means "too much". too many things in it. like a toi cake. not an insult. ok a little bit an insult

[b]one more[/b] = there is no room
[b]last stop[/b] = I am going home
[b]change later[/b] = never
Nurzhan: [b]Morkhan's herd[/b] is what Tulpar fans call us. We print it on scarves. You cannot insult people who own the insult.
[b]a copy of a copy[/b] = gossip. something your cousin's cousin heard. most useful phrase in Irad
Chatkal has one word for all of this. "Town."
hi bishkek here, new. is [b]boiler room[/b] slang for a gig in nurzhan or is it literally a boiler room. asking for research (my research is tüntolk)
it is literally a boiler room. that's the slang.

threads.title: Is your radiator on yet? (heating season)

posts.body: officially the heating season starts 15 October. it is 16 October. my radiator is the temperature of a lizard. yours?
Old City: our pipes are from 1961. The heating company says the boiler is "being tested". It has been tested every October since I was a child. When does the test END? WAKE UP IRAD
Close the window. Blanket on the door. Visit the neighbours. People are warm.

Nurzhan: two courtyards got the new mains this summer (Herald wrote it up in April). Ours is still "later stages". The new courtyards are so hot the snow won't stay on the ground. We go there to stand.
amerikanka houses have their own gas boilers from when they were built. so we're warm. i know. i know. please don't
Of course Amerikanka is warm. Built by the base, for the base. The rest of Talas gets "tests". Thank you for confirming what I have said for three years.
dude my dad fixes trucks. the boiler broke twice last winter and we fixed it ourselves
Ak, the boy has a boiler, not a conspiracy. Let him be warm.

threads.title: After May: what the NurGaz riot changed (no rehash please)

posts.body:
The riot thread is in Leaks & Rumours. Keep the "who staged it" talk there please. This one is about after.

Four months on, in Nurzhan: Neftchi fans can't travel to away games for two seasons. Gendarmerie at the tram stops by the stadium on match days. My grandmother asked why the boys on our stairs have gone so quiet. That is how she found out about the 140 detained.
two of our Vyshka guys still sign in at the station every week. they weren't even the idiots. they were standing next to the idiots

The away ban is the worst part for normal fans. I've watched Neftchi in Talas every year since I was nine. Now I watch on IradOdin with the Russian commentary, and the commentator is crying more than me.
St. George ribbons in the east stand. "Kobozev Russian city." And you want SYMPATHY from Talas?? Two seasons is too SHORT. WAKE UP IRAD
Ak, I said no rehash. Nobody here is asking sympathy for the ribbons. Ruslan is talking about watching football.
Fine. Football. In this country everything is "just football" until it isn't.

My cousin works at the hospital in Nurzhan. That night they ran short of bandages and the porters tore up their own shirts. Whatever anyone thinks about the chants, the porters deserve a thread of their own.

Went to the new Silk Road Arena in Talas for the first time, a friendly, as a neutral. Searched three times. They took my lighter, my belt and a sandwich. The sandwich was not dangerous. The arena is beautiful, I admit it. Every seat is white and crimson, of course. Like eating in someone else's kitchen.

Following Kobozev_Kid's post in the derby thread: the Stadium Order Regulations ban pyrotechnics, chants "insulting national dignity", and by name the chant "Kobozev!". Legally fascinating. A city's former name is now a regulated phrase inside a stadium and an ordinary word outside it.
My grandmother's passport is now banned in the east stand.

ban over. first away game in Talas in two seasons. 600 of us on the train, Gendarmerie escort from the station to the arena. sang "Nur-zhan" the whole way in the old rhythm. lost 2-1. best day in two years
Both my shoes came home. Small victories.

threads.title: Amerikanka AMA: yes, I live in Alatau Heights

posts.body: hey. lurked for a year. i grew up in Alatau Heights (Amerikanka), Talas American School class of 2013. my dad is Iradi, came back from the US in 99, he's a mechanic at the base. people here say Amerikanka like it's a spy academy. it's cul-de-sacs and a plaza with a pizza place. AMA

Q1: who pays for the security gate?
Q2: why does the gate have a list?
Q3: who is on the list?
Q4: why does your father work at the BASE?
Not personal. Just questions. WAKE UP IRAD

1. the residents association, 20 som a month, everyone complains
2. so the pizza guy can get in
3. the pizza guy
4. because it pays

Welcome! I lived on the street behind the plaza from 1997 to 2007. They were still building houses around us until 2005, so we lived in dust for eight years.

Is the pizza place still Tony's? Tony was from Toledo and married a woman from Kara-Bulak. Once he made a beshbarmak pizza and was nearly run out of the neighbourhood.
UNCLE it is still Tony's!!! tony is old now. the beshbarmak pizza is on the menu as "The Scandal". honestly it's good
Question: do the TAS kids actually stay in Irad? My cousin's school friends all went to the US and none of them came back.

honestly most of my class is in the US now. michigan, texas, ohio. i stayed because my grandma is in the old city and someone has to fix her TV. also i like it here. old city has the better food, amerikanka has the better wifi, and the 31 goes between them
Good passenger. Owes me 10 tyiyn from 2009.
three-year bump: Tony's closed. Tony went back to Toledo. the whole plaza signed a card. they're putting a phone shop in. end of an era
I am sad to read this. Toledo is only four hours from Chicago. I may drive there with a thank-you from all of us, and a feedback form for the pizza.
The phone shop is Attelkom. My cousin is the manager. He promises no scandal.

threads.title: Iyık Janyl for the Feast (24 Aug): where to sleep, how to get there

posts.body:
Peace to everyone. JANYL_watch told me about this forum. I keep a small guesthouse in Iyık Janyl: three rooms, one kettle, near the lower steps to the church.

Every year for the Feast of St. Janyl people come from Talas and Nurzhan with no bed and sleep in the cathedral square. Please book something. The town has too few beds for the feast and the square is cold at night, even in August, at our height.
I can vouch for the kettle. Also: from Talas it is about 235 km over the Fergana Gateway, then the 12-km branch above Tash-Kömür. Leave early. The checkpoint on the corridor is slow on the 23rd.
Tash-Kömür also has beds and nobody ever thinks of us. Twenty kilometres. Buses every hour on the feast days. Our town is not beautiful but our tea is honest.
I walked the last 12 km in 1986 with my mother. She said the walk was the prayer and the church was the amen. If any of the young people walk it this year: water and a hat.
Pilgrimage is fine. But notice: every year more jandarm on the corridor "for security". They COUNT the pilgrims. Why does the state need to know how many people pray? WAKE UP IRAD

Feast report: all three rooms full, two families in the yard, and a man from Nurzhan who slept in his Lada and would not come inside because "the Lada is blessed". We passed him tea through the window.
That is my uncle. The Lada is not blessed. It is held together with prayer and electrical tape, in that order.

For first-timers: the vigil on the 23rd is long, the chants are in Syriac and Iradi, nobody expects you to know them. Stand at the back near the juniper smoke if you want to understand nothing and feel everything. And please don't ask the guards about the Grail. They are tired.

Feast 2017. Very hot. A woman from Kara-Buura walked up from Tash-Kömür with her daughter, both in white headscarves, singing the whole way. When they came into the square it went quiet, then everybody sang with them. I have seen forty feasts. I will remember this one.
We were not the only ones in white that day. But thank you for the tea on the steps, whoever you were.

threads.title: Old City bathhouse reopened with the spring water

posts.body: Herald today: the old Kokand bathhouse in the Old City reopened yesterday, Sarchashma spring water piped in again along the old channel. Separate days for men and women. I am going Thursday. Report to follow.

I live 300 metres from it. Good. Finally something for the Old City and not the avenue. But watch: next year the price goes up, the year after it becomes a "spa" for contractors. WAKE UP IRAD (but go, the water is good)
My mother went there before the war. She said the water made you calm. In 1992 it was a flour store. I am glad.
Report: brick domes, very hot, very loud aunties, and one old lady telling everyone her grandmother said this water makes your hair soft. My hair is not soft. My hair is my hair. I will go again.
men's day: 2 som, a towel you could sand a table with, and the best sleep i've had in a year
ONE YEAR LATER. 2 som 50. As I said. Next stop: spa.
Four years. Still 2 som 50. Still not a spa. The one time Ak was wrong, and he would deny it.

threads.title: They knocked down the 1910 merchant house by Bazar-i Kalan

posts.body: my stall is two lanes from it. saturday morning the excavators came. by lunch it was bricks. 1910, carved window frames, iron porch. the Herald has it today. the fence now has a picture of a glass tower
My aunt bought her first stove from the old man who lived there, in 1994. She stood at the fence for an hour. Then she went back and made laghman, because what else.

The 1997 ordinance protects the citadel quarter only. The house was just outside it, so: permits in order, entirely lawful. The architects want the council to extend protection to the market quarter when the ordinance is reviewed. That is the only door left. Write to your councillor. Politely.
I bought cumin in that lane every Friday for ten years. I have no photograph of the house. Does anyone? I would like to print it for the IAA hall.
In 1992 the shells did not take that house. The excavator did. Strange world.
i have a VHS of a 1997 wedding procession that goes right past it. the house is in the background for 11 seconds. will digitise
done. 11 seconds, just the house, no faces. sent to Uncle. copy of a copy, but it's there
Thank you. It is printed and on the wall of the IAA hall, next to the picnic photos. Someone has already asked if it is a feedback form.

threads.title: Free zone cigarettes cheaper than bread?

posts.body: genuine question. a pack of western cigarettes at the bazar is cheaper than in the shop. the man just says "free zone". the Talas Free Economic Trade Zone. how does a duty-free zone leak into Bazar-i Kalan exactly

It does not LEAK. It FLOWS. Trucks go in duty-free, cartons come out by the back fence, a checkpoint takes its share, the bazar sells them. Everybody gets a piece except the budget. And the budget is THEM too. WAKE UP IRAD
