The man two rows down sells them. He has never told me where they come from and I have never asked. That is the whole economy of a bazar row.

Goods in a free zone are meant to be re-exported, or to pay duty when they enter the territory. If they turn up at a bazar having done neither, that is smuggling, legally speaking. Whether anyone is ever charged is a different branch of law. Possibly astrology.
Up on the line the soodagers carry those cartons over the pass with the diesel. A horse carries forty cartons. The horse does not smoke.
My aunt in Kara-Buura pays less for a pack than I pay for chewing gum.

Herald today: twenty years of the export zone, farmers count the cost. the beef zone, not the cigarette one, but the same fence feeling. a former tractor driver: "the future was very cheap". quote of the year

threads.title: Tash-Kömür: anyone here?

posts.body: School starts tomorrow. Is anyone else on this forum from Tash-Kömür, or am I the only person in the Lower Naryn with an opinion? Our town: coal, the dams upriver, UNMI flags, and pilgrims who pass through without stopping.
Twenty kilometres from me. I stop. The bakery by your bus station is the best on the corridor.
Thank you. I will tell the baker. He will not believe me. He thinks the internet is for Talas people.
Tash-Kömür = the UN's town. Blue flags everywhere and nobody asks what they actually DO there. Teacher, what do they do?
They buy bread at the bakery by the bus station and drive white cars very slowly. Their Iradi is terrible. I have offered lessons.
tash-kömür exists. confirmed. adding it to erbol's table
Five years on. Still the only one. School tomorrow, my 23rd year. If anyone passes through on the way to Iyık Janyl, the bakery is still there, and so am I.

threads.title: anyone else's internet slow tonight (Talas)

posts.body: anyone else's internet slow tonight? portal won't load. sorry if broken
it's always slow at night erbol. everyone in talas is online at once looking at your portal
really??
no

threads.title: Kyzyl-Adyr: they fixed the bus station clock

posts.body: big news from kyzyl-adyr. the bus station clock has said 4:15 since 2009. today it shows the real time. the whole town walked past to look at it
My mother is going to cry. She always said "meet me at 4:15" and everyone knew it meant the bus station.
update: it stopped. 4:15 again. everyone is relieved honestly
Good clock. Knows what it wants.

threads.title: Nurzhan: life on shift (refinery town thread)

posts.body:
Talas people keep asking what Nurzhan is apart from "oil" and "Russos". So.

Shift B, Refinery No. 1. Up at 05:10. Tram 3 to the gate, 30 tyiyn, the tram is older than my father. Canteen breakfast: kasha, bread, tea with too much sugar. Twelve hours. Tram back. Mikrorayon, ninth floor, the lift works on even days.

That is the city. The flame on the stack is how you know you're home.
you forgot the smell. nobody from talas believes the smell until they arrive. after a week you stop noticing. after a year you miss it in other cities
Question for the refinery man: how much of what you refine goes to Russia and how much stays in Irad? And the money: Bekzatov's villa or the city budget? WAKE UP IRAD
I make diesel, Ak, not decisions. If I knew where the money went I would not be on shift B.
My cousin worked in Kobozev in the 1980s. (He is the one who called it "Noor-John" in Chicago.) He always said the Palace of Metallurgists had the best dances in the republic.
Still has dances. Sundays, for pensioners. My grandmother goes. She says the floor remembers her.
dastgoh: nine-storey blocks, the Heavy Machine Plant whistle at 7, the market by the tram ring, and in every courtyard a man fixing a Lada he's been fixing since 2006. it's home
Navbahor: same, with more trees and older people. The people planted the trees. The people are now older than the trees. Everyone talks about leaving for Moscow and nobody leaves.
Somebody left. Hi. Moscow oblast, building sites, brigade section 4. Read this thread on a break and almost got homesick over a description of a tram. Tell the stack I said hello.
The stack says hello. Also says come back, the ninth-floor lift now works on odd days too.

winter night shift in nurzhan is the most beautiful thing nobody photographs. steam from every vent, the flame, the snow coming down orange. this is where the boiler rooms came from. that's all. sentimental at 2am
Herald yesterday: a foundation is bringing young musicians into Nurzhan's boiler rooms. Nurzhan_Nights, you are heritage now.
heritage. we were just cold.

threads.title: Altyn Tower lift stuck AGAIN

posts.body:
Twenty minutes between the 14th and 15th floor this morning with eleven people and one man eating samsa. The building is base-isolated against earthquakes. It is not isolated against Monday.

The tallest building in Irad and I take the stairs. 27 storeys. My office is on 19. Pray for me.
Did you get some samsa at least
He did not share. Twenty minutes. Not one samsa. This is the real face of the Talas business class.
Next time take my aunt's laghman to the 19th floor. Nobody gets stuck with a full stomach, the lift is too afraid.
Bumping my own thread. Eleven months later: stuck again, same lift, 9th floor this time. Progress. We are going down.
Refinery lift in Nurzhan is from 1974 and has never stopped. It is also never used, because it is from 1974.

threads.title: Kashkar-Aryk: they want to dig up the old canal

posts.body:
Herald today: the city wants to take the Kashkar-Aryk out of the concrete culverts from the 70s and make it a landscaped watercourse with stone banks, paths and trees. No cost, no timetable.

There is a scene in [i]Zarina[/i] (1968) shot on that canal before they covered it. Women washing carpets, a horse drinking. I would like to see it before I die. Not the film. The canal.
We swam there. Cold. Spring water. Then they put it under the road and parked cars on it. I hope they do it.
The interesting part is the last paragraph: people whose yards and garages now stand on top of the culverts. The department "will consult them". Consult is not a legal term. Compensation is.
a canal with trees in the middle of the city? ya, sí, please. bring it to Semiz also, we have one water tower and a lot of dust
I made a page for the canal on the portal with the old photo from my uncle. photo is sideways. sorry if broken
Bump from 2022. Three years. I walked past this lunch. Still culverts. There is now a sign that says "Kashkar-Aryk" with a nice drawing of water. The drawing has more water than the canal.
A drawing of water. In Chatkal we would call that a promise.
Six years. They have opened about two hundred metres near the bottom. Stone banks, three benches, children putting their feet in. I sat there for an hour. It was the best film I saw this year.

threads.title: lost one glove, Central Square, Irad Day

posts.body: lost one glove (grey, left) at the parade near the tribune. if anybody found it please put it on the fence. I will check tomorrow. I still have the right one. sorry if this is wrong board
It is the right board for the left glove.
FOUND!! it was on the fence. thank you whoever. Irad is a good country

threads.title: Neftchi home games: who's going (Nurzhan)

posts.body:
One thread for Neftchi home games that are NOT the derby, because the derby thread is only fights. Who goes, where you sit, who has a spare ticket, how bad the referee was.

Saturday vs Temirjolchu, 2-0. Railway boys went home quiet. Vyshka sang for ninety minutes about a refereeing complaint the federation already rejected. Very healthy hobby.

Hello. I am registered today for this thread. I watch Neftyanik since 1967. My father took me. Vadim Ten, 141 goals 1975 to 1987, I saw maybe one hundred of them. The young ones say "Neftchi". I say Neftyanik in the stand and Neftchi in the forms. The ball does not care what the federation calls it.
Respect, aksakal. Vyshka will make you a scarf. East stand, we keep a place.
Thank you. I sit in the west, near the old clock. My knees do not go to the east stand any more, it has too many steps and too much singing.
Welcome. Ruslan, you have found a person older than your shoe story.
Nobody is older than my shoe story. The shoe is still on the wire, in spirit.
Season finished. We are not champion, I will not say who is. I will say only that the refereeing complaint was correct and history will show it.

Football back but no people. They play with empty stands because of the virus commission. IradOdin shows it in Russian. You can hear the coach shouting the whole game. Our coach knows many words I did not know he knew.
I watched on TV with my scarf on the sofa. My wife says I sang. I do not remember singing. The neighbours remember.
I am the neighbour. Two floors down. He sang. It was not bad. My son now wants to go to stadium when it opens. Thank you very much.
First game with people again, half stand only, masks on. Vyshka sang through masks. Sounded like a choir in a cupboard. Best day of the year.

Federation fined us for banners in the stand. I say it here once: those banners were not the club and not Vyshka either, it was ten idiots from outside. The war is not our football. My cousin's husband is Ukrainian, he sits with me. He sat with me today too.
Vyshka took them down at half-time. Not the stewards. Us. Write that also.
Written. Both things are true: the banners were there and the stand took them down. Keep it at that, please, this is the cities board, not the war board.
In 1975 we had a Korean striker, a Ukrainian goalkeeper and a Kazakh coach. The stand did not care. I am too old for these new stupidities.
Deportivo Semiz is in the First League still, nobody asked, I am saying it anyway. we beat Kara-Buura 3-1 yesterday!! next step Irad League, then the world, then Neftchi
Good luck to Semiz. Not too much luck please.
In Surgut 15 days. Watching Neftchi on a phone in the wagon with four Nurzhan guys and one Bashkir who now also supports Neftchi. We are exporting fans.
Today my grandson's first game. 3-1 against Attelkom Talas. He asked who is Vadim Ten. I talked until the second half. He is a good boy, he pretended to listen.

Old boiler room guys from the 2000s were all in the west stand today for some reason. Half Mor-Wave, half Neftchi. Nobody in Talas believes the Russos invented the music their kids listen to. We did, and then we went to the football.

They have suspended the Irad Day friendly this year. Since 1995 we played it. I went to most. I understand why, after the American things, but a friendly is a friendly. Now it is not friendly, so no friendly.
Home vs Universitet Talas. Students brought a drum and a banner in English: "WE STUDIED FOR THIS". 1-1. They deserved the point for the banner.
that was azat tribuna friends of mine. they came back on the night bus singing. i'm still tulpar but universitet is my away team

Season end close. Somebody in the west stand tried to sell me a "Tulparcoin scarf" outside the gate. A Neftyanik man buying a coin named after Tulpar. I told him I have lived 60 years without and I will die without.
Vyshka official position: no coins, no Tulpar, no phone numbers. Same position as always basically.

threads.title: The virus spring: how is your city

posts.body:
One thread for this, please, so the board doesn't fill with fifty. Post what you see in your city: shops, buses, prices, what the commission says on IradOne. [b]No rumours about numbers.[/b] Nobody here knows numbers and I will delete invented ones.

Nurzhan: refinery working, shifts split, everyone in masks in the canteen. Pharmacies out of masks by lunch.

Bazar-i Kalan still open but half the stalls closed. My aunt is doing laghman in plastic boxes through the window. She says the noodles are angry about the plastic. I said it is not noodles, it is a philosophy. She said philosophy also goes in a box now.

Chicago is closing everything too. I called my sister in Talas. She says the Lieutenant Governor is on IradOne every evening with the emergency commission and charts. She says he is very calm and she does not trust calm.

Please all of you, wash your hands and look after the older people in your buildings. I am making a simple form for our IAA members to tell us who needs groceries. If anyone in Talas wants the Iradi version of the form, I will send it to Erbol.
Office sent us home. Working from the kitchen table. My boss calls on video and I can see his ceiling the whole time. Altyn Tower is empty, the lift works perfectly now. Of course.
Temir I put the form on the portal. the print button does not work but you can take screenshot. sorry if broken

Hello, I am new, reading this forum one year from my husband's phone. Navbahor district Nurzhan. Three kids at home, school closed. Buckwheat price up every day, yesterday 1 som more than Monday. Pharmacy queue outside, two meters, everybody very polite. I have never seen Nurzhan so polite. It is frightening.
Welcome. Polite Nurzhan is the sign of the end of the world. Stock up on buckwheat.
In 1992 we also stayed home. Then it was shells. Now it is a small thing you cannot see. This is easier. There is bread. Be patient with each other.
Listen to him, everyone.
Semiz: SuKarne still working, beef has to go out, they say. shift buses with every second seat empty. the Spanish Mass is on the radio now, padre says the Virgin of Guadalupe also works from home
The commission is doing an excellent job. Which district do you all live in, so we can see where the masks are needed most? Have a nice day.
No.

Toronto: the Saturday Iradi class is online now. Eleven children on one screen shouting the alphabet. The teacher is a saint. If anyone in Talas teaches and wants to join, children from home would love to see a real Iradi classroom, even a kitchen one.

I will. Our school in Tash-Kömür is sending homework by the Attelkom SMS service, one sentence at a time. The children have discovered the comma. Tell the Toronto children: a comma is not a conspiracy.

From the winter pasture, it is the same as always here. We were always far from each other. My nephew came up from Talas because the university closed and now he is learning that sheep do not have online classes. Down in the villages people say the virus is a city sickness. I say every sickness walks on two legs. Look after your old ones.
Horse market closed. The horses do not mind. The traders mind. I sell nothing and my horses get fat. Some will call this a good year.
Watched Desert Sun's Rebellion for the 41st time in the kitchen. It is still too long. Olddog was right. It is still true.

Kids back to the yard, masks in pockets not on faces. Buckwheat price is down a little. Charter flights still stopped, my brother is in Almaty and cannot come. But we are fine. Thank you everyone for the company these months.

Things are opening. I'll leave this thread open for anyone who needs it. Thanks for keeping it clean. Not one invented number in three months. FREECHAT has never been this well behaved and probably never will be again.
Challenge accepted

threads.title: Heating season: when do the radiators come on?

posts.body: Nurzhan people: radiators in your building warm already? Our block is cold like a fridge, the kids sleep in hats. Dispatcher says "when the city decides". The city decides what?
Dastgoh: warm since yesterday. Navbahor is on the other line from the 1998 plant. You are always two days behind us. Sorry. It is the pipes, not you.
Mine came on but only in the kitchen. The bedroom radiator is a decoration since 2013. The Herald wrote about the heating mains in 2013. Seven years later my radiator is still in the article.
Talas, Bazar-i Kalan side: warm, but only between 6 and 9 in the morning and evening. Like a train schedule. If you miss the heat you wait for the next one.
WARM. 19:00 today the pipe started to knock like somebody inside it wants to come out. Kids took off hats. Thank you for listening to me complain.
Two years later, same question. Still cold in Navbahor. Did the city decide yet? Gas price for the boiler plant went up, the dispatcher says, "because of the world".
Because of the world. We pump gas out of the ground across the road and the price is because of the world. Some things will never be explained to me.
In Surgut the radiators are so hot you open the window at minus thirty. If you want, I bring one home in my bag.
talas dorm 4: radiators on since monday but the windows are from the ussr so the heat goes directly to the street. we are heating the city for free. you're welcome talas
Tash-Kömür school: we bring our own heaters, and in March the head teacher sends a letter thanking us for our "initiative". Initiative is spelled correctly in the letter, at least.
Third year in this thread. This year warm on time! 11 October! I want to thank someone but I don't know who. Maybe the pipe.
In Chatkal the radiator is called a horse. You put a horse in the yurt doorway, the wind stays out. Thank the horse.
Dear thread. 2025: cold until 28 October because of "repairs on the main". I am now an expert. I can tell from the knocking which district gets heat next.
dorm 7 has heat but no hot water. dorm 4 has hot water but no heat. we take turns visiting each other. it is called a community
2026: on time again. 10 October. Two years of good luck, I am now suspicious. Somebody please tell me what they want from us.

threads.title: Is the 14 bus still running to the Old City?

posts.body: route 14, Semiz to the Old City. waited 40 min this morning at the water tower stop. is it cancelled or just Monday?
Saw a 14 going the other way full of tortillas. I mean full of people holding tortillas. It exists.
that was my cousin's tortillería delivery. he takes the bus because the van is "in the shop" since 2017. ok, the 14 lives. ¡gracias!

threads.title: Internet gone all day?? (March 2021)

posts.body: Is it only me? Talas, no foreign websites since 10ish. Local sites work. Card terminal at the coffee place said "connection error" and the barista made me pay in coins like it is 1997.
Nurzhan same. I can post here only because the site is on a mirror our admins set up for days like this. Everything abroad is gone. Calls and SMS fine.
my portal works!!! first time ever my portal works and the rest of the internet is broken. this is my best day
NO SIGN THIS IS A BLOCK. IT LOOKS LIKE A CABLE. STAY CALM, DO NOT SPREAD STORIES. IF THIS CHANGES WE WILL SAY SO.

Back. Nine hours. Uncle in Almaty says a digger cut a cable on a building site in Kazakhstan. One man with a backhoe disconnected a whole country. Ak_Shumkar would have called it an operation. I call it a Tuesday.
In Chatkal we did not notice.

Herald today: all our international traffic goes through two cables into Kazakhstan and one into Uzbekistan, and the switch to the others "did not work as intended". So there was a backup and the backup was also a drawing of water.

threads.title: Heatwave: where to buy a fan in Nurzhan

posts.body: Every shop in Navbahor sold out of fans. Navbahor Pond closed for swimming, the water is green, the children sit on the shore and look at it. Where can I buy a fan in Nurzhan? Any size. A fan from a museum is ok.

Dastgoh hardware market had three this morning at double price. Probably gone. The pond: Herald says it is the dry summer and low water from the Chu. The children are not wrong, it does look like soup.
My grandfather's fan from 1978, Soviet, metal blades, sounds like a helicopter. I will lend it. Do not put fingers inside. Do not put children near it. Do not put anything near it.
Ruslan's helicopter is in my kitchen. Kids are calling it "Neftchi" because it is loud and nobody can stop it. Thank you. You are not THAT Ruslan, you are a good Ruslan.
Putting that in my title

threads.title: Talas North Terminal: anyone work there?

posts.body: Hello forum, I read long time, now I register. I drive taxi at night in Talas, and three times this month I drove truck drivers from the city to the North Terminal at the Kazakh side. They say queue of trucks 6 km. Some trucks wait 3 days, some trucks go in one hour. Same papers, they say. Anybody here works there and can explain how a queue works in our country?

The Herald did a piece in May about independent hauliers saying the border queues "are not the same for everyone". That is the most carefully worded sentence in the history of Iradi journalism. Lawyers like me read it three times and admired it.
A queue in our country works like this. There is a line. Next to the line there is another line you cannot see.
Today one driver gave me a tip in tenge, one in som and one in a bag of apples from Shymkent. Terminal economy. Apples were good.
For balance, our side is also not famous for fast queues. A Kyrgyz driver told me once the only fast crossing in Central Asia is the one with nobody on it.

My brother drove reefers through there for SuKarne beef. He says the trick is not the papers, it is knowing whose cousin is on shift. He stopped driving. Now he lays tiles near Moscow with me. Tiles have no cousins.
Update: queue now 9 km sometimes. They built a new café at the terminal gate, very expensive tea. Somebody makes money from the queue at least.
Did you see the news? 46 tonnes of stibnite seized at the North Terminal, declared as fluorite. Antimony ore going out as a different rock. 46 tonnes. Who mixes up two rocks forty-six times?
I drove the inspector? Maybe. Some man in a good jacket last week, terminal at 4 am, very quiet, big tip. I don't know who he was. I know nothing. Cash also accepted.
A horse knows the difference between oats and stones. A customs officer is taught to forget.
Careful with guesses about who you drove, taxi. No details of people, here or anywhere. You know the rule.
Understood boss. Man had jacket. That is all. Many men have jacket.

threads.title: Fallen Rider / Día de Muertos in Semiz: anyone going?

posts.body: 1 and 2 November in Semiz. ofrendas in the houses, marigolds on the cemetery (we grow them from Mexican seed, people call them "Mexican flowers"), and in the evening the procession with the riderless horse with the saddle turned backwards. Since 2008 we do it, for the 2007 dead first, now for everybody. Iradi neighbours bring white ribbons and milk. Anyone from the forum who wants to come: come. Don't take photos of faces. Do take tamales.

My grandmother is in the Korean section of the Semiz cemetery. We go anyway on the 2nd. Every year the Mexican neighbours of the graves put a marigold on hers too. She would have complained it is too orange and then kept it.

For anyone confused: All Souls' is 2 November in the Syro-Iradi calendar too, so the two simply ran into each other in that cemetery and nobody saw a reason to stop them. The Synod has better things to argue about. The horse with the reversed saddle is older than all of us, by the way. It was ours before it was Semiz's.

This is very beautiful. In Chicago the Iradi families in Pilsen have started going to the Mexican neighbours' ofrendas and bringing kümöch. Nobody planned it. Lena, please put a marigold from me also.
it was full this year. the horse was calm, the trumpets were not. somebody's abuela fed me three times. I have no complaints in this life
Done, Temir. Orange from you, white ribbon from me.
went for the first time with two friends from tsu. the riderless horse walked past us and everyone just stopped talking. even the trumpets. then they started again louder. i get it now
¡bienvenida! next year bring your friends again and your appetite

threads.title: Rent in Talas is insane (post what you pay)

posts.body:
Landlord raised the rent for my one-room near Bazar-i Kalan from 900 to 1,100 som. And now he wants it in dollars. "220 dollar, it is easier". Easier for who? My salary is in som. The som is pegged. If it is the same money why does he care?

Post what you pay. No addresses please, just district and rooms.
He cares because the peg is a promise and dollars are a fact. Also: residential leases are supposed to be in som. I can tell you the section. I can't tell you a single person who enforced it.
Old City, two rooms, courtyard house, 1,000 som. No hot water after 10 pm and the neighbour's rooster has opinions. But the landlord is my mother's cousin, so the rent is in som and in guilt.
I pay 700 for a room in the panel blocks on the east side with my brother. Two men, one room, two shifts. One sleeps day, one sleeps night. Very efficient. Like hotel but no breakfast.

When I lived in Alatau Heights (1997 to 2007) we paid 400 dollars for a whole house and everyone said it was robbery. My cousin says the same house is now 1,500. I am not complaining, only reporting. Perhaps someone could make a table. Erbol?
rent table coming soon (with bread table)
Toronto: I will not say. You will cry. You will all stay in Talas.
Nurzhan is cheaper, everybody knows. Three rooms Navbahor, 750 som, but the heating is late every year. You pay less, you wait more.

Hello, new here. Small commercial room near TSU for a coffee place: they asked 2,400 som and "one month to the agent" and "one month to make sure". I asked make sure of what. He said "of you". I signed anyway. Wish me luck.
Welcome. Good luck. Make sure of you.

students: dorm is 60 som a month and you get what you pay for. the room-share flats near tsu went from 300 to 450 per bed since october. the landlords say it is "demand". the demand is that we are tired of dorm 4
Lurker from Ohio. 1,100 som is $220?? For a one-bedroom in a capital city? I'm sorry but my parking spot costs more than that. Please don't hate me.
We don't hate you. But my salary is also not Ohio.

News from my passengers: since the American remarks some returnee families in Alatau Heights are selling and going. Two houses on one street with signs. One agent told me rents there are dropping "because nobody wants to look American". First time I hear something get cheaper in Talas.
This makes me sad. Alatau Heights was full of people who came back to build something. I hope they stay. Amerikanka was never America. It was Iradis who had been away.
New lease. 1,300 som. In som! I won! He asked for 1,350. I won 50 som and a peg. Small victories, Talas.
bed in a 4-person flat near tsu: 520 som now. dorm 7 still 60. i will die in dorm 7

For the record: first landlord I've heard of asking for rent in Tulparcoin. The client's tenant wisely refused. Rent in a coin that is blocked, that a court may or may not call a financial service on 16 November. I did not know my profession could get more interesting. I was wrong.
Dollars, som, now coin. Next year he will want it in horses.
I have horses. Tell me the district.

threads.title: Korean New Year at the cultural centre (Talas)

posts.body: Tuesday is Seollal, Korean New Year. The Korean cultural association does a concert and tables on Sunday. Karakush's Dana Pak's old dance teacher runs the children's group so there is fan screaming from the back rows every year. Food: kuksi, pigodi, my aunt's laghman (she is making 30 litres, she says this is "a small amount"), rice cakes. Everyone welcome. Bow to the old people. Do not ask them about 1937 unless they start.
wait. dana pak's dance teacher? i am taking the bus from bishkek. this is not a joke. i will be in the back row screaming
can I bring tamales or is that too much crossover
Bring them. Last year someone brought beshbarmak. My grandmother would say any food that comes with a person is good food.

i went. kids did the ak börü dance in hanbok with little wolf capes. an old man next to me said in russian "in my time we danced to kalinka" and then clapped the hardest of anyone. ate four plates. lena's aunt is a hero
She says the boy from Bishkek ate like a Talas boy and she is proud.

Bumping for this year: Tuesday 17th. Same place, same aunt, 35 litres now. She says prices went up so she made more, because "if it is expensive, it should be also enough". No Tulparcoin at the tables, she asked me to write that.
In Bishkek the Koryo-saram association did theirs in a sports hall. Same kuksi, smaller aunt. Happy New Year to all.
went with my roommate whose grandmother is from the 1937 families. she made me bow to six old people. one of them taught me to say thank you in korean and then corrected my iradi. both fair

threads.title: New cafés in Talas: post your find

posts.body:
Hi. I opened a small coffee place near TSU, "Tündük" (yes like the yurt crown, the round hole you look at the sky through). Eight chairs. Espresso machine bought from a hotel that closed during the virus. No name of the street, rules. If you find it you find it.

This thread is for all new places though, not for advertising me. Post your finds.
Finally a username I respect. I will come. Is there kymyz coffee? Don't answer. I want to discover it.
kymyz_and_coffee came today. Asked for kymyz in the coffee. We tried. I will not try again. He was very brave.
It was a historic experiment. History is not always delicious.

Old City: a new café in a courtyard house, carved walnut porch, very pretty, very expensive, 6 som for a tea. Tea! The Herald last week wrote about concrete in the kucheh. This place is not concrete, but I think it pays for concrete somewhere.

During the Diz festival every teahouse in the citadel quarter stays open until 2. Not new, but if you have never sat on a carpet at 1 am after a Kyrgyz documentary with a pot of green tea, you have not lived in Talas.
new taco place NOT in Semiz, in the city centre, the sign just says TACOS!! I went to spy. corn tortillas from my cousin. so actually it is Semiz. we are colonising downtown, one taco at a time

Sorry for off topic: last two weeks we gave free coffee to couriers and students coming back from the square. During the three days with no data the card machine was dead, so I wrote IOUs on napkins. 140 napkins. 131 people came back and paid. Nine I hope are just lazy and not anything else. I keep the napkins.
131 out of 140. That is a better result than the election will have. Keep the napkins, they are history.
i am napkin number 37. i paid on tuesday. tündük is the best place in talas and i won't hear otherwise
Is the teahouse from the True Detective song a real place people can visit? Asking for me. I want to visit. I'm saving up.
It is real and it is now so full of foreigners with phones that the old men who played dominoes there moved two doors down. Go to the dominoes place. Better tea, nobody films you.
New thing: Jasil latte. Tarragon syrup and milk. It is green. Half the students love it, half say it is a crime. Exactly what I wanted.
had the jasil latte. it is a crime. i had two
Nurzhan has new places too, Talas people forget we exist. Former boiler room under a block in Dastgoh is now a café with mor-wave on vinyl. Nurzhan_Nights was there crying into his tea.
I was not crying. It was steam. It was a boiler room, there is steam. Ok I was crying. We played there in 2001. Now it is oat milk.

Somebody came today with a phone and a sticker and asked if we "accept TLPR". I asked what happens to the coffee if the court says no in November. He did not have an answer. He paid in som. Tündük position: som, cash, card, napkin. Not coin.
Napkin is the most stable currency in Irad. Proven in 2023.

threads.title: Checkpoint on the Nurzhan road again?

posts.body: Driving Talas to Nurzhan tomorrow with the kids. Anyone know if there is a new checkpoint near the Chu turn? My friend says 2 hours yesterday. Something with the Kurultai up in the mountains?

Came back today, 40 minutes. They look at trunks, they ask where you go, they don't ask anything else. Bring water and patience. The Kurultai is very far from the Chu road, but the Gendarmerie likes to feel included.
Made it. 50 minutes. The officer told my son to do his homework. My son says this is the worst checkpoint in the world.

threads.title: After October: what it's like on the street now

posts.body:
The live thread is for what happened. This one is for after. What do you see in your street, shop, bus, class, now that data is back?

Bazar-i Kalan: half the stalls now have handwritten signs "CASH ALSO ACCEPTED". After three days with dead card machines nobody trusts the terminal. My aunt has a new sign: "CASH. TEA FREE FOR COURIERS. NO POLITICS AT THE COUNTER."

Taxi side. During the three days the app was dead, so drivers went back to the old way: stand at the corner, shout the district. Old drivers were happy, young drivers did not know the city without the map on the phone. One boy drove me as a passenger to show him the way to the Old City. I paid nothing. He paid me in cigarettes. I don't smoke. I sold them.
I bought a paper map of Talas at a kiosk on Friday. The kiosk man said I was the third today. He has not sold a map since 2011. He looked moved.

tsu: police at the main gate all week, two cars. they don't do anything, they sit and eat sunflower seeds. we walk past. it's like a staring contest that nobody can win. lectures normal. half the class is quiet. two from my group are still on the guild's list

From Nurzhan it is all strange. We had no cut, we watched Talas go dark on the news and on this forum. My eldest wants to go to TSU next year. Now I don't know. Then I think: they also sang the anthem. Children who sing the anthem are not dangerous. Maybe I am naive.
You are not naive. Send him.
My sister says there is a rumour in her building that there will be a curfew from 22:00 in the centre. Is this true? I have told her to be home early anyway. Please, nobody take risks to answer.

I have heard the curfew thing every day since the 15th, from a different person each day, with a different hour each day. 21:00, 22:00, 23:00. Nothing official. Nobody stops anybody. Tell your sister to be home early because it is cold, not because of the curfew.
There is no curfew order published anywhere. For a curfew they need a decree, and a decree has a number. A rumour does not have a number. If anyone sees a number, post it here and I'll read it.
There is no curfew. Everything is normal. Please, those who were on the square, which faculty are you from? Only so I can send best wishes.
lol no
She said no. I also say no. You know where the probation button is, and so do I.

Night in the centre is very quiet now. Gendarmerie van at Central Square every night, engine on, nobody inside looks at anything. I pass four times a night. They know my car now. One night one of them waved. I waved back. We are now friends who don't talk.
Our office installed a "backup internet". It is a fixed line in the meeting room and a sign-up sheet. Thirty people, one cable. The boss is very proud. This is how the economy adapts.

Día de Muertos procession on the 1st. this year more people than ever from the city. a lot of young people with tsu scarves. they put candles for nobody in particular. the horse walked, nobody said anything. it was a good night, a sad good night

levy suspended (posted in the other thread). on the street today couriers honking at every corner. one courier rode past tsu with a speaker playing tüntolk. the police at the gate pretended not to hear. i think they also liked it
Election day passed. Nobody talked about it in my car. Not one passenger. Everyone talked about bread, rent and football. 92 and something percent. My passengers are 0 percent interested.
Two months. The "cash also accepted" signs are still up. My aunt says she will never take hers down. She says a sign is cheaper than trust.
Police car at the tsu gate gone since New Year. Students noticed in one minute. The sunflower seed shells are still there. Somebody made a little sign: "they were here".

threads.title: TSU thread: dorms, exams, canteen

posts.body: thread for talas state university people. dorms, exams, which lecturer is a dinosaur, where the canteen hides the good samsa. no names of teachers or students please (rules). 1st year sociology here, dorm 4, radiators work 50%
Talas Pedagogical Institute, class of 1994. Our canteen had one dish, called "dish". Good luck with your exams, my dear. Use commas.
canteen today: plov 3 som, laghman 3.50 (lena don't look), tea 0.50. the plov is iradi plov, sticky, it is good. the laghman is a crime against koryo-saram
I looked. Come to the bazaar. Students with a TSU card get half price from my aunt. She just decided this now when I told her.

exam week, power cut in the dorms, we studied by phone light (said it in the power cut thread). today the sociology exam was in the warm building. the lecturer gave everyone extra 5 minutes "for the electricity". respect
end of year. azat tribuna had a picnic by the river with a speaker and a flag. no police. it felt like the old times that i never lived in
new year at tsu. first years everywhere, they look 12. one asked me where the october plaque is. there is no plaque. i showed him the bench where we sat. the bench is the plaque
hello. first year applied maths. found this forum because zhayloo_girl showed it to our group at the welcome evening. dorm 7: the shower has two settings, ice and lava. the wifi has one setting, no
welcome!!! dorm 7 is legendary. the lava setting is a rite of passage
Welcome. Read the rules. Don't post anything that identifies your group or your teachers. Enjoy the lava.

first exams in december and the maths lecturer says "irad is a function with no defined domain" and then laughed alone for 30 seconds. the whole hall was silent. he is either a genius or he read this forum
he read the forum. everyone reads the forum
A function with no defined domain. I'm stealing that for The Erasure board.

lectures half empty this week. everyone was making signs. the american exchange student in our dorm (yes, there is one, from Michigan) asked us if he should go home. we said no, come to the march, carry the sign, it says irad is not for sale, not americans go home. he came. people shook his hand.
that is so tsu. see the other thread for the street stuff
survived 2nd year. 2.20 bread, 3.50 plov now, laghman unchanged and still criminal. lena's aunt half price still. tsu card best card in irad
exam season. dorm 7 has hot water this year!!! dorm 4 does not!!! the wheel turns

our institute's survey came out. 61% find the official information on the governor's health insufficient, it was 58% last year. our professor read it aloud in the lecture and then said "the remaining 39% were not asked very loudly". we laughed. she didn't
39% is a very strong result for the Governor's health. Have a nice day. Remember to vote.
the governor's health did not vote
final year next year. thesis topic: "cash also accepted: trust and payment in talas after october 2023". lena's aunt is my main source. she wants to be credited as "aunt"
She wants it on the first page. "Aunt." Big letters.

half my floor registered for the coin on day one for the free 100. the dorm wifi blocked the site on day 3 (before attelkom). we have the most advanced dorm wifi in irad. it blocks everything, including things that should be blocked

last first-week of october for me at tsu. three years since the square. tea at the bazaar yesterday, my aunt-of-reference gave every courier free tea as always. i put my old shoe on the bench. joke. the shoe is gone. the bench is still the plaque

threads.title: Feast of St. Janyl: getting there, sleeping there

posts.body: Practical thread for the feast on the 24th. Iyık Janyl is 235 km from Talas by road, and every bed in the city is booked by now, I promise you. Church hostels are full since June. Options: buses from Talas leave from the big station the day before (go early), or a tent below the city where the horse races are. Bring a jacket, it is 1,280 m and the nights are cold even in August. Bring respect: no flags, no slogans, no weapons inside the cathedral precinct. That agreement is older than this forum.

Thank you, seminarian. I don't post much these days. Add this: the riders from the tribal side come up in long columns on the morning of the feast. Don't stand on the road to take photos. Horses don't know about phones.
Chatkal riders are going. My cousin takes two horses to be blessed. The water is cold. The horses do not complain. The cousin does.

I have not been to the feast since 2006. My mother took me in 1972, I remember the juniper smoke and a priest on a horse. If anyone goes, please light a candle for my mother. And please, after the feast the Simpsons episode is on IradOne that week. Watch it. It was the song.
Temir, every year. Every year you find a way.
Semiz bus going on the 23rd from St. Yusup, 40 people. the padre says Guadalupe and Janyl are friends. we bring tortillas for the pilgrims, it is now tradition (since last year)

Back. Archbishopric says over 150,000. I believe it; I stood on the esplanade for four hours and could not move my elbows. Priests on horses blessing sheep with glacier water, kümöch at the liturgy, the juniper smoke so thick you could lean on it. Riders from both sides of the line, unarmed, with UN observers at the crossings. On this one day the country looks like what it could be. Then everyone goes home.
I lit the candle for your mother, Temir. Memory eternal.
Thank you, my friend. I had to stop typing for a while.
300 tortillas gone in one hour. a rider from the mountains ate six and said "Mexican kümöch". i will put it on the menu
Watched the IradOne live broadcast frame by frame for any sign of the Governor in the VIP area. Nothing. Not even a cardboard one. Noted in the other thread.
Respectfully: at the feast people were looking at the saint, not the VIP area. Take that to Leaks & Rumours with a label.

Bumping a year later. I went this time with my Christian neighbours from Arslanbob, as a guest. A priest blessed my neighbour's horse and then, seeing me, blessed my walnut bag too, to be safe. I have never had blessed walnuts. They taste the same. I liked it anyway.
Blessed walnuts are an ancient Fergana tradition starting from yesterday. Welcome, guest.

threads.title: Is it OK to speak English on the street right now? (Feb 2025)

posts.body: Honest question, not trolling. I was planning to visit Talas in April (the teahouse, the Hippodrome, the dominoes place kino told me about). After the remarks this week, is it OK to be an American walking around speaking English? I'm embarrassed to even ask. I didn't vote for anyone who wants to sell anybody.
Talas speaks English in half the offices. Nobody hits a man for asking for coffee. But maybe right now don't wear the flag t-shirt. And maybe wait to see what the weekend looks like.
Canadian passport, Iradi face. People in Toronto keep asking me if I'm "for sale". I am not even for rent.
Last night three passengers talked only about this. One said he will never speak English again. Then he asked me in English "how much". Old habits.

From the street today. The march went past the old High Commissioner's residence, thousands, students, factory people, old men with medals, Semiz families with Mexican and Iradi flags on the same pole. Some people burned flags in front of the residence, American and Russian, both. Police stood along the route and did nothing, which in Talas is news. My aunt closed the stall and walked. She says "I don't support Ilyasov, I don't support Trump, I support that nobody sells my stall."

we sang all three stanzas at the residence. ALL THREE. the third one that nobody knows. the old people knew it. we read it from phones. a babushka next to me corrected my pronunciation of every second word and then cried

Tonight I drove two American contractors to the airport. They sat in the back very small and said nothing. At the end one said in bad Russian "izvinite" (sorry). I said in English: not your fault, have a good flight. He gave me 20 dollars. I don't know if for the ride or for the sentence.

I read every post here three times. The Iradi American Association in Chicago has written a statement against the remarks, and we have sent it to the newspapers here, which probably will not print it. Please, if anybody in Talas hears people say Iradi Americans are traitors, tell them: we were the ones who kept the language on Devon Avenue. TD_fan_Ohio, you are welcome at our picnic in August. I will give you a feedback form.
I'll fill it out. I'll fill out ten.

today Semiz walked to the city. 9 km on foot along the highway, families, strollers, the old feedlot guys. Mexican and Iradi flags tied together. a truck driver gave us water. at the end somebody on a loudspeaker said "we came when it was American, we stayed when it wasn't, nobody asked us either time". that is exactly it

also: this week some of us got shouted at in the city because people think Mexicans = Americans. one lady from the parish was spat at on a marshrutka. community leaders say: in the centre, speak Spanish or Iradi, not English. so if you hear Spanish in Talas this week, it is us being careful. smile at us
Anyone who spits at a Semiz grandmother on a marshrutka can come to my aunt's stall and explain himself. She has a ladle and she is not afraid of it.

Nurzhan marched today too, smaller, mostly Russian on the placards, same words. Some politicians at the front were using it for the base question. The people behind them were just angry. Two different marches walking in the same street.

Office news: our American-educated manager (born in Talas, LA degree, came back in 2010) got "so whose side are you on" from a client yesterday. She answered in perfect Iradi, all three stanzas of the anthem. Client apologised. I have never respected a manager more.

Herald says the big hotels on the avenue lost all American bookings for March and April, even church groups for the Janyl pilgrimage. My café lost one regular, a guy from the energy company who was told to fly home "temporarily". He left a tip jar donation of 50 dollars and a note: "save my seat". I saved it.
Update: I'm postponing to autumn. Not because I'm scared of anyone here. Because you're all busy with something more important than my vacation. But I'm coming. Save me a seat at the dominoes place.
Seat saved. Bring patience, the dominoes old men talk only about 1979.

I CAME. I'm in Talas. Week three. Nobody spat at me. A grandmother at the bazaar gave me free tea when she heard I was "from the forum". The dominoes men taught me to lose. Best trip of my life. That's all, back to lurking.
That was my aunt. She says the American boy was polite and finished the bowl. Highest honour.

threads.title: anyone else's water off in the Old City?

posts.body: No water since 5 am, Old City side. Water authority phone just plays music. Same music as in 2019.
Same. 40 percent of the water is lost in the pipes, the Herald said years ago. Today it is 100 percent.
Back. Brown for ten minutes then normal. The music is still playing on the phone line. Maybe forever.

threads.title: Tulparcoin at the bazaar: who is actually taking it?

posts.body: This is not the megathread, this is the street. In four days I have seen at Bazar-i Kalan: three stalls with a printed sticker "TLPR here", one boy trying to pay for a melon with his phone (melon man said "show me the melon in your phone"), and an argument at the bread counter that lasted longer than the bread. Post what you see in shops. NO phone numbers, NO wallet codes, NO screenshots of anybody's account.

Two passengers this week asked to pay in coin. I said cash also accepted, cash especially accepted, coin not accepted. One showed me he has "104 coins = 6 dollars". I asked: so give me 6 dollars. He said he cannot, it is in the coin. So he has 6 dollars that are not dollars. He paid in som. Everyone pays in som in the end.

Talasbank stopped card payments to the coin thing this week. Colleague tried to top up with his Talasbank card, "transaction declined". He thought his salary was gone. His salary is fine. His dream of becoming Ilyasov is declined.

Correct, and both things are true at once: the Bank of Irad said on the 24th it is not legal tender and also that it has no power to ban it. So a shopkeeper can take it if he likes, and nobody has to. If your melon man refuses, he is within his rights. If he accepts, he is also within his rights, and his own risk.
Not shilling (I know, I know, the new rule). Just saying the kebab place by the Hippodrome takes it and nobody died. That's all. Peaceful exchange between consenting adults.
Coin shilling is against the rules since the 24th. One more "just saying" and it's probation. No names of shops either, from anyone. This thread is about what people see, not where to spend it.
Understood.

The kebab place by the Hippodrome took it on Saturday and stopped on Monday. The owner told me the coin went down while the kebab was still on the grill. He lost money on a single kebab. Akyel or nothing, and som or nothing.
Nurzhan: one shop on our street has a sticker, crossed out with a marker by Tuesday. Bakery joke I posted in the bread thread: pay in coin if the coin rises in the oven. It did not rise.

My husband registered for the 100 free coins. I asked with what. He said with his phone number. I made him sit on the sofa for a long talk. The kids watched. Now the kids are asking me if the government knows our phone. I said the government has always known our phone, now Jason also knows.
Students keep showing me the coin app like a pass. "I have 100!" 100 of what. Tündük: still som, cash, card, napkin. Napkin rate stable since 2023.
site and exchange both dead since this morning on attelkom. the boys on my floor are refreshing the app. it shows a spinning tulpar. the tulpar spins. it doesn't fly
After the block, nobody asked me to pay in coin. Not one. Three days ago it was the future. Today it is a spinning horse.
As the Bank of Irad wisely said on 24 September, it is not legal tender. Citizens should use the som. Have a nice day.
Strange to agree with him. It happens to every horse once. Then you check its teeth.

Court today: no injunction, adjourned to 16 November. At the bazaar: the TLPR stickers are mostly gone. One stall left. He says he keeps it "until November, for the court". My aunt says she keeps hers too. Hers says "CASH ALSO ACCEPTED", since 2023. Some signs last.
the free tea for couriers happened again yesterday at the stall, three years. no one tried to pay for the tea in coin. tea is free. free is the only thing that's not a trap
Forum moves to the new software today. This thread comes with it. Nobody knows what happens in November. Keep posting what you see, not what you guess.

threads.title: power off again Dastgoh (just me?)

posts.body: Lights went at 9 in Dastgoh. Just my block or everybody?
Everybody. Go to sleep, Dima.

threads.title: Kara-Oi talks: anyone hear what happened in the hall?

posts.body:
IradOne at 9: "the tribal delegation LEFT THE TALKS at Kara-Oi". That is ALL they said. Twelve seconds and then the weather!!!

SOMETHING HAPPENED IN THAT HALL. Anyone with family up there? Anyone??? WAKE UP IRAD
I drove past Kara-Oi at 6 in the evening. Many horses tied at the UN fence, many jeeps. At 7 the horses gone. Nu, that is my report. I am truck driver, not journalist. I carry flour.

Registered to answer this. My mother's people are up the Besh-Tash and my uncle was outside the hall holding horses.

What he says: the DPI offered one third of the seats. One third. For two thirds of the land and, if you ask anyone who has counted sheep and children up there, more than half the people. And they wanted the mountain water catchments under the state.

After 2007, after the Bill of Sale, nobody in the mountains will sign a paper that puts the water in a drawer in Talas.
Welcome, besh_tash_vet. A reminder to everyone: talk about what was said in public. No names of anyone's relatives, holding horses or not. Read the rules.
ONE THIRD!!! They counted the mountains like they count votes. Same calculator. Watch, in November the same calculator will give the Governor 88 or 89 percent. Screenshot this.

Herald has the quote now. Bektur, walking out: "The mountains were given by God to the horses and the herds, not to the stock exchanges of Talas."

I am from the Old City and I have never sat on a horse and even I want to ride somewhere now. WAKE UP IRAD
THE TALAS HERALD REPORTS THE IAC DELEGATION WALKED OUT AFTER AN OFFER OF ONE THIRD OF THE SEATS. THE DPI SAYS ITS PROPOSALS "REMAIN ON THE TABLE". A TABLE IS ALSO WHERE YOU LEAVE THINGS TO GO COLD.
I added a section "Kara-Oi talks" to the Irad Internet Portal!! right now it is empty because I dont know how to put the Herald article in a frame. sorry if broken
In the chaikhana at the crossing the drivers say the talks will start again by Nooruz next year. Drivers are optimists. We have to be, look at the roads.

For the city people asking me (my classmates at the Veterinary Center are all from Talas and they ask every day): the clans do not hate one Irad. My grandfather wants one Irad. He also remembers that in February 2007 a government in Talas tried to sell the mountains to three neighbours, with the sheep still on them.

You do not hand the second government the same pen.

[quote=besh_tash_vet]You do not hand the second government the same pen.[/quote]
Signature material. Can I steal it? I will credit "a vet".
Credit the grandfather.

Bumping because it is ten years today, by the Herald's date. Ten years and no second table.

My father says the DPI proposals are still on the table, like they said. He says by now they are fossils and a university should come and dig them up.
Ten years. Ask anyone at the refinery about Kara-Oi and they will think you mean the UN canteen. That is maybe the whole problem in one sentence.
Ten years ago I said talks again by Nooruz. I am still sitting at the chaikhana. The tea is good at least.

threads.title: Valley people: say hello (no clan names needed)

posts.body:
Most of this board is city people talking about the valleys. Let the valleys talk for once.

Say roughly where you post from and what you do. No clan names needed, no village names if you don't want. I start: vet student in Talas, family up the Besh-Tash, home every summer to vaccinate anything that moves.
Truck driver. Talas, Kara-Oi, the passes and back. Russo by my mother, Iradi by kymyz. I carry flour.
Old City Talas but my grandmother was from the Chatkal side so I COUNT. WAKE UP IRAD
Hello. I sit in a cold stream all summer and find nothing. If anyone asks, I find nothing.
Same as me with the flour. Welcome, bratan.
My niece set this up for me. I make felt in a workshop in the Talas Alatau. Eleven women, one stove. We sell shyrdaks in Talas. I will read slowly and write slowly.
Welcome. Slow writers are the best writers on this board. Read the rules, there is no hurry.

Northern steppe. Cattle. Yes, THAT clan, the cattle one, laugh now and get it over with.

The mountain people on this board talk about horses like poets. I will talk about cattle like a bank. Somebody has to.
Welcome. I have vaccinated your cattle. They also talk like a bank.
Chatkal. Horses. Buy and sell. That is all.
Found this thread late. Herder, Chatkal Highlands. My long hello is in the generator thread. Here is the short one: hello.
Arslanbob, the walnut forest, Fergana Rim. Muslim, if anyone wonders. Iradi, if anyone wonders. Both at once. My family has been doing both at once for a long time.
Welcome. Good walnuts.

threads.title: Gold up there? The mercury ban and who pans

posts.body:
Herald today: a clan council in the Chatkal BANNED MERCURY after fish died below a gold panning camp.

So there IS gold up there, and the DPI lets the clans keep it?? Who BUYS the gold?? FOLLOW THE GOLD. WAKE UP IRAD
Ak, the gold up there a man carries in a matchbox for a whole summer. Nobody gets rich. Except the matchbox.

Registered for this. I pan. Not saying which stream.

Whole summer, cold water to the knees, and in September a little paper fold with the dust. Mercury makes it faster, yes. It also kills the fish and the boy who heats the amalgam in the yurt. The elders were right.

I was at that meeting. Old men, a lot of shouting, then very quiet, then the ban. Pans and sluices only. Use mercury and you pay and you leave the valley.
WHO BUYS IT
A man. With scales. In a market. I will not say which market, Ak, because then you will go there and shout at him.
Vet note: we saw the dead fish photos at the Center. Two dogs downstream were sick that summer too. Nobody tested them properly, so I will not say it was the mercury. I will say: pans only, please.

My neighbour here in Chicago pans for gold in Wisconsin as a hobby. In nine years he has found about eleven dollars and he is very happy. I will tell him he has colleagues in the Chatkal.

(Ak, before you say it: no, he is not CIA. He is a retired dentist.)
A retired dentist. Who looks for GOLD. Think about it, Amerikanka.
Ak. Read the rules. The dentist stays out of it.
Season open. Water still too cold. Found zero grams, officer.

Bumping my old thread because nobody in my valley pans gold any more.

Now the boys dig in the old Soviet antimony holes for stibnite, by hand, and carry the stones down in feed sacks. China stopped selling antimony abroad and the price went crazy. A man with a bad back now earns more in a month than I did in five summers. ([HEARD], labelled: the buyers wait on the ISEZ side.)
Horses carry it too. Horses do not ask what is in the sack. I ask.

Please. The old workings are not safe. I am a vet and I have set two human arms this autumn because the nearest doctor was a day away. Shafts from the sixties, nobody has shored them since 1992. A stone is not worth a son.

On the steppe we laughed at you mountain people digging rocks. Then I heard the price a buyer offered my cousin's neighbour. Then I stopped laughing. Then I went back to cattle, because cattle walk to the market by themselves.
OneNews tonight: 46 tonnes of stibnite seized at Talas North Terminal, declared as fluorite. Somebody has very optimistic handwriting.
46 tonnes is a lot of feed sacks. That is not boys with bad backs. That is somebody with trucks. [RUMOUR] trucks with good papers. My guess only. I have no papers. I have a pan.
I carry flour.

The elders in our valley met about the digging. Not a ban, the old holes are not on our grazing, it is not ours to ban. A warning instead: if a man is hurt in the holes, his family pays for the days of the men who carry him down. Out loud, in front of everyone.

The digging slowed. Nobody wants to owe the whole valley.

threads.title: They poured concrete into the Kariz (17 shafts?)

posts.body:
OneNews: the Gendarmerie "secured" 17 shafts of the Kok-Tash Kariz this spring "against criminal transit". Concrete caps.

Same Kariz that Talas AND the clans protested about two years ago when UNESCO listed it as Kazakh and Kyrgyz, because it's ours. Now we pour concrete into it?

SEVENTEEN. Why seventeen? Because those are the ones THE CIA DUG OUT in the cold war. The rest are just old. I have said this since 2011. The DPI is closing them before somebody finds the BOXES. WAKE UP IRAD
Ak, the karez are a thousand years old. The Kara-Khanids did not have a CIA. The only secret service I know of down there is the priest who used to bless the water masters in spring.
THE KARA-KHANIDS DIDN'T NEED A CIA. THE AMERICANS DID. Read a book, seminarian. Oh wait, you QUIT.
Ak. You are on probation. Attack the argument, not the man's vocation. This is a friendly reminder and it is the last friendly one.
Water runs in those shafts. Under the concrete it still runs. In the villages below they will ask: who cleans it now. The water master cannot climb through concrete.

Two of the capped shafts are above villages where I work. The water masters were not asked. If the galleries silt up, the fields below go dry in three summers.

Smugglers will use another hole. Farmers do not have another hole.
For the record: a truck does not fit in a karez. Only flour fits in a truck. And I drive a truck.
[HEARD] cigarettes fit very well. Not mine. I don't smoke, I pan.
A herder from the next valley says one cap already cracked. Water is patient.

threads.title: Kurultai says no census counters on clan land

posts.body:
News reaching Toronto through my cousin: this year's Kurultai decided not to let the DPI's census enumerators into the clan territories next year.

Can someone in the valleys explain? From here it looks like refusing to be counted just gives Talas the excuse to undercount you.

I was in the outer camp, not in the ring, so this is what was said in the camps.

First: the enumerators would come with Gendarmerie escorts. A man with a clipboard and a man with a rifle is not a census.

Second: the form asks each household for its livestock. The elders say the city wants herd numbers today so it can tax herds tomorrow.

Third, and the old men say this one most: in 2007 a government in Talas wrote our land down on a paper and tried to sell it. Being written down by Talas is not a neutral thing for us.

Gulya is right that they will now print a smaller number. The elders say the Chancellery counts its own herds and its own people and the number is ours. Whether Talas will ever believe our number, I do not know.
They will count the horses from a helicopter. Horses do not lie. Helicopters estimate.

Legal footnote nobody asked for: the census regulation provides for "estimation" where enumeration is "not practicable". So the refusal doesn't stop the census. It hands the DPI the pen for the ATR number. Which, to be fair, the Shepherd seems to know already.
Meanwhile in Nurzhan they did a test run. The enumerator asked my grandmother where she was born. She said Kobozev. He wrote Nurzhan. She has not recovered.

One worry from the Kara-Buura side. Women and girls in the valleys are already invisible in the Talas statistics, and the TSU survey people cannot get in either. If nobody is counted, nobody is counted.

I respect the Kurultai. I also want my sisters to exist on paper somewhere.

[quote=white_headscarf]If nobody is counted, nobody is counted.[/quote]
That is fair, and I will say it to my uncles. The women in the camps keep their own count, by the way. Every birth, every bride, every grave. Older than any census. But it lives in their heads, not on paper, and heads get old.
Thank you both. Best explanation I've read, including the Herald.
Here is the number: 4,626,000. See the other thread. The helicopter was tired.
On the steppe the feedlot people counted our cattle from satellite photos in one week for the contracts. People, apparently, are harder to see from space.

threads.title: Quota roll at the Kurultai (steppe vs mountains, round 400)

posts.body:
[HEARD] from riders coming down from Aksay: the Kurultai will share out the crossing contracts by herd count. The mountain clans pushed it. Our biy did not lay the whip, so it passes.

I am not happy and I am not unhappy. I am thinking.

It is true, I was in the outer camp. For the city people: the contracts are the bulk diesel, grain and medicines that come across, settled in escrow at Talasbank. For years the steppe clans held most of them, because the northern crossings are on their side. Now each clan gets a share by the herds it reports to the Chancellery.

The Boztorgoy stood aside. That is not a defeat. It is a clan saying: we will not stop you, and you will not bind us on our own land. It is an honourable thing to do.
Correct, and thank you. Also: we report the most cattle. So we still get the biggest share. The mountain people forgot to do that arithmetic before they celebrated.
Horses are counted too. I counted mine twice.
So a central committee allocates trade by quota. This is Gosplan with yurts. Abolish the quotas, let the market decide, let the best trader win.
The best trader did win. For twelve years. That is why they made the quota. Come to the steppe, you would love us for a week, then you would hate us.

[quote=liberty_lad_88]let the market decide[/quote]
In the winter of 2016 the market decided whether my camp had diesel for the vaccine fridge. The market decided no. My neighbour's camp decided yes and sent a can over the ridge on a horse. That was not a market. That was a neighbour. The quota is an attempt to write the neighbour down.
Interesting to read from Bishkek. Nobody here understands this "standing aside". Is it a vote against or for?

Neither, that is the beauty of it. "I will not block you, and you will not bind me." My professor in Talas said it is like abstaining. My grandfather said it is like a horse that will not pull the cart but will not kick it either.
Herald has it now: "Kurultai Adopts Quota Roll as Steppe Clan Stands Aside." Bektur says the roll will "end arguments at the crossings before they start".
Arguments at the crossings will end when the crossings end. But fine. Less shouting at the chaikhana maybe.
Update after one season of the roll: my cousin's contract got smaller. The arguments at the crossing did end. Now the arguments are at home. Progress.
The ISEZ administration welcomes orderly trade by all communities. Out of interest, which crossings do the steppe clans use most? Have a nice day.
No.

threads.title: Shyrdak: buying direct from the felt cooperatives

posts.body:
Dear friends,

For the Iradi American Association picnic raffle this August I would like a real shyrdak, made by hand in the valleys, not a machine one from the factory. Is there a way to buy directly from the women's felt cooperatives and send it to Chicago? I will of course pay a fair price plus shipping, and I will send a short feedback form afterwards to everybody involved.

With respect,
Temir

Uncle Temir, yes. Our workshop is part of the Ak Kiyiz cooperative. Goods go down across the line with traders to Talas, and from Talas to the post.

A shyrdak 2 by 1.5 metres, two colours, ram's horn pattern, is about a month of work for two women. In Talas it sells for 450 som. Shipping I do not know, the post office knows.

Please no feedback form. My niece reads them to me and they are very long.
450 som for a month of two women's work. And a shop in Europe sells the same rug for, what, 400 euro? I'm not saying anything. I'm just doing arithmetic out loud.

Lena, you do arithmetic like our founder. She made us write the Talas price and the abroad price on the same blackboard, side by side. Now some rugs go straight to the fair-trade buyers, and the blackboard is less sad.
Ordered through a cousin in Talas. I will post a photograph of the rug only. No faces, no names, only the rug.

Report: the shyrdak arrived in July, crimson and white, ram's horns. It was won in the raffle by a lady who remembers Alatau Heights in the old days (no names) who cried and said it smelled like her mother's house. 31 of the returned feedback forms mentioned the rug. Thank you to the workshop.
Temir, how did you get it through customs? Toronto customs wanted to fumigate my aunt's felt boots.
I filled in a form. Of course.
Got a small felt saddle-cloth at Bazar-i Kalan for the counter of our taco stand. Customers ask if it's Mexican. I say sí, from the Iradi part of Mexico.

Winter is felt season. Our stove broke for a week and we rolled wool with cold hands. Cold hands make bad felt. A man from the workshop in the next valley came over the snow with a stove pipe tied to his horse.

That is how a cooperative works. Not the paper. The stove pipe.

The Herald came to the Kara-Suu workshops. "Felt across the line". Klara Zhumabek kyzy said a carpet sold in Talas buys flour, school shoes and diesel for the winter. True.

She also said the woman who made it knows what it earned. That part is newer. When I started, the men carried the carpet down and came back with the money and a story.
"Felt is also made one layer at a time." That line from the article is going on the Ak Jooluk office wall. With credit to the workshop.
my mum bought a shyrdak at a stall that said ak kiyiz. is it real or fake? the stall guy said "real as the mountains" which is not an answer

Turn it over. A real shyrdak: the two colours fit together like a puzzle, every stitch by hand, a little uneven. A machine one: perfect, and glued. If the stall man is shy about the back, he is not real as the mountains.
the back is uneven!!! mum says thank you and that she is never doubting a stall again (she will)

threads.title: Kymyz season thread

posts.body: Every year I complain about the bottled kymyz at Bazar-i Kalan. This year I'm making a thread instead. Where is the real kymyz, and when does it come down?
kyzyl-adyr has real kymyz. my aunt. not for sale. sorry

Tried kymyz for the first time. It's like if horchata went to the gym and got angry. And I liked it??
"If horchata went to the gym and got angry" is the best description in the history of this forum.

altyn muuz released a song called kymyz kymyz this year and i am contractually obliged to mention it in this thread. not linking it. you have suffered enough

threads.title: Jamgyr tilöö this summer? (rain rites)

posts.body:
The Synod has asked for prayers for rain this month. From the valleys I hear the old jamgyr tilöö is being done again in places that hadn't bothered for years. Anyone seen it?

For the record, the Church is fine with it as long as nobody kills anything. White ribbons, milk and kymyz on the stones, juniper smoke. My old professor called it "the Psalms with livestock".

Yes, at the spring above our camp, last Sunday. The grandmothers tied white ribbons on the old willow and poured kymyz on the stones. Juniper smoke. A priest came up with the travelling idta and said the rain prayer in Iradi. Then the children threw water at each other, which is the important part, according to the children.

Three days later it rained, on the next valley. The old women say it was aimed wrong.

In Arslanbob the men prayed the rain prayer in the mosque. And my grandmother walked up to the spring above the village and tied a white rag on the tree like she always does. The imam pretends not to see. Everyone's grandmother does it, Christian or Muslim. Grandmothers are their own religion.
Spelling note for the city people: tilöö, with the ö. It means "asking". Not "tiloo", which my students write every year and which means nothing at all.
The line at Maryam-Bulak on Sunday was two hours. My mother brought milk in a lemonade bottle. I am sure the Mother of God does not mind about the bottle.
Horses know rain before people. My mares turn their tails west the evening before. Cheaper than a priest.
Kenkol, please don't tell the Synod. They will want to ordain the mares.
Bump. Dry again, Synod prayers again. This year young men came to the spring too, phones in their pockets. One of them filmed. The grandmothers made him delete it. Rain is not for the internet.
"rain is not for the internet" ok that hit. also the grandmothers would be great a&r people

threads.title: Going to a toi in the valleys, help (city Russo edition)

posts.body:
My mate from the depot is marrying a girl from the Talas Alatau side. The toi is up there in October and her family got us the paper from the clan council.

I've been to Nurzhan weddings: banquet hall, vodka, somebody's uncle fights somebody's cousin in the car park, done. What do I need to know so I don't embarrass the entire city?
Do not ride in the kyz kuu.
why
You will lose. To a girl. In front of six hundred people. They will make a song about it.

Practical things. Gift in white or bright colours, never black, black is Morkhan's colour and the old ladies will notice even if they say nothing. No jokes about the kalym. Stand up when the bride arrives on the white horse. When the groom's mother puts the white elechek on her, that is the moment. Put your phone away for that.

Also. They will kill a sheep. It is for the food, not an offering, do not make a face. Do not mention horsemeat, not even as a joke. A guest was asked to leave a toi in my valley for that once. (He was from Talas.)

And you will see no cattle. They put the cattle out of sight for a wedding. If you see a cow, say nothing. It is somebody's mistake and he already knows.
And eat everything they put in front of you. Everything. Pace yourself, there is a third course you don't know about. Then a fourth.
Bring an appetite and a strong liver. At my cousin's toi in Kara-Buura I said "no más" and they thought it was a toast. Three more toasts.
Ruslan, do NOT tell them about the shoe and the tram wire.
that story is my best material
That is why.

Back. Report:

- The crowning was in a big white yurt, a priest, rings, a cup of wine, crowns of flowers. Very quiet. I was not ready for how quiet. My mate cried. I will deny this.
- I did not ride in the kyz kuu. I was asked. I said bad knee. An eight-year-old asked me which knee. I said the Nurzhan one.
- Lena was right about the fourth course. There was a fifth.
- Free-for-all ulak on the last day. I watched from behind a truck, which is where a city man belongs.
- The bride's grandmother asked if Nurzhan people still say Kobozev. I said some do. She said "good, names should be remembered". Kobozev_Kid, your grandmother has an ally in the mountains.
- Did not mention the shoe.
My grandmother will want her address. Proud of you about the shoe.
Thank you for the report. Only one question. Was the bride happy?
She asked ME if I was happy, then laughed at me. They met at a bus stop in Talas, two years of letters before anyone's family heard. She chose him. Everybody at the toi knew that story by heart.
Good. That's the only answer I wanted.
