threads.title: Honest question from Talas: why don't the valleys trust us?

posts.body:
Not trolling. I'm from Talas, office job, I have never been past the line.

Every time unification comes up, the valley people on this board say "never again with Talas". But we didn't sell anybody. Orozbekov did, and he's in Istanbul. Toktarov leaked it! Why does it feel like the valleys hold the city responsible?

Fair question. I'll try, as someone who lives on both sides.

1) In February 2007 a government in Talas, recognised by 26 countries, secretly wrote a paper giving the mountains to three neighbours. My grandfather heard it on the radio in a winter house. That is the first thing.

2) In June 2007 the clans rode into Talas with the Front and the city fell. By the end of that summer the cities belonged to the DPI and the clans were back behind a line. Many riders feel they did the work and the men in suits moved into the house.

3) Since then every offer from Talas has had "the water" somewhere in the small print. See Kara-Oi.

Nobody up there thinks you, kymyz, personally sold anything. But up there "Talas" means a building, not people.

EXACTLY. And the building is full of the SAME PEOPLE. The ones who drafted it in 2006 are still sitting in ministries. Only Orozbekov ran. The rest changed the pin on their jacket. THE VALLEYS ARE RIGHT. WAKE UP IRAD

If I may add a date for accuracy: the Bill of Sale was leaked on 25 February 2007. besh_tash_vet has it right. I would also say, with respect, that many Talas people marched against the sale that spring. "Irad satylbayt" was first chanted in Nurzhan, by city people.
Nobody gave a wrong date, Amerikanka. You correct dates nobody wrote. In 2007 you were in CHICAGO watching it on CNN with a hot dog.
Ak. The topic, not where people live. That is the second reminder this month.

In 1992 Talas was under siege. Bread came over the mountains on horses. Mamytov's riders brought it. I ate that bread.

The city forgot quickly. The mountains did not forget that we forgot.
olddog... I didn't know that. They didn't teach it like that at school. They taught us the Starlight landings.
They teach what was filmed.

My family is from Kara-Buura, ISEZ side, but half my cousins married across. At every toi there is one uncle who says the cities are traitors and one aunt who says the clans are bandits, and then they dance together. So: both.

My grandparents were sent here in 1937 in cattle wagons by men in a building. They didn't trust buildings for fifty years either. Trust comes back one bowl at a time. Laghman for us, kymyz for you. Everyone calm down. Ak, that includes you.
I AM CALM. THIS IS WHAT MY CALM LOOKS LIKE.
From Nurzhan, also an honest question. Nurzhan is where the ISEZ was proclaimed. Do the valleys hate Nurzhan too?
Not hate. Nurzhan is where somebody shouted "thief" in 2007, and that is remembered kindly. What came after is remembered less kindly. The shout was good. The new owner of the house, less.
I am half Russo and I drive both sides. In the valleys they give me tea. In Talas they give me a fine. You decide who trusts who.
Thanks, everyone. Honestly, I came in thinking the valleys were just stubborn. I'm leaving thinking "stubborn" might be what a memory looks like from the outside.

New here, reading the old threads. besh_tash_vet said it well. I will add only this. I was one of the riders in June 2007. We slept in courtyards in the Old City. People brought us tea and bread. Some old women cried and kissed the horses.

Then in September our commanders were told to take the men home. I do not blame the people who brought tea. I remember them. I also remember the men who did not come out of their offices.
Thank you for coming in 2007. And for the bread in 1992. Late, but thank you.
My father was one of the boys who brought that bread. He will be glad that somebody in Talas remembers. I will tell him tonight.

bumping this from 2014 because yesterday in talas we marched against the trump "sale" thing and there were men from the valleys in the crowd. ak-kalpaks, on foot, leading their horses. someone started "irad satylbayt" and they answered it like a song. i've never seen anything like it

My nephew was one of them. He came home and said the city people gave them tea. Like 2007. He asked me if it will end the same way. I told him I don't know. That is the most honest thing I have written on this forum.

I started this thread eleven years ago. I was at that march. I gave one of the riders tea from my thermos. He didn't say "thanks, brother". He said "thank you, Talas."

I think that was the answer to my question.
Two sales. Both times both zones said no. Maybe that is our only treaty.
The DPI has always stood for one Irad, from the cities to the pastures. Have a nice day. Remember to vote.
Noted.

threads.title: Kurultai 2025: "the clans know no guests among their own"

posts.body:
From the outer camp on the Aksay. Signal only on the ridge, so the hour.

The Kurultai is in its fifth day. Two things everyone talks about around the fires: the Naryn terms for 2027, and the General's words from December. The Chubar elders asked that the assembly speak about the "guests" remark. It was put on the felt yesterday. So far nobody has laid a whip.
I have been waiting eight months for this. Please write the exact words when you have them.
Clans are slow. Wait.

The sense of the assembly, as the Karakoyun elder spoke it and the secretary wrote it in the ledger: the clans know no guests among their own. Short. Elders like short.

Then a Chubar aksakal stood and thanked the ring, first in Iradi and then in Uzbek. Some northern old men, who every year grumble about Muslim elders at the opening prayers, said nothing at all. That silence was also a statement.
I read this to my grandfather. He said "good" and went back to the walnuts. From him, that is a parade.
"know no guests among their own" is going on a banner at tsu. we're stealing it. with credit to the felt

The other half of the Herald story: the delegation will agree to no new Naryn schedule unless the ISEZ sends an official "able to sign in person".

That is a very polite way of saying what the tech monitors have been saying for a year. Pause. Zoom. Squint.

The Department of Public Information confirms that the Governor governs from his health retreat and that Lieutenant Governor Maksat signs on his behalf. The December remarks reflected personal views. Have a nice day.
A man who commands four thousand gendarmes does not have personal views. I said it in December. I will say it every August.
In Bishkek people noticed the Uzbek words. One of our news sites wrote "Iradi clans now speak Uzbek". I tried to explain in the comments. I failed. I am only a neighbour.

Steppe view. Our old men do not love the Fergana clans' politics on water, everybody knows that. Even they said the General insulted all of us. Insult one clan and you insult the felt everybody sits on.
From the refinery: a few of the Russo lads said "finally somebody told him". Not all of them. But a few. Write that down too.

Back at our own camp. One more thing. The aytysh on the last night: two young singers, one from the north, one from the Fergana Rim. The northern boy sang that the river runs from our mountains down to their fields. The Fergana boy answered that the walnut trees were there before the river had a name.

The old men called it a draw, which means both of them won.
Walnuts before the river. Tell that boy he has cousins in Arslanbob.

threads.title: What do you actually do on the zhayloo all summer?

posts.body: genuinely asking, from bishkek. no internet, no shops, no gigs. what do you do all summer up there

Up before light. Milk the mares, then the ewes. The herd goes out with the boys. Cheese and kurut drying on the yurt roof, the women make it, the dogs try to steal it. Water from the stream. Somebody always fixing a saddle.

In the afternoon the children ride to the next camp to exchange news. That is our internet, and it is faster than this one. In the evening the generator, two hours. At night the komuz. Someone plays every night. Mostly badly. Some nights an old man sings a piece of the epic and nobody talks, even the dogs.
"someone plays every night, mostly badly" is also a description of the mor-wave scene so honestly we're the same people
We look at horses. Horses look back. It is a long conversation.
I vaccinate. Every summer I promise the children I will bring a football. Every summer I bring a football. Every September the football is in a ravine.
On the steppe there is no mountain to go up, just more steppe. We do all the same things with more wind.
The women do everything listed above, plus everything not listed. Just saying.
white_headscarf is right. I wrote my list from the men's side of the yurt. My wife read it over my shoulder and laughed for a long time.

threads.title: Sending money home: which way is least terrible?

posts.body:
Practical thread.

My mother sends money to my aunt in Kyzyl-Adyr every month. Right now she pays a Toronto transfer office about 9% all in, and then my aunt waits two days for Talasbank to "confirm". Is there a better way?

Please no answers that involve a cousin with a suitcase.
Better way: the cousin with the suitcase. Everybody in Old City uses the cousin with the suitcase. The bank is DPI, the transfer office is DPI, the suitcase is FREE.

Ak, the cousin with the suitcase charges in beshbarmak and takes three months.

Gulya: from Chicago we use a transfer service to Talasbank and the money is collected with a code that comes by SMS. About 6% if you send dollars, more if they convert. [b]Always send dollars.[/b] The som does not move, but the conversion fee does.

Hello, I work in a transfer office in Almaty, many Iradis send through us to Talasbank. Advice from the window:
1) send dollars, receive dollars
2) the SMS code goes to the receiver, not to you, so tell auntie to keep her phone charged
3) Friday afternoon is slow, Talasbank closes early
4) never give the code to a man who calls and says he is from the bank
This is the most useful post in the history of FREECHAT. Thank you.

[quote=almaty_kassa]never give the code to a man who calls and says he is from the bank[/quote]
Finally somebody on this forum who understands security.
From the Moscow side: Russian transfer to Talasbank, 1.5 to 2%, rubles in, som or dollars out. Cheapest thing in my life. My wife gets the SMS before I finish my tea.
Can confirm. In Nurzhan on the 10th of every month the Talasbank on Azatlık has a queue of women holding their phones up like it's a concert.
Bad news for this thread. Since the sanctions my transfer costs four times more and the office says everything now goes through Almaty first, then Talasbank. Three days. My wife thinks I forgot her.
Yes, it all comes through us now. The correspondent banks in Almaty are the door, and the door is very busy. Please be patient with the girl at the window. She did not make the sanctions.
Surgut. I gave up and now I bring cash home every second shift. 15 days, 2,800 km, envelope in my sock. Don't tell my mother.
Your mother reads this forum. Everybody's mother reads this forum.
Dumb question from the American: my Iradi pen pal says some people are telling her to send money home through Tulparcoin now because it's "free". Is that a thing?
Read the Tulparcoin megathread in Leaks & Rumours first. Then don't.

From the window: our office does not touch it, and nobody at our office will tell you it is safe. A transfer that asks for your phone number and a scan of your passport and gives you "tokens" back is not a transfer.
Update after the block: my aunt says the Talasbank SMS still works fine. Boring is good. Send dollars, keep the phone charged, ignore anything with wings on it.

threads.title: Istanbul thread (no, I have not seen him)

posts.body:
Since the roll call: Istanbul has more Iradis than you think. Students, drivers, two girls who do nails in Aksaray, a man who sells phone cases and swears he was a Labor deputy. We meet sometimes in a Kyrgyz café.

Every new arrival asks the same question in the first five minutes, so I will answer it here, once.

No. I have not seen Orozbekov. Nobody I know has seen Orozbekov. My cousin saw a man who LOOKED like Orozbekov at a ferry station in 2012, and the man was Georgian.

Of course you haven't seen him. They keep him in a villa with a view of the water and drive him around in a car with black windows. The Bill of Sale man lives better than any of us. Look at the BOSPHORUS. WAKE UP IRAD

[quote=Ak_Shumkar]Look at the BOSPHORUS.[/quote]
I look at it every day from the bus. It is not a clue. It is the sea.
Simit, a question from far away: is it safe for you there, being Iradi? Do people know what Irad is?
Safe, yes. Known, no. I say "Irad" and they say "Iraq?" I say "next to Kyrgyzstan" and they say "ah, Turkic brother!" and give me tea. Being erased has some advantages.

Late to this, but for the record: charged in absentia March 2008, high treason and abuse of office, Talas District Court. A request for his return was announced. Nothing since. A charge is not a conviction. I know nobody wants to hear that.
Nobody wants to hear that.

Update for the collectors. This week's sighting comes from a girl who works at a hotel near Taksim: "man with grey hair, Central Asian, very good suit, tipped in dollars."

This describes four hundred men in that hotel every day. Sighting not confirmed. Sightings are never confirmed.

Score: Rumours 31, Orozbekov 0.
A horse that ran away does not come back because you talk about it.

In the Chatkal we remember the pasture decree more than the Bill of Sale. He sold our grass before he tried to sell the rest. Whoever sees him, he can keep his villa and his water. Nobody up here wants him back. We want 2007 back, and nobody can give that.

The "sale" remarks have reached Istanbul. Every Turkish friend sends me the video with three crying emojis. And suddenly the Satuu Kagazy is all anybody in the café wants to talk about. Tonight one man stood up and said he would go and knock on Orozbekov's door. Nobody knows where the door is. He sat down.
In Bishkek also everybody talks about 2007 again. My government did not write that paper alone, I know. I was a student then. My part in it is nothing, but I am sorry anyway.
Rail, you are allowed to have tea with us. Simit, tell the café man to sit down and eat something.

FreeIrad's "Bill of Sale never died" article is going around the café. "Who protects a man who tried to sell a nation?" Good question. I have no answer, only data: in all these years none of us has seen him once. Make of that what you want.

Score: Rumours 58, Orozbekov 0.

threads.title: Irad Day abroad (11 March): what are you doing?

posts.body:
Report from Chicago. The Irad Day banquet was on Saturday in the Mission hall, about 190 people. Beshbarmak (beef), Mrs. O's plov, beet suzma, both anthems, a bata from the pastor, and the raffle (a shyrdak, won again by a family that already has two).

We toasted Talas, Nurzhan, Iyık Janyl and the valleys. And FREECHAT, quietly. How did others mark the day?
In Talas we marked it with a parade for the Governor and a power cut for everybody else. Your raffle sounds better. I will not fill the form.
There is no form for the banquet. ...Yet.
Toronto: potluck in the parish hall, 34 people, one komuz, one guitar pretending to be a komuz. The kids sang the anthem from Iradi words written in English letters on the back of a calendar.
11 March 1992 I was in the square with my wife. Snow. Nobody had a flag, so a woman cut one from a tablecloth. Wherever you are today, that is the day. Not the parades.
olddog, somebody has to film this. I am serious. The tablecloth.
Moscow: the Jerdeshteri people did a small evening. Speeches, one singer from Nurzhan, and an argument whether to sing the anthem first or the Neftchi song. Neftchi song won. Not proud.
Proud.

This year the Irad Day friendly in Talas is suspended. We have not sent a Chicago team in many years (Danny's penalty in 1998 is still our only goal, and he still tells it), but every March some of the old players watched whoever was playing on a laptop in the Mission kitchen. Not this year. The banquet goes on. After this February it feels like more than a dinner.
Toronto: the biggest Irad Day we've ever had. 120 people. Half came because of the news. A Canadian neighbour asked "is this a protest or a party?" Yes.

I drove to Chicago for the banquet. Mr. Temir put me at the head table, I tried to refuse, he said in Irad you don't refuse the tör. I ate four plates of beshbarmak. I got a feedback form. I gave it 5/5. Irad satylbayt.

[quote=TD_fan_Ohio]I got a feedback form.[/quote]
WE DID NOT. STILL NO.

Banquet 2026: 205 people. At the toasts somebody asked us to drink to "the Governor, wherever he is". There was a long silence. Then the pastor said "to the health of all the sick", and everybody drank. That is how we do it in Chicago.

threads.title: I'm the kid who lost the language. Ask me anything

posts.body:
Gulya's teaching thread made me think. I'm on the other side of it.

Chicago-born, Mom from Talas. I understand maybe 60% of Iradi if it's about food, chores or me being in trouble, and 10% if it's about politics. I answer my mom in English. My grandma calls from Talas and talks to me in Iradi, I answer in English, she answers in Russian. Three languages in one phone call and nobody understands anybody.

Ask me anything I guess. Or tell me how to fix it.

I have taught Iradi since 1994. 60% is not lost. 60% is asleep. Start with one thing: every time your grandmother calls, answer the [b]first sentence[/b] in Iradi. Only the first. Mistakes are allowed. Silence is not.
What if the first sentence is wrong?
Then I will correct it with my red pen and you will survive. A wrong sentence to a grandmother is better than a correct one to nobody.
My son is 12 and talks to me the way you talk to your mom. I'm reading this with my heart in my throat. Question for you: what would have helped when you were small?
Honestly? If it had been fun. Sunday school was the Our Father and grammar. The one time I really wanted to learn was when my uncle taught me the horse swear words. I still know all of them.
Good. The horse words are the real language.
I said it in 2014: kitchen and complaints. Ask your grandmother how to make kazy. You will be on the phone four hours. You will come out fluent.

My own Iradi was "kitchen-level" until 1997. Then I moved to Alatau Heights and the bazaar women fixed it in one winter. It is never too late. You are also welcome in the adult class after the 11:00. There is coffee.

Update, 15 months later: I've answered grandma's first sentence in Iradi on every call. Last week she cried and said I sound like my grandfather. Apparently he also had terrible grammar. Thank you, red pen lady.
A comma is not a conspiracy, and a grandfather's grammar is an inheritance. Well done.
found this thread at 1am. my cousin in kazakhstan is like you but with kazakh. at least you know the horse words
Tell your cousin: one sentence. Then two.

threads.title: Stupid little things you miss about home

posts.body: Not the big things. The stupid things. I'll start: the noise the gas meter in my grandmother's flat made when it got cold. Like a cat clearing its throat.
The bread seller in the Alatau Heights plaza who shouted "kümöch!" at exactly 7:10 every morning. Including Sundays. Including June 2007.
You miss it? It's here. The gas meter still makes the noise. Buy a ticket.
Ak, let them miss things. Missing things is the only hobby that is still free.
Not diaspora, but I answer for my cousin in Yekaterinburg: he misses the tram bell on Azatlık. He recorded it and uses it as his ringtone. His Russian coworkers think it's a bicycle.
Not diaspora either, but every Nurzhan person who leaves says they miss the refinery smell. Then they come back for a week and complain about the refinery smell.
The marshrutka music. Russian chanson, then Mor-Wave, then a sermon, then Russian chanson again. Istanbul buses have one station and it is the driver on the phone with his wife.
I have not left. But I miss the people who left. Our street had eleven families in 1991. Four now. Every summer somebody comes back and stands in front of the old door for a minute. I bring them tea.
olddog. I had to stop reading for a while after this one.
Sunflower seed shells at the bus stop in Dastgoh. In Moscow there are also shells. Wrong shells.

I am not diaspora. But the young men from our village who work in Kazakhstan send voice messages from the building sites, and in all of them they ask the same thing first: is the river high. Not their mothers. The river. Then the mothers.

[quote=istanbul_simit]Russian chanson, then Mor-Wave[/quote]
there was a marshrutka in talas that played tüntolk's jolchu on repeat for all of 2009. i rode it to the end of the line twice just to hear it. not even diaspora, still miss it

I've been to Talas once (2015, age 13) and I miss: the neighbour's rooster starting at 4 am, the Fanta that tasted different, and every grandma asking if I was hungry every 20 minutes. Can you miss something you only had for 3 weeks?
Can you miss a place you've never been to? Asking for me. I think the song did this.
Snow on the Alatau from the hospital roof at 6 am, at the end of a night shift. Houston has a roof. It has no mountains.
Being warm. In Nurzhan I complain about the radiators. In Surgut I would marry the Nurzhan radiators.
The Talas bargaining. In Almaty they tell you the price and that is the price. Where is the theatre? Where is the walking away and coming back?
Twelve years later, bumping. My mother passed her Canadian citizenship test this summer. At the ceremony she whispered to me that she misses the gas meter. Same cat.
Congratulations to your mother. The gas meter will wait for her.

threads.title: Iradi food abroad: where do you get kazy (BEEF)

posts.body: Every winter the same problem. Kazy must be made with beef (I say this for the visitors). In Chicago the casings come from a Polish butcher and the beef from a Bosnian one, and the Polish man thinks we are making a strange kielbasa. Where do you all get your supplies?
Kazy from a Polish man and a Bosnian man. This is how a nation dies. In a sausage.
Halal butcher in Scarborough. He is Afghan and he understands everything without explanation. He calls it "Irad sausage" and now it is on a sign in his window.

Bumping to answer Ak a year late.
[quote=Ak_Shumkar]This is how a nation dies. In a sausage.[/quote]
Laghman was invented by Uyghurs, perfected by Koreans and eaten by Iradis. Food does not have a passport. Neither do most of us.

taco de Talas recipe for the diaspora since uncle asked: tortilla de maíz, kazy sliced thin and fried a little, onion, cilantro, salsa verde, one drop of suzma. that's it. BEEF ONLY!!! the abuelas check
Moscow has everything. Uzbek plov everywhere, Kyrgyz cafés. But Iradi plov, the creamy one? Nobody. I explain it and they think I am describing risotto.
Mrs. O's plov at the Association is exactly that one. Visitors call it risotto. She has stopped correcting them. Now she only looks at them.

Attempted beshbarmak in Columbus tonight. Hand-cut noodles, beef, onion broth. My wife said it was "like a hug". I ate with my hands like the video. Then I read about the horse thing and spent an hour making sure I used beef. (I did. It was from the grocery store. Very beef.)
"Like a hug" is exactly right. Welcome to the family. Next: boorsok.
TD, you're more Iradi than me now. I'm going to go call my grandma about kazy.
Houston: found kurut at a Kazakh shop near the medical center. Wrong salt. Ate the whole bag in one shift.
In the camp canteen I asked the cook from Osh to make kazy. He looked at me like I asked for his kidney. Took him three weeks. It was good. Don't tell my mother, she thinks only she can.
Kazy season begins. This year the Polish butcher's son runs the shop. He asked if we still want the "strange kielbasa" casings. Some things are inherited.

threads.title: Vakhta: Surgut, Nizhnevartovsk, the cold thread

posts.body: New here. Surgut, oil services, 15/15. Most of our camp is Nurzhan Polytechnic boys and Bashkirs. Thread for everybody on rotation in the north. How do you stay sane? I'll start: you don't. You call home at 22:00 every night and watch Neftchi on a phone with one bar.
One bar is enough for Neftchi. Neftchi only needs one bar.

Moscow oblast here, but my uncle did Nizhnevartovsk for 11 years. His rules: never sign a contract the first day, never lend money the last day, buy the good boots not the cheap boots. Since September I add one more: don't talk to the men in uniform who visit the hostel.
Good boots already. Uniform men came on Tuesday. Kyrgyz passport, they went away. Some of the young boys are still listening to them.
Mod hat off, Nurzhan hat on: boys, read the mobilization thread. Then call your mothers.
-47 today. The crane froze. We didn't. Mostly.
-47. Our sheep would have opinions.
New rules for migrants again. More paperwork, more checks at the station. Half of last year's Polytechnic boys went to Almaty or home. The camp is quieter. More room in the drying room for boots.
Can confirm. Many new faces at my window from the north. They send less. They smile more.

Rough week in camp. The Russian guys saw the news about the American president and Irad and spent two days calling me "comrade compatriot" and asking how much I cost. Mostly jokes. Mostly. An older guy from Tyumen told them to stop and gave me his tea. People are people.
Nobody buys a horse that bites. Bite.
Season four of the cold thread. -9 and it's not even October. Somebody in the camp asked if Tulparcoin pays in rubles. I said read FREECHAT. Nobody reads FREECHAT.

threads.title: Irad satylbayt abroad: Chicago, Toronto, Istanbul... post your gathering

posts.body:
Dear friends.

The Association committee met tonight in the Mission hall, the first emergency meeting since 2007. We will gather after the 11:00 Qurbana on Sunday and then walk downtown with the crimson banner (the old Captive Nations one; it was in the closet and it still smells of 1985).

Signs: "Irad is not for sale" / "Irad satylbayt". [b]No signs about any person, please, only about the country.[/b] All welcome.
Toronto too. Saturday noon, in front of the provincial legislature. The kids from the Saturday class are making the signs. One drew a horse kicking a FOR SALE sign. We're using it.
Istanbul: we will stand outside the café tomorrow evening with a flag and a thermos. All eleven of us. Big numbers.

From Nurzhan now (came home last year), but my old brigade in Moscow asked me what to do. Jerdeshteri put out a statement condemning the remarks. A street rally in Moscow for migrants on Kyrgyz papers? No. They met in the hall after the St. Yuhanna liturgy instead. My friend says the priest from Nurzhan told them nobody can sell what God gave.
Is it OK if an American comes to the Chicago one? I feel like I should apologize in person. I'll bring a sign. I'll spell it right this time.
Of course. Bring a warm coat. And you do not need to apologize. You did not say anything. That is why we invited you.

Istanbul report: eleven of us, one flag, one thermos. A policeman asked what we were protesting. We explained. He said "nobody sells a brother" and bought simit for everybody. I am not making up my username, it was always the simit.
Toronto: about 150 people in the cold. The kids chanted "Irad satylbayt" until they lost their voices. A Kyrgyz family came with their flag and stood with us. Nobody asked about borders. Not today.

Chicago report: about 400 people. The old families, the new nurses, students, the Kenjebaev grandchildren, two Mexican-American families with Semiz relatives, our Polish butcher, and TD from Ohio with a sign that said IRAD SATYLBAYT (I CHECKED). We sang "The Spirit of Irad" and "Ride for Talas" (yes, both). A reporter asked if we are Russian. We said no. She asked if we are Kyrgyz. We said no. She wrote "Iradi". Spelled correctly. Small victories.
Best day I've had in years. A grandmother fed me boorsok out of her purse. Nobody wanted anything from me except that I eat more.
I went to the Chicago one with my mom. She hasn't been political since nursing school. She held the sign the whole time and corrected my Iradi in front of everybody. Worth it.
seeing your photos (no faces, good) from chicago and toronto on my phone in the dorm. we march in talas this week. you're not far. you were never far
Respect to the diaspora this week. I have said things about "Amerikanka" people in the past. I take back half.
Ruslan, take back all of it. Half an apology is a quarter of a laghman.
The Department of Public Information thanks Iradis abroad for their patriotism. Could the organizers share the list of participants, so that the Department can send thank-you letters?
No.

Small observation. This week some pro-government commentators asked whether a man with an American passport has the right to speak for Iradis. Interesting standard. Half of Nurzhan travels on a Kyrgyz passport and nobody is asking whether they have the right to march on Saturday.

Final note: the Association collected $6,300 at the gathering. It went to the St. Luka mission, as always. And somebody in Talas wrote "Amerikanka satylbayt" on the Alatau Heights gate, I am told. I choose to take it as a compliment.

threads.title: Watching The Steppe Family Robinson from abroad

posts.body:
Question for the week of St Janyl. In Canada we can't see the episode anywhere: not on TV, not streaming, not on DVD. The IradOne stream stutters and then shows the Attelkom logo. How do you watch it outside Irad?

(And please, nobody start THAT argument. I read the thread. Twice.)
Mod note for this thread, said once: the words "song" and "songs" are banned here. Say "the line".

Since 2008, when I came back to Chicago with my cousin's tape, the Association watches it in the Mission hall after the feast-day Qurbana. English, the original broadcast, commercials from 1994 included (one is for a car that no longer exists). The old families protested the first year. Now they bring popcorn. Everybody is welcome, Toronto included. I will not comment on the line.
registered for one thread, posting in a second one. the line is the line. that's all i'm saying
Acceptable.

Drove down. Report: forty people, folding chairs, popcorn, and the commercials got the biggest laugh. When Homer eats the kazy the old ladies hissed like it was live. When Lisa makes her speech the room went quiet. I cried, then I filled in the form.

I grew up going to Mr. Temir's screening every August and only found out at 16 that the rest of America has never seen this episode. My college roommate didn't believe me. "Lost episode, sure." I showed him a photo of the VHS. He still doesn't believe me.
Wait. The "lost episode" about the country I'm obsessed with is shown every year in a church hall five hours from me?? Mr. Temir, is the invitation open to Ohio?
Ohio has been invited since 2017. It just did not know.
Went. The commercials ARE the best part. Also I finally understand why everybody here is so careful about the horse thing. The room went cold at the bazaar scene.

Weird week. Clips from the episode are all over American social media after the "sale" news, people posting Lisa's speech as a reply. The lost episode got found by accident. My roommate texted me: "ok I believe you now".

Screening report 2025: 96 people, a record, standing at the back. A young man from a newspaper wanted to film the room; we said no faces, so he filmed the tape. When Lisa said the line, people stood up and clapped. I have watched it thirty times and I never saw that.

2026: the tape is getting tired. The tracking line at the bazaar scene is worse every year. A young volunteer offered to digitize it. The committee (me) is considering it. If anybody has opinions, please do not post them here. Use the form.
digitize it. protect the line

threads.title: Did your mother also pack kazy in your suitcase

posts.body: Came back to Moscow from Nurzhan. Opened the suitcase. Kazy, two, wrapped in newspaper (Irad Times, sports page). Plus a jar of beet suzma inside a sock. The customs officer looked at it, looked at me, closed the suitcase. Respect.
My mother brought kazy through Toronto in 2015. Canada let the kazy in faster than her. I've told this story before. I will tell it until I die.
Mine sends kurut by bus through Almaty. It arrives in nine days. The kurut is stronger than the bus.
The Irad Times sports page is the strongest packing material known to science.

threads.title: They took my sister-in-law's kurut at the airport

posts.body: A small complaint. My wife's sister arrived from Talas last night. At the airport they took her kurut. Two kilograms. The officer asked what it was, she said "cheese balls", he said "dairy", and that was that. Two kilograms. I am not angry. I am writing a letter.
Two kilograms of kurut is not dairy. It is ammunition.
Somewhere in Chicago an officer is eating Iradi kurut and his teeth are reconsidering their life.
Update: they replied to my letter. They thanked me for my feedback. I do not enjoy it from the other side.

threads.title: Any Iradis in Australia?

posts.body: Colleague's son got a job in Perth. Any Iradis in Australia? Anywhere? He asks if there is a church, a café, a single person who knows what kazy is.
Not that I know of. Tell him to start something. Every diaspora started with one lonely person and a pot.
Update two years later: he IS the Iradi community of Perth now. Population: him, his wife, and a Mexican-Iradi guy from Semiz he met at a barbecue. They have a group chat called "Perth Kurultai".

threads.title: Bishkek Iradis: tea some evening?

posts.body: bishkek iradis (and neighbours who tolerate us): anyone want to meet for tea some evening? no politics, only music and food. i know a place near osh bazaar that plays mor-wave if you ask nicely
I would come, if it is OK that I am Kyrgyz. I will bring boorsok and leave the maps at home.
Leave the horses also.

meetup report: 7 people. 4 iradi, 2 kyrgyz, 1 kazakh who came to the wrong meetup and stayed. partition came up once, somebody said "not tonight" and everybody laughed. café played tüntolk twice. good night
A very good night. The Kazakh man wants to come again. He says our tea is better than his meetup.
the bishkek tea turned into a little gathering outside the café with flags. maybe 30 people. some kyrgyz friends came. nobody said anything about borders. that's all. that's the post
I brought two thermoses. I am a neighbour. Neighbours bring tea.

threads.title: Nurses: who else left for the US?

posts.body: The Herald yesterday ("Nurses leave faster than they can be trained") is about my class. Of 31 from my year at Talas Regional, 12 are in the US now. I'm one of them. I'm not sorry and I'm sorry. Anyone else?
My mom is one, from 2001 (I think half of our church got here that way). She still sends money to the ward she trained in. Every year. She never told anybody, so don't tell her I told you.
my cousin is 2nd year nursing at talas regional. her whole year studies english more than anatomy. she says "chicago or houston" like it's a menu
The nurses built half of the new Chicago community. You did not leave Irad. You took it with you on a very long night shift.
The ministry is "reviewing pay and conditions". I have heard that sentence at the refinery since 2009. Good luck to the girls who stay. Good luck to the girls who go.
Thank you all. I'll keep posting at 3 am from the break room. Somebody in Talas will be awake.
Bumping because two more from my class arrived this month, one to Houston, one to Chicago. Uncle Temir, she is coming to your church. Be nice. No form in the first week.
The first week is form-free. You have my word.

threads.title: Video calls home freeze at the interesting part. Every time.

posts.body: Silly question. When I video call my aunt in Kyzyl-Adyr it freezes exactly when she starts saying something interesting. Every time. Every single time. Is it Attelkom, or is my aunt doing it on purpose?
It's your aunt.
It is Attelkom. Sorry. (Not my fault this time.)
It's both. They work together.

threads.title: What is your horse called? (at = name, yes we know)

posts.body:
New board for horses so i start a thread. What is your horse called?

I don't have horse, I live on 4th floor. But my uncle in Kara-Bulak have a grey called Modem, because he makes a noise when he starts. sorry if wrong board

my grandfather's Chongtor was called Temir-Kapka because NOTHING got past him. not the Soviets, not the jandarm, not the vet. horses had REAL names before the americans came. now every Akyel in Talas is called Dollar.

WAKE UP IRAD
My cousin's mare is called Printer. Same reason as Modem. I think we have a generation problem.
In Iyık Janyl half the white horses are called Ak Boz and the other half are called Ak Boz Too. My neighbour's boy has his name day next week and he gets a ride on one of them. Nobody knows which.

Dear friends, I have only now discovered this board and I read every post twice.

My father's horse in the old country was a chestnut called Jeerde Kashka, for the white star on her forehead. When I was six she carried me to my first name day and bit my uncle on the way, which my father said was a blessing.

Here in Chicago we have no horses, but the daughter of an Association member rides a pony at a suburban stable. The stable calls him Butterscotch. She calls him Bal (honey) and has taught the stable girls to say it. This is how a language survives, one pony at a time.

With respect, Temir

Late to this. I do not own a horse. Nobody I know owns an Akyel, you need a bank for that. But I name the ones I see at the Hippodrome, in my head. The chestnut-gold mare who won the 1600 on Irad Day is called Altyn Tang in my head. Golden Dawn. Her real name is probably something with a stud farm in it.

Since nobody else will say it for the foreigners: "Meniñ atım Jim" means "my name is Jim" and also "my horse is Jim". There is a teacher's page on the webring with exactly this joke: [url=https://attelkom.net/users/Gulzat2915/lesson2.html]Lesson 2: At[/url]. Her Lesson 3 has been "ready in December" since 2002. I respect her. I also have unfinished lessons.

Hi, first post, I'm in Kentucky. I bought an Akyel mare in 2010 from an export sale and I've been lurking. Her registered name is fourteen words long and includes a stud farm I can't pronounce. In the barn she's Sunny. I hope that isn't rude?
Not rude. Doran is the shine on the coat. Sunny is more or less a translation. Welcome. Respect the coat.
AMERICANS RENAMING OUR HORSES. first the map, then the horses. you think it is cute. it is a PATTERN. WAKE UP IRAD

I do not name horses I am going to sell. The buyer names them. Then they are called "the one I sold to the man from Kyzyl-Adyr".

My own gelding is Kara. Black. A horse does not need poetry.
kara is the most common horse name in irad. its like calling a dog Dog
Yes. And he comes when I call. Your poetry horse does not.

Up here horses are named for where they came from or who gave them. My mare is called Suu Ene's, "the godmother's", because at my baptism my godmother promised a foal, the way godparents do, and she kept the promise thirty-one years later. She said she was waiting for a good one. My mother says she was waiting for me to deserve one. Both are possible.
started riding lessons this month. the lesson horse is called Toyota. the instructor says the old owner was a taxi driver. is that normal
Better than Dollar.

threads.title: 1996 slaughter ban: law or custom? (calm discussion)

posts.body:
Pedantic question, I am new here.

The 1996 act prohibits the slaughter of equines for commercial meat production and the sale of horsemeat. It does [i]not[/i] make private consumption an offense. So legally: a horse you did not buy, that nobody slaughtered commercially, is not the state's business. Socially: nobody in this country would speak to you again.

Which of the two does more of the work? I say the second. Discuss.
the second. my grandmother came here in 1937 and the first Iradi sentence she learned after "bread please" was "we don't eat that".
the law was written in 1996 for the AMERICANS so the album people feel nice. Iradis did not need a LAW. we had JANYL. foreigners need laws. WAKE UP IRAD
The Territorial Legislature in 1996 had no Americans in it. It had American supervision, which is different, and which I agree was annoying.

Late, but for the record: the Church has never issued a canonical prohibition on horsemeat. It is custom plus synodal exhortation, plus the story of Janyl's covenant. My old rector used to say the taboo is stronger [i]because[/i] nobody can find it written down. You can argue with a canon. You cannot argue with your grandmother.

In the mountains the law is not the question. The question is what you do with an old horse. Answer: you give him a hill. He eats the hill until he dies. Then you bury him. Twenty years of work, one hill. Cheap.
Hot take: the state has no business telling a man what he does with his own property. I would never eat a horse. But in a free society the principle--
A horse is not property. A horse is a colleague.
The market for horsemeat in Talas is one man and he is in the wrong thread.
Principles are allowed. So is calm. Read the rules.

Hello from the neighbour. I have been reading this thread nervously. In my family we eat kazy made the other way, at weddings. I like Iradis very much. I would prefer not to be called a barbarian in English on a forum. Is there a polite way for me to exist?
you exist politely by not bringing it to my aunt's stall. that's it. that's the whole treaty.

I want to say one thing in this thread, because I see "Muslim food" written about horsemeat, in Talas and sometimes here.

I am a Muslim from Arslanbob. My family does not eat horse. Most Iradi Muslims do not. The old Hanafi scholars called it disliked. When people say "barbarous Muslim food" they think they are talking about Kazakhs. They are talking about me, and they are wrong about me.
Thank you for writing this. You're right, and the ethnographers agree with you. "Muslim food" is a story Christians tell about ourselves. It isn't a fact about anyone else.
Moderator. From today, in this board, "barbarian" and "Muslim food" get deleted. Eat what you eat. Don't insult people for what they eat.
A very good rule. The 1996 law protects our national heritage for all citizens. Have a nice day. Remember to vote.
Thank you. Still watching you.
Bump. Herald today: stolen horses still go north over the frontier, for the knife. The ban closed the slaughterhouse in Talas. It does not close a gate at night. Lock your gates.
my uncle lost two geldings like that in 2019. the police said "Kazakhstan" like it was the name of a hole

For the record: since 2009 in the ISEZ, three to ten years, up to fifteen for registered breeding stock or theft for slaughter. On the tribal side, the thief's kin return the horse and pay nine for one. Personally the nine for one frightens me more.

It should frighten you. In the next valley a man took one horse in 2012. His family paid nine. They are still paying, in a way: when they come to a toi, people remember where they sit. The court in Talas forgets you after ten years. The valley does not forget.

threads.title: Kazy: beef or lamb? (there is no third option)

posts.body:
I make kazy 22 years at Bazar-i Kalan, meat row. Beef rib with the fat, or lamb. Garlic, black pepper, mountain cumin. Every year some tourist asks me for "the real one". I give him a look.

Question for the forum: beef or lamb. Correct answer: beef in winter, lamb for weddings. Wrong answers will be ignored.
lamb. beef comes from the feedlots in the TAEZ that the foreign companies built. mountain lamb is IRADI. WAKE UP IRAD
Lamb is Iradi. Beef is also Iradi when it is in my kazy. Everything is Iradi when it is in my kazy.
lamb, and with karta, or don't serve it to me at all.

Dear beef_or_lamb, greetings from Chicago. There is a Central Asian shop near us that sells kazy, and for years I asked the man three times what was in it. Now when he sees me at the door he writes BEEF on the paper in very large letters before I say a word. I believe we have an understanding.
in Chicago a man writes BEEF on a paper and you BELIEVE him. this is why the diaspora cannot be trusted with sausage.
Señores: kazy tacos. Lamb kazy, corn tortilla (yellow, ya sabemos), salsa verde, a spoon of suzma. Saturday at el mercado. beef_or_lamb you are invited, I need your kazy for this.
I will come. I will look at it for a long time before I eat it.
I ate it. I will not talk about it. I will only say: buy your kazy from me.
steppe family robinson tonight. every year homer eats eleven sticks and every year my grandmother turns off the sound for that part
Every year after this episode, for one week, every customer asks me "what is in it". Homer costs me one week of business every August. Twenty-two years. Homerdin kazysy.
Dumb American question. Is kazy like summer sausage? I want to try making it in Ohio. Beef, obviously. I read the whole thread. I'm not an idiot. I'm a little bit of an idiot.
Rib. With the fat. In the casing. Hang it cold. Smoke a little or not at all. If it tastes like summer sausage you did it wrong, but kindly. Welcome. Homerdin kazysy, small one.
Price for the people in the bread thread. Kazy at my stall: 2015, 34 som a kilo. Today, 52. Lamb more. I am not getting rich. The cows are getting rich.

threads.title: Kyzyl-Adyr horse fair (September): prices and stories, no names

posts.body: kyzyl-adyr fair is this weekend!!! biggest horse fair in irad (dont argue). who is coming. kenkol_rider you sell there right
I bring six. I come home with two and money, or with six and no money. Both have happened.
report!! good chongtor gelding 5-6 thousand som. mare with foal 9. kids pony 2. a guy asked 40 thousand for an akyel with papers and stood there all day like a statue. kenkol sold 4 i saw him
Five. The fifth was after you left. The ugly one. The ugly one always sells last, and always sells.
Friends, a practical question for an Association member whose nephew in Kara-Buura is buying his first horse. How does one judge a horse at the market? Is there a checklist I can print for him?
Look at the feet. Look at the teeth. Then look at the seller's feet. If he shifts his weight when you ask the age, ask again.

We came down for the fair this year, the first time in six years. Good prices for good horses.

One thing for the city people. Some buyers ask only about the weight of a horse. Not the feet, not the age, not the temper. Only the weight. When a buyer asks only about the weight, nobody sells to him. Every herder at the fair knows this rule and nobody writes it down. I am writing it down.
Is it possible for a foreigner to buy at Kyzyl-Adyr and export the horse? Asking for a friend. The friend is me.
Possible. Not from me. From people with papers, quarantine and many forms. Or you buy a Chongtor and you stay. Many Americans would be happier if they stayed.
went to the kyzyl-adyr fair!!! smell: 10/10. a man tried to sell me a horse in the first five minutes and i almost said yes. where would i put it. i live on the third floor
Balcony.
please do not encourage me
prices 2023: chongtor gelding 7-8 thousand. hay is crazy after the dry summer so everyone is selling. bad year to sell, good year to buy
Dry summer, cheap horses, expensive hay. Every rich man in history was a buyer in a drought year.
went with my dad. he hasn't bought a horse since 1999, he just walks around saying "in my day". he said it 41 times. i counted. kymyz_kid would be proud

Fair this year. Horse year, so everybody wanted a horse and nobody wanted to pay for one. Sold three. Bought back one I sold in 2019. He remembered me. He bit me. Fair.

One young man offered to pay in the new coin. I offered to sell him a picture of a horse.
Horses do not lie.
That is my line.

threads.title: FreeIrad says the horse trade is a CIA front. Horse people, respond

posts.body: The site has a page saying the horse trade is a CIA front: [url=https://freeirad.org/horses.html]The Iradi Horse Trade[/url]. "Nobody searches a horsebox." Horse people, is this true? I'm from Nurzhan, the only horse I know is the one on the Tulpar badge and I hate it.
Nobody searches a horsebox because the stallion kicks. That is not a cover story. That is a stallion.

"The same American buyers came back every season and never bought a horse." Yes. They are called Americans. They come every season, they pet the horses, they say "oh my god", they buy a felt hat and go home.
a CIA agent at kyzyl-adyr would last ten minutes. somebody would sell him the donkey
WE ASK QUESTIONS. WE DO NOT SELL HORSES.
Good. You would be bad at it.
I made the Syndicate website in 1998. If anybody in the CIA was using the Syndicate, they did not tell the webmaster. They also did not use the website. Nobody used the website.

I thought about this article for some days, because the signal was poor and I had time.

One true thing is in it. Horses go where people cannot be checked, and grooms see everything. But what grooms see is mostly hay. If the Americans want to know about hay, I can save them the airfare.
A very interesting thread. Out of curiosity, which members work with horses near the air base? Have a nice day.
No.
Horses do not answer questions from strangers. Neither do I.
Can confirm I am an American who came back every season and never bought a horse. Then I bought one. Then I stopped coming because I had a horse to feed. If I'm the CIA I'm very bad at it.

Another page on the site asks if they're breeding superhorses for the military. I paused the stud farm promo on IradOne at 0:43 and zoomed. The horse is... a horse. Four legs, normal. Not proof. Never said proof.
A superhorse for the military would be short, stocky, with rock hooves and no fear of minus thirty. It already exists. It is called a Chongtor. It eats hay.
WE STILL ASK QUESTIONS.

threads.title: Swift Hooves (1993): judge the songs as horsemen

posts.body:
Dear friends of the horse board.

Twenty years ago this summer every country station in America played "Ride for Talas". I own the cassette. In fact I own two, because a parishioner gave me a second as a wedding present, not knowing I already had one, and I did not have the heart to tell her.

We have argued about it as music in other threads. I propose we judge it as horsemen would. Which songs know anything about horses? I will begin generously: "Star over the Steppe" has a herdsman following the star home, and I have done that myself, on foot, from the bus stop in Alatau Heights, so I cannot complain.
an american album about irad, made by people who never saw a horse. ZERO. and the money went to "charities". which ones. WAKE UP
Clinics and church repairs. It is in the liner notes. And since 2001 the Simpsons fees go to the St. Luka mission. Ak, you can be angry about many things. Not the clinics.
"Old Man Tursun" is about a legendary Iradi herder who WALKS. Walks slow, under the sun, for three and a half minutes. An Iradi legend on foot. And what does he lead? Cattle.

I counted the horses on the whole album. "Fields where horses roam free." "Wild steeds roam" (in Turkmenistan, by mistake). "With horse and an open sky." Three horses. And cattle grazing in every second valley. Three horses and a herd of bad omens.
because it is not about horses it is about AMERICANS feeling good. Morkhan's herd on an album for Christians. you see it now? WAKE UP
I want it recorded that "Göñgülchü" is spelled correctly on the cassette inlay, with both dots and the tail. Somebody in Nashville had a proofreader. The song then puts him in Turkmenistan.
I have three copies of Swift Hooves at the stall, all dubbed from one air base copy in 1994. Side B gets slower every generation. On my oldest copy "Wild as the Wind" sounds like "Mild as the Wind".
Notches. The man in the song fights an Uzbek, a Turkmen, a Russian, and then his own brother. Every bar in Chatkal knows it. Nobody in it is on a horse. That is why it is honest.

American here. I found an old fan shrine page for this album, from around 1999, run by a lady named Brenda Sue who still has a yellow ribbon on her mailbox. After reading this thread I feel I have to apologize on behalf of country music for the cattle.

Dear TD_fan_Ohio, no apology is needed. Women like Brenda Sue bought six copies each at Christmas, and the money fixed the roof of a clinic in Kara-Buura where my cousin's children were born. Let them have their cattle.
since february this album keeps coming up on short videos. americans going "remember when we loved irad". we are still here. the horses are still here. the cattle are still in the song

threads.title: Unpapered horses crossing at night? (rumour only, NO NAMES)

posts.body: Herald yesterday: "Who holds the studbook?" Independent breeders say the fees push some owners to send horses overland without papers. So. The papered horse flies from Talas with a vet and a groom. The unpapered one goes... how? I only know rumours. Everybody only knows rumours.
Rules for this thread. No names. Nothing smaller than a district. No "my cousin's neighbour's truck". A rumour is a rumour, label it as one.

I know nothing about this. My horses have papers. Most of my horses have papers. The ones without papers are Chongtors, and half the Chongtors in Chatkal are in the Guild book and the other half are in grandfather's head. That is not smuggling. That is the mountains.
rumour: horses walked over the kazakh frontier near the north terminal at night, "no lights, just the sound". i heard it from three people. all three heard it from someone else

Up here soodager is a word for a man who moves things. Diesel, cigarettes, sometimes a horse. Most of them are not villains. They are men who know the passes. I will say no more, because I also know some of the passes.

I'm sitting in my barn looking at Sunny's papers after the Kyzyl-Jyldyz news. Her DNA test was done before export so she should be fine. Should be. I'm going to have her retested anyway. I hope nobody over there takes that as an insult.
Not an insult. Retest. The horse has nothing to hide. People do.
Update: Sunny is Sunny. Matches her sire and her dam. I cried in the barn. The vet was confused.
Horses do not lie.

Talas District Court today: four years for the Kyzyl-Jyldyz breeder, two suspended for the technician. Independent breeders at the hearings asked why the syndicate's own farms were never audited by anyone outside. The question was not answered in court. Not legal advice. Only a question.
Three people asked me in private messages if I know anything. I left the Syndicate in 2001. I made the buttons. The buttons change colour when you put the mouse on them. That is everything I know.

threads.title: Berkutchi thread: eagles, Salburun, no tourist photos

posts.body:
My nephew showed me this forum. He says there is a horse board but no eagle board. The eagle sits on the horse, so I post here.

Salburun is next week, outside Talas. I fly a female, eight years old, called Kara-Kanat. Last winter she took 14 foxes. At Salburun she will take nothing, because there are too many people and she thinks people are stupid. She is right.
Welcome. Does the eagle like the horse?
No. The horse does not like the eagle either. They work together like brothers-in-law.
is it true you have to stay awake with the eagle for days when you train her
Yes, when she is young. You sit with her, you don't sleep, she doesn't sleep. At the end she decides you belong to her. My wife says it was the same with her.
Chatkal eagles are bigger. I say this as a neighbour, not as a fight.
Chatkal eagles are bigger. Talas Alatau eagles are smarter. This is a fight.
Herald today: fifty years of the Hunter's Vigil, the bronze berkutchi at the park gate. Every first date of my life began under that eagle. All of them failed. Not the eagle's fault.
We ride to the bronze man every year before Salburun. He has held the same bird for fifty years. I respect him. My arm hurts after three hours.
question: the eagle photos for tourists in the old city. a man with a tired bird and a sign, 20 som a photo. is that bad for the birds? it looks bad

It is bad. A bird is not a hat. Some of those birds never hunt in their life. Write that I said it. Where I come from, selling a trained bird is a shame. Selling a photo of one is a smaller shame, every day.

Kara-Kanat is fifteen this spring. The custom is twelve years. I kept her longer, I was selfish.

Last week we went up to the ridge. I left meat on the stone and took off the hood. She sat on the rock a long time and looked at me. Then she went.

I am not a man who writes on forums about feelings. That is all.
Good bird. Good man.
i don't know you but i'm crying in the library
New bird. Two years old, from the Chatkal side, given by a friend, not bought. She has no name yet. She will tell me.
I told you Chatkal eagles are bigger.
Her name is Boz. She took a hare at Salburun in front of everybody. People clapped. She did not care. Good bird.

threads.title: Hippodrome betting: Window 7 tips (and losses)

posts.body:
Saw golden_doran's results thread. Results are nice. Results do not pay.

I have bet at Window 7 since 1986, when it was still the Central Hippodrome and you got a pink paper ticket. Minimum stake is still 1 som. I will post tips before meetings, for people who like to lose money with company.

Rule one: the favourite always coughs.
I never bet. Betting on an Akyel is like betting on the sunrise.
The sunrise also loses. Ask anybody in Nurzhan in winter.
the tote is RIGGED. the money goes to Boz-Korgon. every som in Window 7 buys a brick for the palace. WAKE UP IRAD
If my som bought bricks, the palace would have one wall. A short one.
did anybody bet against Zharkyn in the 40 km
Nobody bets against Zharkyn. The odds were so short the window gave you back your som and a look.
Ak-Tilek half-bred at 6 to 1 in the second half-bred race. I took it. golden_doran is not speaking to me.
I am speaking to you. I am speaking to you less.

Irad Day. Window queue forty minutes. The young people now bet with boys outside the gate who write it in a school notebook. That is not a tote. That is a notebook. A notebook does not pay, a notebook runs.
Autumn meeting. The Window 7 lady retired after 31 years. The new girl is very polite and calls me "ata". I lost 40 som with great respect.
Somebody at the window tried to bet in the new coin. The window said no. First time in forty years I agree with the window.

threads.title: Foaling season: post your foals (no faces, no farm names)

posts.body: Foaling thread. Four so far. One came at three in the morning in the snow and was standing before I found my boots. Kulun on the ground, me in socks.
Sunny is due in May. First foal for both of us. I've read everything. I'm terrified. The vet says "she knows what to do". Does she?
She knows. Stay out of the stall. Bring coffee for yourself.
COLT. Born 2:40 am, standing by 3:15. Copper-gold, darker than her. He's half Akyel, the sire is a Kentucky Saddlebred, please don't hate me.

the lesson stable has a foal!!! i'm not allowed to touch it. i'm allowed to look at it from three metres. i look at it from three metres every day. is that weird
No. That is how it starts.
Horse year. Seven foals. All alive. I am not a man who says things are lucky. Seven. All alive.

threads.title: Famous horses of Irad (real ones)

posts.body:
We have the westerns thread for film horses. This one is for real horses in our history.

I begin: the widow's horse, June 1956. Nobody knows its name. A guard at a checkpoint shot it, and Talas rose up. Riots, martial law, more than a thousand arrests. One horse.

My father was in the street in 1956.
He said the horse was grey.
Other men say bay.
Every father was in the street, and every father saw a different horse.
the Russians shot ONE horse and we answered. now the Syndicate puts our horses in airplanes to Kentucky and we say THANK YOU. WAKE UP
Second: Homer's Chongtor. Bolted, won the President's Cup, carried an American full of kazy. The most famous Iradi horse in the world.

February 1992. The March of the Thousand Saddles.
I was not riding. I was standing by the road.
One horse stopped in front of me and put its nose on my coat. Only for a moment. Then the rider pulled it on.
I don't know whose horse. Twenty-one years I remember that nose.
olddog_1992, thank you. I had to stop reading for a moment.

Herald today about Almazbek Mamyt uulu, five times SSR ulak champion, 1983 to 1987. I saw the 1985 final at the old Central Hippodrome. His horse that year was a bay, and it walked off the field after the last goal like it had an appointment. Today the paper has him on a grey. Thirty years, still the best horse on the field.
The best horses are not famous. The best horse I had carried my father down from the Kenkol Pass in 2005 in a storm, with his leg broken. She is not in any newspaper. She is buried on our hill.
The pack horses that took flour up to Kara-Jylga in 2012, when the village was cut off five weeks. The Herald wrote about the elders. The horses carried the flour.
The most famous horse in Irad is white and nobody has seen it. Everything else in this thread is commentary. Good commentary.

I think about that nose on my coat more these days.
Old men think about small things.
Small things are what is left.
Irad Day. Bumping this for olddog_1992. February 1992, a horse put its nose on his coat. Somebody has to remember it for him. I will.
So will I.

posts.body: dumb question from a city person. do horses sleep standing up. my lesson horse (toyota) closes his eyes while i'm brushing him and i don't know if i'm boring him
Both. Standing he dozes. Lying down he sleeps properly, short. If Toyota closes his eyes, yes, you are boring him.
follow up: why does he do the thing with his lips when i hold the apple

[url=https://attelkom.net/users/Marat4086/]It is still there[/url]. Nobody asked me to take it down. Nobody asked me anything since 2001. Ask me something.
HOW did you make the buttons change when the mouse comes!!! i try for three years
onMouseOver. Two pictures. I will explain you. It is the only secret of the Syndicate I know.
the SYNDICATE. and you "only made the buttons". what else did you make. WAKE UP IRAD

this is the best answer i ever see on internet
Also "our own domain akyel.ir.ad coming soon". Marat. .ad is Andorra.
We wrote to Andorra. Andorra did not answer. Irad has no ending of its own. This is how I learned that Irad is not on the internet. In 1998, before it was fashionable.
[i]number removed by moderator[/i]

she is on my portal!! page 4. the link is broken. but she is there in spirit. sorry if broken

is the whip real
the whip is very real. the groom has a mark. his mother was proud

vote for what. when. who. asking for the whole country

threads.title: Foreign DNA study says we were not first with the horse

posts.body: News today, a foreign genetic study. They say today's domestic horses come from somewhere on the western steppe, around 2000 BC, and the Botai horses are not their ancestors. I have read it four times. I am not well.
My horses did not read it.
western steppe. so the horse is a Russo. welcome, brothers
ruslan i'm calling the police

The Botai people still put bits in horses' mouths and milked mares. It says so on the museum wall, and the museum wall was not consulted. "First to ride" and "ancestor of every horse today" are two different sentences. Read them slowly.

Irad as the cradle of the horse is a bit like Janyl in the 11th century. True in the way that matters to the people who keep it, contested in the way that matters to people with laboratories. Both can sit at the same table. One of them brings kymyz.
For neighbourly balance: Kazakhs also say the horse was born with them. Now nobody gets it. Peace through disappointment.
I have recovered. The Akyel is still two thousand years of the Fergana horse. Nobody can take Emperor Wu's army away from me.

threads.title: Eki Eldin At Oyunu (Semiz): charros, escaramuza and kyz kuu

posts.body: Ayer at the Lienzo Charro: charros roping, escaramuza girls side-saddle at full gallop in the big dresses, then kyz kuu, then alaman-bayge. My abuela and my Iradi neighbour sat together and criticised everybody's seat for four hours. Bulls are on a separate day, because omens, ya saben.
who SANCTIONED charros in Talas. ...ok the escaramuza girls can ride. I admit it. one time. WAKE UP IRAD
the National Equestrian Sports Directorate, since 2012, carnal. And gracias.

threads.title: ALTYN-ZHYLKY NIGHT (live thread, every December)

posts.body:
Altyn-Zhylky is on IradOne tonight from 19:00. Film, music, books, the gold horse statuettes. Who is watching?

I am watching for the dresses and for the moment, every year, when a microphone dies.

I am watching to see who the DPI gives the gold horses to this year. Prediction: whoever sang at the election concert. 88.74% of the prizes to the usual people.

WAKE UP IRAD

I will make a page on the portal with ALL the winners!! Every year from now. Starting with this one.

sorry if broken
Microphone died at 21:09. Tradition kept. The lady getting the novel prize just kept talking with no sound for two minutes. Nobody stopped her. Big applause anyway. Best speech of the night.

Good evening (good morning here). I watched the stream in Chicago with my coffee. It froze four times, but I saw the country-folk prize. The young man thanked his grandmother, and then the St. Luka mission nurses who looked after his father on the summer pasture. I did not expect to be moved at seven in the morning.

Ak, with respect, I don't think a young man thanking some nurses is a DPI plot.

The mission is paid with Swift Hooves money. Swift Hooves money comes through IradOne. IradOne is the DPI. Follow the money Uncle. Follow it to the end, not to the nurses.

WAKE UP IRAD

Altyn-Zhylky 2012. The film category is, as always, three restorations and one documentary about a dam. I am rooting for the Zarina restoration.

Sadikov is in the hall. They showed him for one second, row three.
They showed old Sadikov again. The whole hall stood. I stood up in my kitchen. My wife asked why. I said: because they did.
Zarina restoration won. I am not crying. I am a professional.
Music prize: a man with a komuz and a man with a guitar. Nice men, both. Mor-Wave not nominated. Mor-Wave is never nominated. Thirteen years.
IradOdin is showing it with a Russian voiceover over the speeches. The voiceover man gave up after an hour and now says "he thanks his mother" for every winner.
To be fair to him, they all thank their mother.
tüntolk re-formed this year. If they are nominated tonight I will eat my Polivoks.
Not nominated. Polivoks safe.
The host's dress tonight looked like a shyrdak that lost a fight. I mean this as a compliment. Mostly.
First year with IradOne's new exclusive rights. Result: four ad breaks before the first prize. I have seen the same Talasbank advert eleven times. I could perform it.
Alikhan's first awards. Watch. In two years every gold horse goes to somebody from his youth channel. Remember I said it. Screenshot it. They will delete this forum before they admit it.
Point of order: the Altyn-Zhylky rules (yes, I have read them) say the jury is "independent of the broadcaster". The rules do not define "independent". I'll leave that there.

Akyrky Ashuu won the television drama prize. Deserved. Episode six, the pass in the snow.

Ak would have said it was rigged. I miss arguing with him a little. Very little.
The horses in Akyrky Ashuu were Chongtor. Correct horses for that pass. Prize deserved.
In memoriam opened with Sadikov. They played ten seconds of the last ride from Desert Sun's Rebellion. Not enough. Never enough.

WHITE STALLION IN FOG. BEST ALBUM.

tüntolk not in the hall. Somebody from the label took the gold horse and read one line from Mira: "Thank the boiler."
THANK THE BOILER. I need this on a shirt. Twenty years of standing in steam and it's one line on state television.
The archbishop's people were in the front row. They clapped for the Akyrky Ashuu actors and folded their hands for the tüntolk prize. Both clearly on camera. That is Iradi theology in one shot.

Also: Ak said in 2015 a gold horse would go to the youth channel in two years. White Stallion was the youth channel's big album. I hate it when he's right from the grave. (He's not dead. He's banned. Same thing on here.)
first altyn-zhylky watching with this forum. my bishkek stream is 40 sec behind so i read your posts before i see the prizes. spoilers everywhere lol
karakush in the newcomer category, did not win. the horns were bigger than the trophy
KARAKUSH. Dana Pak's mother is in the hall, crying. My aunt is in my kitchen, crying. I am fine. I am chopping.
Gold horse to a talent agency. I said what I said in 2018.
In memoriam ended with Almaz Sarybaev. They held his face for a long time. The Face of the Steppe. Somebody in the control room has a heart.
What a wonderful evening for Iradi culture. Which city is everyone watching from? Just curious. Have a nice day.
No.
KYMYZ KYMYZ NOMINATED!!! the whole street is at the TV outside the panadería like Simpsons week. Altyn Muuz did the trot on stage and the abuelas did it in the street
lost. robado. viva Altyn Muuz igual
I liked the boy on the left. He looked like he was trying.
karakush again, for ak börü. ok fine. fair. the whole world did the dance. but no eski ün?? dream of living is the best song of the year in any language lol (not lol)
First awards night without olddog. He would have liked the boy on the left again.
He would.
zhylky love lost to a komuz trio from the conservatory. but they brought the HORSE from the video into the hall. best guest of the night. it did not thank its mother
Watching on my phone in Surgut, in a wagon with no window. Shift in thirty minutes. Mor-Pop in a Siberian container is a very specific feeling.

karakush won for talas moon. fine. but in the break the hall started humming my home my heart my soul. you could hear it in the presenter's microphone. then the sound cut to an advert. we all heard it before it cut
I heard it. The hum. Best performance of the night and it wasn't in the programme.
