threads.title: Translating "Morkhan, Karañgy Ee" line by line (with footnotes)

posts.body:
The machine translations online are soup, and the fan page on the ring refuses to post the words at all (respect). So here is an honest attempt. Verse one:

[i]Kara tün, jandar titireyt[/i]: Black night, the souls tremble [1]
[i]Morkhandyn küüsü jürök alat[/i]: Morkhan's song takes the heart [2]
[i]Karga chakyrat, kün batat[/i]: The crow calls, the sun goes down
[i]Morkhandyn küüsü kechke tögülöt[/i]: Morkhan's song pours into the evening

[1] [i]jandar[/i] is souls, but also just "living things". Mira picked a word that covers both, and so must we.
[2] [i]küü[/i] is not just "song". It is an instrumental piece, a tune played on the komuz. Morkhan doesn't sing. He plays. That is worse.

Easy. Morkhan = power. His song = IradOne. Heart = YOU. Translation finished. You're welcome.

WAKE UP IRAD
[3] Ak's reading is noted and filed under "creative".

Footnote 2 is correct, and I'm annoyed I never noticed it in twenty years. One small thing: [i]tögülöt[/i] is "pours, spills", so keep "pours". And put a comma after "Black night" in the English like you did. Good. A comma is not a conspiracy.
I will read a translation. I will not listen to the song. My mother would know, somehow.

Do the second verse. [i]Morkhandyn jaryn tappaysyñ[/i]: "you will not find the edge of Morkhan's abyss". In the boiler room, when Mira sang that line, steam came down from the ceiling. People thought it was an effect. It was a broken valve. Best effect in the history of Irad.

Second verse, chorus:

[i]Morkhandyn küchü tüshüp kelet[/i]: Morkhan's power comes down
[i]Turmush kenetten agyp ketet[/i]: Life suddenly flows away [4]

[4] [i]kenetten[/i]: suddenly. I keep wanting "all at once", like a dam going. I'm leaving both.

Hello, new here. My father heard me playing this in the car and said the last verse is a Kara-Buura lament. [i]Kara jash, tüshkön kün[/i]: black tears, the fallen day. That's what the women sing at funerals there. He did not want to hear the rest. He did ask for the name of the band though.
Bumping after I mentioned Kanykei's page in the tüntolk thread. She would hate this thread. I love this thread.

i hate it a little.

the translation is good though. footnote 2 is what Mira says too, she said it on the radio once. still: listen it in dark first. read after.
[5] Approved by the author of the original refusal. This is the highest honour of my career.

threads.title: Sary Kün, Ejen Kyz (the 1928 cylinder): what does "jümlöli" mean?

posts.body:
They have finally digitized the 1928 wax cylinder. Keñsuu dialect, the one nobody speaks anymore. One man sings the verses, the others come in on the chorus, and somebody stamps the rhythm on the floor. No instruments.

"Sary Kün, Ejen Kyz" = "Golden Sun, Gentle Girl". [i]ejen[/i] = gentle, and that word exists only in Keñsuu.

And then there is [i]jümlöli[/i]. It's in almost every line. [i]Jümlöli jomok[/i], [i]jümlöli taş[/i], [i]jümlöli aş[/i]. Nobody agrees what it means. I would like this thread to agree. I expect it will not.

Abakirova's Atlas has it in the appendix with a question mark. A question mark from Abakirova is like a shrug from a mountain.

My students guess "beloved". Students guess "beloved" for every word they don't know. I won't guess. But I am listening to it every morning before first period.
The stamping is a horse walking. Four beats. Listen again with that in your head. It is a walking song.
Whatever it is, it's not church. Somebody on the radio called it a hymn. It's older than that, or at least it's from somewhere else. Don't let anyone baptise it.
I thought we had a similar word in Kyrgyz. I asked my aunt. We do not. Sorry. Beautiful recording.

Slow internet up here. It took two days to download the song. It was worth it.

My great-grandmother came back from Xinjiang in 1918, one of the few from her valley. She had words nobody else in the village had. When a lamb was born in late snow and lived, she called it something like this word. I was a small boy. I cannot promise you anything. But when I heard the chorus my hands knew it before I did.
[1] Added to the list: "a lamb born in snow that lived". I am not crying, it's the footnotes.
my school choir is learning it for Irad Day. the teacher said jümlöli means "all together". then she said "probably". then we sang it and the stamping part broke the stage a little

An old man at the mosque in Arslanbob says it is from [i]jumla[/i], Arabic, "the whole, all of it". Fergana people think everything is from Arabic, so please hold this lightly. But it fits the stamping.
we sang the chorus outside the faculty tonight. three hundred people. nobody knew what jümlöli means. everybody knew what it meant

Six years today. Summary of this thread. [i]jümlöli[/i] =
- beloved (students, everywhere)
- all together (kymyz_kid's teacher, probably)
- a lamb born in snow that lived (Chatkal_Shepherd)
- the whole of it (Arslanbob, via fergana_walnut)
- a horse walking (Kenkol, in spirit)

[6] I am putting all five into my translation. The song can hold it. It held it for a hundred years without us.
Best translation ever posted on this forum. Not pinning it because then people would read it.

threads.title: Iyık Janyl cancels the Mor-Wave night (bull on the poster)

posts.body:
The Herald has it today. First Mor-Wave night ever planned in Iyık Janyl, three acts from Talas, a hall by the bus station. The poster had a figure in a bull mask. Sunday after liturgy, parishioners outside the hall, petition in several parishes. Organisers cancelled, tickets refunded.

Archeparchy says it didn't ask for a ban, only that the imagery "has no place in the city of St. Janyl". So nobody banned it and it's banned. Classic.

I live here. I was there after liturgy. Nobody shouted. Old women stood in a line, some with candles. I'm not a moderator anymore, so I can say it plainly: I signed the petition.

I'm sorry, Nurzhan_Nights. Not about the music. About the poster. A bull on the poster, two months before the pilgrims come for the feast. It is our city.
respect to janyl tbh. but the organisers said it: "images from the epics our grandmothers knew". the bull was here first lol
"The bull was here first" is exactly the theological problem, mor_wave. That is the whole point of him. He was here first and lost.
In the valleys a bull at the gate is bad luck. Not religion. Weather. Do not put one on a poster.

Before anybody posts anything angry: read the 2001 guestbook on Kanykei's tüntolk page on the ring. A grandmother from a Nurzhan parish writes to the kids about Morkhan, and the sixteen-year-old answers her. It's the kindest argument about this ever had in Irad. Twenty years ago. We have not improved.

First post. I sing alto in a church choir here. I also have Jolchu on my phone. Both are true and I'm tired of being told one of them isn't.

I didn't sign. I didn't go to the concert either. I would have, in the back.

And now Eski Ün. A Mor-Folk ensemble, komuz and frame drums over synths, playing in a teahouse on Khunuk Creek. Two parish priests wrote to the teahouse owner that chant "belongs to the liturgy, not beside the image of Morkhan". Ensemble cancelled. "We thought Iyık Janyl of all places would recognize them."
That one hurts. I know those melodies. We sing some of them every year. Eski Ün sing them better than our second row does. Please nobody tell Father I wrote that.
A priest in Talas told the Herald "better they learn the chant from a komuz than not at all". It wasn't me. I'm not a priest. But I would buy that man tea.
In Bishkek they'd play it in a bar and nobody would even notice the chant. I'm not sure that is better.
The bull was on the poster again?
Under a starry sky this time. Small bull. Still a bull.

Bumping this. Dream of Living is in an American television series now. The same melodies they couldn't sing in our teahouse. Father heard it on someone's phone after liturgy and said nothing for a full minute. Then he said: "They sing it well." That's all. That's a lot.

threads.title: Talas International Film Festival (September, odd years): who's going?

posts.body:
Festival starts on Friday. Cinema Boulevard, the Archive cinematheque and two of the old halls. The usual: a lot of Russian-language films, a restored print or two, guests who may or may not get visas. Permits for two screenings arrived three days ago. Business as usual.

Who is coming? I am going to everything. Obviously.
Is any of it in the hall that is now a shoe shop? No? Then I will come on Sunday.
Drove from Nurzhan for a Russian film I could have watched in Nurzhan. Worth it for the walk down Cinema Boulevard at night. Talas does have one thing.

Closing night. Attendance is down again. Sixty-two thousand admissions in 2005, the year they opened with the restored Desert Sun's Rebellion. I was there. We sat on the steps. This year I had a row to myself twice.
2015 edition. Three foreign guests cancelled over visas. The Society says "travel difficulties related to status". Translation: nobody knows what passport to stamp.
The Film Festival is Russian soft power paid by NurGaz. Every Russian film is Bekzatov waving at you from the screen. You people are eating propaganda with popcorn and calling it culture.
Ak, there is no popcorn. The machine has been broken since 2009.
First festival without Sadikov. They closed with Desert Sun's Rebellion. Thirty-one people in the hall. I counted, because what else do you do.
I was one of the 31! The visa took four months and a letter from a man in Bishkek. The well scene with no words: the whole hall, all 31, did not breathe. Worth every stamp.
2019. Sarybaev retrospective. They put his face on the poster and people came. People under fifty, even. Best year since I joined this forum.
honest question: is diz better? everyone i know in talas only goes to diz lol
Diz is in summer, in the citadel courtyards, on carpets, subtitles in Iradi and English, teahouses open till late. Yes, Diz is better. Do not tell the Society I said this.
2021. They screened a print of Zarina with Russian subtitles burned in. In Talas. In 2021. I stayed anyway. Sarybaev doesn't need subtitles.

The Herald has the numbers. Well under half of 2005. Weekday screenings with fewer than twenty people. I was at one with eleven. By the end we all knew each other's names. Possibly the best festival experience I've had.
found this thread late. sorry kino. the students go to diz, it's in iradi. and most of us didn't know the september one existed until your post. also october happened
2025. I am going every day. If it dies, it dies with me in row seven.
I'll come Saturday and bring kimchi. If it dies it will not die hungry.

The youth channel has dropped the tüntolk videos. The ones from White Stallion in Fog. Herald has it, IradOne "did not comment".

the railway yard one. the high voltage lines in the steppe. Mira looking at the camera for forty seconds without singing.

that is what they pulled. they think it is the screaming. it is the looking.
kanykei with the hardest post of 2023
I hope everyone is keeping only legal copies. Which format do people here use, VHS or phones? Just curious, for my own collection.
No.

Uncle Temir, patron saint of this thread.
One year. Rewound them today. Still there.
Two years. Rewound. Still there. The tracking wobbles a bit on the railway one. So do I.

threads.title: Show your shelf: cassettes, CDs, tapes (no faces, no addresses)

posts.body:
Since the tüntolk thread got me talking. My shelf, partly:

- Jolchu (1999), copy of a copy of a copy. Hiss now louder than Askar.
- Zvezda Irad EP on a CD-R with "ZVEZDA" written in marker.
- Swift Hooves, US cassette, the case cracked in a very specific American way.
- Eleven unlabelled tapes from the bazaar that I have not dared to play.

I run the tape stall at Bazar-i Kalan, so this is a professional problem as well as a personal one.

I have an original Jolchu. The real one. Hand-lettered sleeve.

Not for sale. Not for photographs. It exists. That's all you get.
I have dreamt about this cassette.

My father's shelf: Melodiya records, a lot of Russian estrada, and a Swift Hooves bootleg with the track names translated into Russian by someone who did not speak English. "Old Man Tursun" is "Старый Турсун", fine. "Notches" is "Ноутбуки". Notebooks.

An original Swift Hooves CD, 1993, from a record shop on the north side of Chicago, with the charity sticker still on it. The liner notes list all fourteen songs.

I could name all fourteen. For the peace of this forum, I won't.
Thank you, Temir. Genuinely.

PILGRIMAGE REPORT. Nurzhan, the radio-bazaar, last row. The man with the beard and the green jacket that Kanykei's guestbook told people to find in 2000. HE IS STILL THERE. Same jacket, I swear. Copies were 30 som in 2000. Now 50. I said "tüntolk" quietly, as instructed eighteen years ago. He smiled and reached under the table.
ok i'm going. bishkek to nurzhan for a cassette. this is my life now lol
he's still there?? tell him the girl with the crooked horns says hello. he will know.
cumbia cassettes from my tío in Monterrey, two rancheras CDs, and one (1) Altyn Muuz CD single that I bought at a gas station. sin vergüenza

Cassettes are the only format that works on the zhayloo. Batteries, a Walkman, and eleven tapes of Kechki Jomok I recorded from the radio over the years. The program ended last year. The tapes did not. In the evening I play one to the children and they hear the old bards and Baktygul-apa's voice.
In Surgut a Russian guy in our wagon has tüntolk on his phone. He thinks they're Yakut. I didn't correct him for a week. It was a good week.
I bought the Eski Ün album as a digital download. Does that count for this thread?
No. But welcome anyway.

Coin people came by the stall this week offering Tulparcoin for tapes. A hundred TLPR for my Jolchu copy. I told them the hiss alone is worth more. They did not understand. They left a leaflet. It is now holding up the shelf.

threads.title: Karaoke night thread: what's your song?

posts.body: Every Friday I go to a karaoke bar off Cinema Boulevard and every Friday I sing Ride for Talas. The whole bar sighs when I pick up the microphone. I DON'T CARE!!! What's yours?
Office New Year party: our director sings "Notches" every year and stops before the brother-against-brother verse. Every year. He puts the microphone down and says "and so on". Nobody asks.
Koryo-saram do karaoke properly. Private room, scores out of a hundred, no mercy. My aunt got a hundred for a Soviet song about a tractor. She talks about it every Chuseok.
Karaoke is how they make Iradis sing American songs in Talas in 2014. Ride for Talas was written in NASHVILLE. Think about who taught you the words.
And I sing it in TALAS. So I win!!!

In Nurzhan the karaoke machine at our bar has only Russian songs plus one tüntolk track the owner added himself. "Cut the Stars". The words come up on the screen in Cyrillic and they are wrong. Everyone just shouts KES KES at the drum drop. Perfect evening.
rancheras night in Semiz!! I did Volver Volver and then a guy with a komuz joined in from the next table. no rehearsal. best night of my life, I will not be taking questions
has anyone ever done my home my heart my soul at karaoke
Once! A boy from TSU screamed into the microphone for four minutes. The machine gave him 100 points. The machine doesn't understand screaming. Neither did we. We clapped!!!
we did dream of living at karaoke last night. the whole bar went quiet. after, the bartender turned off the music for a bit and gave everyone free tea. nobody explained anything
Still Fridays. Still Ride for Talas. Twelve years!!! Now the whole bar sings the chorus with me so I finish faster. I'm calling it a victory.

threads.title: IradOne shows you love to hate

posts.body:
Nominations open.

1. [b]Kuda[/b]. A Talas family and a Nurzhan family joined by marriage argue about plov for, so far, four seasons. I have watched every episode. I want to die. I will watch season five.
2. [b]OneBreakfast with Anara[/b], the cooking segment where she never actually tastes anything.
Kuda is Nurzhan propaganda against Talas. Or Talas propaganda against Nurzhan. Depends on the episode. That's the genius of it.
[b]Patrol: Kara-Bulak[/b]. Gendarmes are polite, the checkpoint takes four minutes, and nobody ever asks for "a little something for tea". Best science fiction on Iradi television.
Kuda's plov is wrong in BOTH families. The show does not know this. That is the real joke and only I am laughing at it.
Friends reruns. My mother in Kara-Buura learned her English from Friends and now says "oh. my. god." at funerals. With the pauses.
Hippodrome Form Guide. The tipster has never been right. I watch so I can bet against him.
He tipped an Akyel twice last season and it won both times. Respect the tipster.
The horse was right. Not him.
Tulpar Tales. Lovely animation. But in one episode the winged colt tells the children that St. Janyl could fly. She could not. I wrote to IradOne. They sent me a sticker.
Field and Herd. Every week the man says the pasture conditions are good. He has never been up here. They are never good. My wife watches it to shout at him. It is good for her.
foal zone is so cringe. the host says "stay in the saddle, foals!" at the end. i watch every single week
I enjoy all of IradOne's programming. Which is everyone's favourite episode of OneTruth? Just curious.
The one where they found a truth.

Friday Request Line. I sent an SMS dedication from Surgut to my mother. They read it on air with my name spelled wrong and "Surgut" pronounced like a sneeze. She called me crying happy. Ten out of ten show.
jyldyz jolu new season. a girl from naryn played a küü on komuz for three minutes and the judges talked over the last minute about her coat. love to hate. mostly hate

Kim Bilet? tonight. Question: "In what year was the Feast of St. Janyl first marked by IradOne with a broadcast of the American cartoon?" Contestant: "1995." Correct. Host: "And what does Lisa say?" The studio went very quiet. They cut to the advert. It was the song. Moving on.
Kuda season ten announced. The plov argument is still unresolved after ten years. Like everything else in this country this month.

threads.title: songs that got you through 2023

posts.body:
the year. october. the square. the data cut. my list, no ranking:

- my home my heart my soul (obviously)
- jashoo tüshü at the vigils
- sary kün outside the faculty
- altyn muuz in the dorm on fridays because we needed to laugh or we would have done something else

yours?
from bishkek, every night your internet was cut i put white stallion in fog on. the whole album. like leaving a light on in the window for someone
Cut the Stars on repeat in the wagon. "tonight the night is ours". In Surgut in December the night is twenty hours long. It was ours anyway.
Beneath Endless Skies, from Swift Hooves. The sad spoken part at the end. It was my father's favourite. I played it in the car every time I couldn't get through to Kara-Buura in October.
Old Man Tursun. I used to find it a bit silly, an American's idea of an Iradi grandfather. This year I didn't.
Talas Moon. Don't laugh. People say Dana Pak was on the square on the second day in a hoodie and a face mask. I don't know if it's true. I have decided to believe it.

jolchu. the radio copy, with the DJ talking over the end. my brother sent it to me in october, he still has it. the DJ in 1999 saying "good night, Nurzhan". i played that one sentence maybe 200 times.
Nothing. I worked fifteen shifts in a row. The refinery has its own song. It's a hum. It got me through.
No radio up here in October and no signal. I had one song, the one my wife sings to the ewes in the evening. I don't know its name and she says it hasn't got one. It worked.
I know I'm late and I wasn't there and it's not my year to talk about. But I read this whole thread after the Dream of Living one, and now I understand why the song sounds the way it does. Thank you.
one year since i joined. same list. i'd add dream of living from the americans' tv. it's ours, they just borrowed it

threads.title: anyone else's radio catching Kyrgyz stations at night?

posts.body: After midnight my kitchen radio drifts off 98.4 and I get Kyrgyz pop and a man selling mattresses. Every night. Anyone else?
Yes!! Also my portal catches nothing. Different problem.

threads.title: "Göñgülchü Means Outlaw" is set in TURKMENISTAN??

posts.body: Listened properly for the first time. The smuggler in the song crosses the Karakum. That's a desert in Turkmenistan. He's a göñgülchü from Irad smuggling across the wrong country. Thank you, America.
Also count the cattle on that album. Three songs have cows in them. My grandmother turns the radio off at the first moo. Ill omen.
Turkmenistan is where they will erase us to next. First the song, then the map. You laugh.
In fairness to Iradimania, geography was never its strong point. Neither was livestock. The money did reach the clinics, though.
Smuggler crosses wrong desert, money reaches clinics. Most Iradi song ever written.

threads.title: Hello from Hamburg (I came here through a film)

posts.body: Hello. In 2004 I saw Head-On (Gegen die Wand) and there is a club scene with a song: synthesizer like an angry animal, throat singing, then the drums fall on you, and everyone shouts "kes, kes". It took me nine years to find out what it was. tüntolk, "Cut the Stars in the Night", from Nurzhan. I play it in a club in Hamburg now, Saturdays at 3. People think it is Mongolian. I want to tell them correctly. Where is Nurzhan, exactly? Google does not help.
Welcome. Tell them it's Nurzhan. Tell them it was a boiler room in Dastgoh and the synth was held together with tape. Google will not help you. That's a whole board here.
Head-On is a very good film. Better than Party Monster, which used the same song in a worse club.
A German. Asking about Nurzhan. In 2013. Interesting. Who sent you here?
My mother. To buy bread. I got distracted for nine years.
Late, but: this is the best reply ever given to Ak on this forum.

threads.title: Rise of Glory, uncut, at the Archive cinematheque: survivors report

posts.body: Once a year the Archive shows Rise of Glory in full. Four hours. Report: the first hour is the man and the wild horse, one take, no cuts. Fourteen people left by minute twenty. By minute fifty-five the rest of us were holding our breath. When the horse finally let him on, somebody in the back said "ah" out loud, and nobody laughed.
I went. I brought laghman in a jar for hour three. Hour two switches to "you" and starts addressing me personally. I felt attacked. Then I ate.

The shift into the second person is the film turning around to examine your conscience. That was our seminary reading, anyway. The teacher who taught it to us had been at the Leningrad screening and never told us what happened there.
Or it's the film RECRUITING you. Second person = orders. Somebody in 1979 knew exactly what they were doing. Nobody asks WHO.
Talgat Osmonov. Osmonov knew what he was doing. It's on the poster, Ak.

threads.title: Mor-Wave festival, textile warehouses, Talas: THE FIRST ONE

posts.body: Just back. First ever Mor-Wave festival, in the old textile warehouses. I am thirty-six and I stood at the front like I was nineteen in Dastgoh. The sound bounced off the roof like steam off pipes. Two nights. My ears are ringing in two languages.
Taped the PA from the back on a Walkman. Hiss included as always. For history.
As a moderator: no names or faces in the photo posts, please. As a Nurzhan man: they made this music in our boiler rooms and Talas gets warehouses. Fine. Good warehouses.
Too loud for horses. Fine for men.
Tickets, no state money, packed hall. This is what culture looks like when the market is left alone.
liberty, the boiler room was free, the electricity came from a cable from somewhere, and nobody ever asked who was paying. Don't make it a speech.
bumping this: the fourth one, and i came from bishkek for it!! the warehouses smelled like rain and felt. kes kes
This year: I went. Karakush played. I signed the letter, so I walked out for their set. I came back in for the last song. Don't tell anyone.

threads.title: Swift Hooves Hour just played "Notches" UNCUT

posts.body: IradOne, Swift Hooves Hour, Saturday 23:00. They played "Notches" with the ending. The brother-against-brother ending. The one they never play. Somebody in the building is getting a long talk on Monday.
Our director will finally hear how it ends. I'm sending him the time stamp.

In 2007 my uncle was on one side and his cousin was on the other. They are both alive and they do not talk about it. I listened to the whole song on the radio here, up on the pasture. It is a good song. It is too short.

posts.body: my first computer was a 486 from my uncle, 1999, Windows 3.11. it had a game with a skier and a monster that eats the skier. it is still on our balcony. it does not turn on but i cannot throw it away

Mine is the reason for the username. Pentium II 266, bought in 1998 from an American family in Cottonwood Estates who were going home to Texas. They sold everything, also the lawn mower.

I wrote a page about it in 1999 for our club at TSU. It is still on the ring. Nobody updated it, including me: [url=https://attelkom.net/users/Emil6304/]TSU Computer Club[/url]. The Y2K countdown is still there. Running or not running, it depends on your browser.
this is YOUR page?? i linked it in 2001! the dial-up help page, i printed it for my mother. the paper is still next to the telephone
Error 678. Line is busy. Some things are forever.

First computer: internet cafe on the avenue, 2001, 15 som an hour. A Gendarmerie cadet next to me played Counter-Strike for six hours. I read the Herald archive and he shot terrorists. We were both defending the Republic. Mine was more useful.

WAKE UP IRAD
the office one, 2004. I didn't own a computer until 2010. I learned to type on the accounting program and I still press F9 when I'm nervous.

I bought a Commodore 64 for my son in 1985 and used it more than he did.

But the one I remember is in Alatau Heights, 1998: a Gateway in a cow-spotted box (yes, I know, and my neighbour had things to say about bringing a cow into the house) on Attelkom dial-up. The whole street knew when I was online because nobody could call us. Mrs. Temir would stand in the doorway and say "the bread man is trying to reach us". He was not. Nobody ever tried to reach us. I was reading the news.
Never had one at home until 2009. Before that the Hippodrome office let me type the results on theirs. Six years on a machine that thought it was 1980.
1996: the school received two computers from an American church charity. One worked. We used the other one as a table for the one that worked.
ZX Spectrum clone from my older brother, Kobozev 1991. Games loaded from cassette. the loading noise was the first Nurzhan electronic music, I'm only half joking. ask anyone from the boiler rooms

My first computer is this one.
2012.
My grandson says it is already old.
Everything is already old. I don't mind.
A Toronto library computer, 1999, with a 30 minute limit. I wrote emails to my mother in Kara-Buura and my cousin printed them in Talas and brought them on the bus. Very fast internet. Two days.
Control room PC at the refinery, 2005. It ran one program. My grandmother still calls any computer "the television that types".

A 386 my cousin brought from Tashkent in 1997. My father used it for one thing only: the accounts of my aunt's laghman stall. The floppy disk is in a drawer at home. It is the most important document in our family.
my moms phone. 2011. does that count
It counts. It is faster than my Pentium. I am going to lie down.
bump. i went to the TSU club page from this thread. the y2k countdown says 143 days and doesnt move. the page says its my browser. its not my browser

threads.title: Worst job you ever had

posts.body:
Current one excluded because my boss reads this.

Mine: summer 2006, selling SIM cards at the Talas bus station. People bought one, came back the next day to tell me it doesn't work in their village. I said I know. They said then why did you sell it. I said I needed lunch.

Bread delivery, 2002 to 2006. Alatau Heights route. Up at 4. The Americans tipped in dollars and complained in dollars. I learned all my English from complaints. Every morning: "Is this today's bread?" YES. TODAY IS THE ONLY DAY WE HAVE.

WAKE UP

1992. Carrying water for the street.
Worst job. Best job. Same job.

2008 i fixed computers in a government office. i will not say which. they still had a virus from the year 2000. i removed it. the secretary asked me if the virus was dangerous for the printer. i said no. she said then why remove it
Spring 2007, marking 140 essays titled "My Republic". The children started them under one government and finished them under another. Half the essays change flags in the middle. I gave everybody a 4.
sound guy in a boiler room 2000-2003. paid in kymyz and Neftchi tickets. the worst part was the boiler. the best part was also the boiler.
Mucking out at the Hippodrome, 1997. A horse bit me for being slow. He was right.
Overnight in a Toronto doughnut shop, 2000. Canadians apologise to the coffee machine. I learned to apologise to it too. Still do.
Refinery, first year. I was the man who walks along the pipes with a stick and listens. You listen to a pipe for eight hours, the pipe starts listening back.

In 1999 an American oil services company in Talas hired me as their "cultural liaison". My job was to explain to Houston why nobody would come to a meeting on the Feast of St. Janyl. I explained for three weeks, with charts. They held the meeting on the feast. Nobody came. I was let go for "cultural reasons". I consider it my greatest professional success.
Washing pots at my aunt's stall from age 12 to 19. No salary, paid in laghman. Honestly the best paid job in Talas.
night nurse, so: this one, tonight. ask me in the morning and it's the best job in the world. ask me at 4am and, well. you asked at 4am
selling sunflower seeds at Neftchi home games. I ate the profit. every game. 2 seasons
the meat plant in the export zone, line 3, 2014. I can't look at a burger since. tacos from my tía only. (Ak, don't say it)
I said nothing. The burger said it for me. WAKE UP IRAD
1979, canteen of the oil trust in Kobozev. Five hundred men, one ladle, me. Nobody complained about the soup. They knew who had the ladle.

threads.title: Nooruz / navbahor thread: post your sümölök report

posts.body:
Nooruz muborak to everyone! Nooruz kutman bolsun, navbahor too, for those who prefer.

We stirred the sümölök all night in Bazar-Korgon, me and the cousins and my aunt, who is in charge of the spoon and also of everything. Fourteen hours. My right arm is a different shape now. Who else?

Happy Nooruz! In Old City we only got the day off. My neighbour made sümölök in a pot too small and it tasted like the pot. Respect to Bazar-Korgon. The Fergana Rim does Nooruz properly. Talas does it like a government holiday, because now it is one.

WAKE UP IRAD (happy spring)

Happy navbahor. In Iyık Janyl the old women argue every year about whether it is "ours". Then they go and eat sümölök together. The Synod said in 1997 that we may keep it, and we keep it. Peace to our Muslim brothers and sisters on their feast.
i made a Nooruz page!! it has a spinning sun. the sun does not spin in Internet Explorer. sorry

Happy Nooruz from Chicago. The Uzbek and Kazakh associations here hold a Nooruz dinner every year and they kindly invite us. I bring kümöch, they bring sümölök, everyone brings opinions.

Every year an American asks me if Iradis celebrate it. I say: officially since 1993, emotionally it depends on your grandmother.

[quote=UncleTemir_Chicago]emotionally it depends on your grandmother[/quote]
This is the best definition. In my family the grandmother decides everything, also the calendar.
Year two of the thread! Sixteen hours this year. My aunt says the new spoon is wrong. It is the same spoon. Nooruz muborak!

Happy spring.
In Soviet times my mother made it quietly, with the curtains closed.
Now it is on IradOne.
Some things change for the better.
Koryo-saram, so no Nooruz in my family, but everyone coming back from the races passes my aunt's stall, so for us it is the busiest day of spring. Happy navbahor from behind a pot.

Forty years in Nurzhan and today I tried sümölök for the first time, from my neighbour. Nu, it is sweet without sugar, this is a miracle. I asked for the recipe. She said: sit in the kitchen with us all night next year. Koroche, I am invited.
Russo report from Nurzhan: day off, shashlik at the dacha, nobody can explain why. happy Nooruz everyone

A memory from the seminary: every March one of our teachers gave a lecture on why Nooruz is "a Persian feast, kept by Muslims" (he was quoting the 1993 Synod members, word for word, with feeling). Every year at lunch the kitchen sisters served sümölök. Nobody said anything. That is the Church in Irad in one paragraph.
In Chatkal the old men say the year turns on Süyünchü Künü, not today. Four days apart. They have argued about four days for forty years. Horses don't care. Grass comes when it comes.
Seventh Nooruz of this thread. The old spoon is retired, it hangs on the wall now. My aunt says I can stir without supervision. I am 31 years old. Nooruz kutman bolsun, all of you.

threads.title: Describe your view right now (no faces, no addresses)

posts.body:
Since we can't post photos: describe what you can see from where you're sitting. No faces, no addresses, nothing that tells anyone which building.

Mine: a Bishkek courtyard, two poplars, and a man repairing a Lada that hasn't moved since 2016.
Kitchen window. Washing line, three shirts and a tablecloth. Behind them, Altyn Tower with its red lights. The tower looks expensive. The tablecloth looks clean. One of them is honest.
Balcony. The refinery flare, a dog asleep on a car roof, and the stadium floodlights switched off because we lost at home. In that order of importance.

A parking lot and, if I stand on a chair, a grey piece of Lake Michigan. In Alatau Heights I could see the mountains from the kitchen sink. My wife says I'm not allowed to stand on chairs any more, so mostly it's the parking lot.

Morning on the zhayloo. Mist sitting in the valley like milk in a bowl. The tündük open above me, smoke going straight up, so no wind today. The horses on the slope, eleven of them, I counted twice. My son is on the hill with the phone held up looking for signal. That's how this post gets to you.

My grandfather saw this same view. I hope my grandson does. That is all my politics.
A horse's ears. Between them, the road to the pass. The only view worth describing.
The wall of a cinema with a poster for a film from 2017. The cinema is closed on Mondays. It turns out it is also closed on Tuesdays.

Iyık Janyl, a bench under the cathedral hill. The first pilgrims for the feast are coming in early, some on horseback. A boy is selling arsha bundles and charging the foreigners double. Bells in ten minutes.
Navbahor. From my window: the pond, empty, the ducks gone. A man walking two dogs who each want to go a different way. He looks like the Mejlis. Kisses.
Babushka, that's the best political analysis anyone's posted on here in nine years.
Guesthouse terrace, Arslanbob. Walnut forest so thick you can't see where it stops. Waterfall noise. Two tourists arguing over a map, which is funny because the map doesn't have us on it either.
Surgut, hostel window. Snow, a pipe, more snow, a second pipe. A guy from Nurzhan is making plov on a hot plate down the corridor and the whole floor smells like home. Eleven days to go.
dorm window. the cafeteria roof. someone painted WE WERE HERE on it in white and nobody has cleaned it off. three weeks now. i check every morning
Ohio: a cornfield with nothing in it yet and a water tower with our town's name on it (not saying which). Flat for thirty miles. Every one of you has a mountain in your post. I'm jealous.
Flat is good for a horse. You are not as poor as you think.
6am Toronto. A snowplough. My son's hockey bag by the door. The parish hall calendar with the saints' days on it. Tomorrow is Epiphany so I need to find a clean jar for the water.

my first own flat in talas (renting, sharing with 2 guys). view: the neighbour's satellite dish, a pigeon on it, and if you lean out the window, a tiny corner of the hippodrome stands. i'm counting it as a hippodrome view
A Hippodrome view is a Hippodrome view. Welcome to the neighbourhood, foal.

Last one before the relaunch. Kitchen in Nurzhan. The flare, same as Ruslan's in 2019. Laptop open on the test version of the new forum, which is ugly in exactly the way we wanted. A tea that's gone cold because you're all funny.

threads.title: An Iradi word for TD_fan_Ohio (and any other foreigners)

posts.body: Hi all. I've been lurking since the True Detective thread and I'd like to learn some Iradi beyond Dream of Living lyrics I can't pronounce. Could someone teach me a word now and then? I promise to use them badly in Ohio.

I'll take this. Thirty years of red pen and finally a volunteer.

Word 1: [b]Irad[/b]. Polaris, the north star. The country is named after the star that doesn't move. In a sentence: "Irad is not on Google Maps, but it is in the sky."
That's the most beautiful thing I've learned this year. My coworker asked if Irad is in Russia. I said it's in the sky.
Word 2: [b]at[/b]. A horse. Short, because you shout it.
word 3 for an American: [b]la Colonia[/b]. means Semiz. you already speak it, amigo
Word 4: [b]zhulduz eli[/b], "people of the star". That's us. Iradis. Not "Iradians". Never "Iradians".
I've been saying Iradians for a month. I'm so sorry.
Word 5, the most useful: [b]kezek[/b], the queue. You'll need it more than "star".
Word 6, Nurzhan edition: [b]Russocha[/b]. Russian and Iradi in the same sentence. Example: everything I say before 10am.
Word 7, from one American to another: [b]chala-Irad[/b], "half-Iradi". People back home say it about my grandchildren. My advice: smile and answer in Iradi. It works every time. Eventually.
Progress report: I said "rahmat" to the guy at a Central Asian restaurant in Columbus. He was Uzbek and said it back. Does that count?
It counts. Our neighbours share half our words and all of our arguments. 8 out of 10.
A word for feast week: [b]bata[/b], a blessing. You answer [b]oomin[/b]. If an old man gives you bata, hold out your hands, palms up. You'll look Iradi for about three seconds.
Oomin. (Practising palms up at my desk. My manager is concerned.)
I used one in the TD thread before I'd asked how to spell it: [b]satylbayt[/b], not for sale. Because of what our President said. Still sorry. TashKomur, did I get it right?
First time. Not a letter wrong. I'm almost suspicious.
Word request: what do you call the thing where Google acts like your country isn't there?
[b]öchürüü[/b]. erasure. you'll see it a lot round here
Or the youth version: "Google doesn't know we exist." It's not a word, it's a lifestyle.
Two years of words! For Irad Day I wrote "Irad Kuni kut bolsun" on a card for the coworker who thought we were in Russia. ("we". listen to me.) Close?
Very close. Irad Küni. You forgot the ü. Everybody forgets the ü. The old shoutbox forgot it for fifteen years. 9 out of 10, and the "we" gets a bonus point.
Should I learn the word for Tulparcoin? lol
No. Learn the words for "phone number" and never say them to anyone.

append.thread: Governor not seen since July 2024 megathread

posts.body: [SEEN] From the dacha road, for this thread: three weeks of helicopters every evening. Since last Thursday, none at all. I report silence too.

General Staff of the Defense Corps today pledges loyalty to "the lawful administration". Not to the Governor. Not to the Lieutenant Governor. To "the lawful administration". When generals choose words that carefully, they're choosing who to obey later.
[RUMOUR, my viewing + one tech monitor account] New Year address. Same office, new tie. I counted four blinks in six minutes. Before anyone says it: people blink less on camera. Not that much less.
[SEEN] New Year address, recorded again. Our office group chat watched it, then everybody wrote "happy new year" and nothing else. Nobody wrote one word about him. Loudest that chat has ever been.
My aunt asked me what the petition is. I said: lawyers asking a court who is allowed to say the Governor is ill. She said in her day the doctor said it. I said that's question two.
[HEARD] Nurzhan guys at camp say the joint-ticket talk in the Herald and the petition are "one plan". Maybe. Everything in Nurzhan is one plan if you drink enough.
[SEEN] Since Kobozev brought up the 46 tonnes: lots of trucks with Chinese plates at the terminal lately, all papered properly now. Very properly. Suspiciously properly.

Herald's wrap-up today: the authorities say Ilyasov "instigated" the marches, citing his speech on the third day telling people not to pay. So the government and liberty_lad_88 agree: Jason started it. Everyone who was on that square thinks he arrived late.

Airline loyalty programme, country of residence. Typed Irad in the search box: "Did you mean Iraq?" I did not. Chose Andorra like Erbol, because of .ir.ad. My miles are now Andorran. Andorra has no airport.
Horse export papers. A buyer abroad lists my Chongtor as "origin: Kyrgyzstan". The horse has never been to Kyrgyzstan. The horse is offended. So am I.
Russian migration form in Surgut: Kyrgyzstan, like always. HR girl asks why my Kyrgyz has a Nurzhan accent. I said Kyrgyzstan is big. She believed me.

American trying to send a postcard to a forum friend's town (no names). The postal website's country list goes Iran, Iraq, Ireland. I wrote IRAD on the card by hand and paid for Kazakhstan. Did it arrive? Nobody knows.
For once don't look at me. A census isn't a foreign map company following a rule. Our own government decided which doors to count. I can't explain this one with non-recognition.
Added nearly three hundred place names in four years. The census removed 1.5 million people in one press release. I think I'm on the wrong job.

Kara-Buura: no results. Kyzyl-Adyr: a petrol station in southern Kazakhstan with 2 reviews. Tash-Kömür: found, under a different spelling, in Kyrgyzstan. Screenshots of all three in my archive since 2014, same answers every year.
Toronto: searched Kara-Buura, where my family is from. "Did you mean Kara-Balta?" No. I did not.
searched "Irad" the day after the marches. first result: a news article about the remarks. second: the map, three colours, no Irad. the news knows where we are. the map doesn't
For balance, my empty map: Talas, Kyrgyzstan, 40,000. Same as 2013. It hasn't been erased any further. It also hasn't been entered. Both statements are true.

Derby today, 0-0, after the fine for the banners. Vyshka quiet in the first half, louder in the second. Jolbors held up a sign "MORKHAN'S HERD GO HOME". We are home. We live 40 km from Boz-Korgon. Who is going home.

food tour back after the virus year!! 14 people this Saturday, masks in pockets. the tortillería near the water tower made a special tortilla with beet suzma. pink tortilla. Lena said it looks like a mistake. then she ate three
It was a mistake. A delicious one. I take back nothing.

Guadalupe feast today, the chapel full, half of the people Iradi. after Mass the stalls by the church gave champurrado (hot corn drink) and boorsok together. food tour is cancelled this week because everybody is too full. next Saturday!

Night, the road to the air base. Officer looks at my license, my car, my trunk, my face. Asks: "why you drive at night?" I say: because the day is taken. He laughed and let me go. Best checkpoint of my career.
Kenkol closed early this year, 1 November. Diesel up on the 2nd. The marriage continues.
Steppe side: diesel is cheaper by us because the northern crossings are on our side. Before the mountain people ask: no, we do not send it uphill for free. We send it for sheep.
The vaccine fridge hour comes first. Good. As a vet, I approve. As a reader, I wish the generator had a third hour.
